evidence.source: lest perhaps he reach forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever
evidence.target: To him that overcometh, I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of my God

3:22.note: What fallen Adam was barred from reaching lest he live for ever, the overcomer is given to eat: the tree of life in the Paradise of God.

evidence.source: of Lamech seventy times seven-fold
evidence.target: I say not to thee until seven times but until seventy times seven times

4:24.note: The Lord's measure of forgiveness takes Lamech's measure of vengeance — seventy times seven-fold — and turns it inside out.

evidence.source: This is the book of the generation of Adam
evidence.target: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ

5:1.note: Matthew opens his Gospel in Genesis' own formula — the book of the generation — for the Christ who recapitulates Adam.

evidence.source: Noe was a just and perfect man in his generations
evidence.target: if these three men shall be in the midst thereof, Noe, Daniel, & Job: they by their justice shall deliver their own souls

6:9.note: Ezechiel's Noe, first of his three righteous men, is Genesis' just and perfect man who walked with God.

evidence.source: all that moveth and liveth shall be yours for meat
evidence.target: meats which God created to receive with thanks-giving

9:3.note: The universal grant of food to Noe stands behind Paul's defence of meats which God created to be received with thanksgiving.

evidence.source: our Lord dispersed them from that place into all lands
evidence.target: When the highest divided the nations: when he separated the sons of Adam, he appointed the limits of people

11:8.note: Moses' song looks back to Babel: the dividing of the nations and the appointing of their limits is the dispersion from that place into all lands.

evidence.source: Go forth of thy country, and out of thy kindred, and out of thy father's house
evidence.target: I called him alone, and blessed him, & multiplied him

12:1.note: Isaiah bids Israel look to Abraham's call: one man called alone out of his father's house, and blessed and multiplied.

evidence.source: I will make thee into a great nation
evidence.target: I will make thee into a great nation

12:2.note: God offers Moses the very promise-word first given to Abraham — and Moses refuses it, pleading for Abraham's seed instead.

evidence.source: To thy seed will I give this land
evidence.target: This is the Land, for the which I sware to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: To thy seed will I give it

12:7.note: On Nebo the Lord shews Moses the land in the promise's own words, first spoken to Abram when he appeared to him.

evidence.source: as the Paradise of our Lord
evidence.target: our Lord God had planted Paradise of pleasure from the beginning

13:10.note: Genesis itself measures the well-watered Jordan plain by Eden: as the Paradise of the Lord.

evidence.source: I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: if any man be able to number the dust of the earth, thy seed also shall he be able to number
evidence.target: Who may be able to number the dust of Jacob

13:16.note: Balaam's question answers the promise: who may number the dust of Jacob, the seed made as the dust of the earth that no man can number?

evidence.source: Melchisedech the king of Salem, bringing forth bread and wine, for he was the Priest of God most High
evidence.target: Thou art a Priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech

14:18.note: David's oracle takes its everlasting priesthood from Salem's king, the priest of God most High who brought forth bread and wine.

evidence.source: Look up to heaven, and number the stars, if thou canst. And he said to him: so shall thy seed be
evidence.target: thou didst multiply their children as the stars of heaven

15:5.note: Nehemias' prayer recites the promise as fulfilled: their children multiplied as the stars Abram was bidden to number, if he could.

evidence.source: Abram believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice
evidence.target: thou didst find his heart faithful before thee: and thou madest a covenant with him

15:6.note: The same prayer remembers why the covenant followed the believing: a heart found faithful before God.

evidence.source: I am the Lord that brought thee out from Ur of the Chaldees for to give thee this land, and that thou mightest possess it
evidence.target: Abraham was one, and by inheritance he possessed the land

15:7.note: The dwellers in the ruins argue from the promise itself: Abraham was one, and he possessed by inheritance the land God brought him out of Ur to give him.

evidence.source: An infant of eight days shall be circumcised among you
evidence.target: circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel

17:12.note: Paul's own circumcision, the eighth day, is his pedigree measured by the ordinance given in Abraham's house.

evidence.source: Make haste, temper together three measures of flour, and make hearth cakes
evidence.target: leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened

18:6.note: The parable's three measures of meal are Sara's, tempered in haste at the tent door for the visit of the Lord.

evidence.source: Is there any thing hard to God?
evidence.target: there shall not be impossible with God any word

18:14.note: Gabriel answers Mary with the assurance spoken at Mambre: no word shall be impossible with God — the same annunciation of a son where nature said none could be.

evidence.source: in him are TO BE Blessed All The Nations of The Earth
evidence.target: in thee shall all nations be blessed

18:18.note: Paul's form of the promise — all nations blessed — follows this renewal of it at Mambre, rather than the 'kindreds' of its first giving at Genesis 12:3, which the seed already carries.

evidence.source: Bring them forth hither that we may know them
evidence.target: Bring forth the man, that entered into thy house, that we may abuse him

19:5.note: Gibea repeats Sodom almost to the word: the guest demanded out of the host's house by the men of the city at night.

evidence.source: our Lord rained upon Sodome and Gomorre brimstone & fire from our Lord out of heaven
evidence.target: after the example of the subversion of Sodom and Gomorrha, Adama, and Seboim, which our Lord subverted in his wrath & fury

19:24.note: Moses holds up the subversion of Sodom as the standing example of a land burned with brimstone and sown no more.

evidence.source: rained upon Sodome and Gomorre brimstone & fire
evidence.target: Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrha, dryness of thorns, and heaps of salt

19:24.note: Sophonias measures Moab and Ammon — Lot's own posterity — by the city Lot was delivered from: as Sodom, and as Gomorrha.

evidence.source: Therefore our Lord rained upon Sodome and Gomorre brimstone & fire
evidence.target: Lo this was the iniquity of Sodom thy sister, pride, fullness of bread, and aboundance

19:24.note: Ezechiel expounds what the iniquity of Sodom was, whose overthrow Genesis records: pride, fullness of bread, and a hand not stretched out to the poor.

evidence.source: rained upon Sodome and Gomorre brimstone & fire from our Lord out of heaven
evidence.target: as God subverted Sodom and Gomorth

19:24.note: Amos recalls the subversion as God's own act in history, the pattern of the overthrows he works in Israel.

evidence.source: Take thy only begotten son, whom thou lovest, Isaac
evidence.target: he gave his only-begotten Son

22:2.note: John's only-begotten Son, given by the Father who so loved the world, answers Abraham's only begotten son, whom he loved, taken up for the offering.

evidence.source: go into the Land of vision: and there thou shalt offer him for an holocaust upon one of the mountains which I will shew thee
evidence.target: Salomon began to build the house of our Lord in Jerusalem, in mount Moria

22:2.note: The mountain of Isaac's offering is the temple mount: Moria — the 'Land of vision' as Genesis names the place, for 'in the mountain our Lord will see' (Genesis 22:14).

evidence.source: He took also the wood of the holocaust, and laid it upon Isaac his son
evidence.target: bearing his own cross he went forth

22:6.note: Isaac carries the wood of his own holocaust up the mountain; the Son bears his own cross forth to the place of sacrifice.

evidence.source: as the sand that is by the sea shore
evidence.target: Juda and Israel innumerable, as the sand of the sea in multitude: eating, and drinking, and rejoicing

22:17.note: Under Solomon the oath stands fulfilled in a single clause: Juda and Israel innumerable, as the sand of the sea.

evidence.source: he found that same year an hundred fold: and our Lord blessed him
evidence.target: they yielded fruit, the one an hundredfold, the other threescore, and another thirty

26:12.note: The sower's hundredfold is Isaac's measure: the one sowing in Genesis that found a hundredfold in the same year, in famine, because the Lord blessed him.

evidence.source: He that shall curse thee, be he cursed: and he that shall bless thee, be he replenished with blessings
evidence.target: He that blesseth thee, himself also shall be blessed: he that curseth thee, shall be reputed accurst

27:29.note: Balaam, hired to curse Israel, blesses her in Isaac's own blessing-words spoken over Jacob.

evidence.source: our Lord seeing that he despised Lia, opened her womb, her sister remaining barren
evidence.target: she upbraided her, that our Lord had shut her matrice

29:31.note: Anna and Phenenna replay Rachel and Lia: two wives of one man, the Lord opening one womb and shutting the other, and the beloved wife sore vexed by her rival.

evidence.source: dilate my seed as the sand of the sea, which for multitude cannot be numbered
evidence.target: the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, that is without measure, and shall not be numbered

32:12.note: Osee takes up the promise Jacob himself had pleaded at the Jabbok: seed as the sand of the sea, that cannot be numbered.

evidence.source: Cast away the strange gods that are among you
evidence.target: take away strange gods out of the midst of you

35:2.note: Josue at Sichem renews Jacob's own command in the same place: cast away the strange gods — the gods Jacob buried under the oak at Sichem.

evidence.source: the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars adore me
evidence.target: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, & on her head a crown of twelve stars

37:9.note: Joseph's dream-sign returns in heaven: sun and moon and stars gathered about the woman who brings forth the male child.

evidence.source: come, let us kill him, and cast him into an old cistern
evidence.target: This is the heir, come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance

37:20.note: The husbandmen's cry in the Lord's parable is the brethren's cry over Joseph the heir of the dreams: come, let us kill him.

evidence.source: sold him to the Ismaelites, for twenty pieces of silver
evidence.target: they appointed unto him thirty pieces of silver

37:28.note: Joseph is sold by his brethren for pieces of silver, at Juda's counsel; the Son of David is priced at thirty pieces by Judas.

evidence.source: Why doth not interpretation belong to God?
evidence.target: there is a God in heaven that revealeth mysteries

40:8.note: Joseph and Daniel, the two dream-readers set before kings, make the same disclaimer: interpretation belongs to God, who revealeth mysteries.

evidence.source: these are the names of the children of Israel, that entered into Ægypt, himself with his children
evidence.target: These be the names of the children of Israel, that entered into Ægypt with Jacob

46:8.note: Exodus opens by taking up Genesis' list-formula to the letter: these are the names of the children of Israel that entered into Egypt.

evidence.source: All the souls of the house of Jacob, that entered into Ægypt, were seventy
evidence.target: all the souls that came out of Jacob's thigh were seventy

46:27.note: Exodus repeats Genesis' reckoning of the descent: seventy souls of the house of Jacob.

evidence.source: The days of the pilgrimage of my life are an hundred thirty years, few and evil
evidence.target: we are pilgrims before thee, and strangers, as all our fathers

47:9.note: David's prayer takes Jacob's own word for his years — pilgrimage — and makes it the confession of all the fathers.

evidence.source: was increased, & multiplied exceedingly
evidence.target: the children of Israel increased, and as it were springing up did multiply, and growing strong exceedingly, filled the land

47:27.note: Exodus' first paragraph resumes Genesis' last word on the sojourn: Israel increased and multiplied exceedingly, even under a new king that knew not Joseph.

evidence.source: his younger brother shall be greater than he: and his seed shall grow into nations
evidence.target: These are the multitudes of Ephraim, and these the thousands of Manasses

48:19.note: Moses' blessing of Joseph reckons what Jacob foresaw with crossed hands: Ephraim the younger grown into multitudes.

evidence.source: thou didst ascend thy father's bed, and didst defile his couch
evidence.target: when he had violated his father's bed, his first-birth-right was given to the sons of Joseph

49:4.note: The Chronicler explains Ruben's lost birthright out of Jacob's dying sentence: he had violated his father's bed.

evidence.source: taking thy rest thou didst lie as a lion, and as it were a lioness, who shall raise him up?
evidence.target: Lying he hath slept as a lion, and as a lioness, whom none shall be bold to raise up

49:9.note: Balaam's oracle on Israel couches in Jacob's own lion-words over Juda, taking his rest none dares rouse.

evidence.source: Till he do Come That is to be Sent
evidence.target: A star Shall Rise out of Jacob, and a rod shall arise from Israel

49:10.note: Balaam's star out of Jacob and rod out of Israel answer Jacob's sceptre that shall not be taken from Juda till he come that is to be sent.

evidence.source: The Sceptre Shall Not be Taken Away From Judas
evidence.target: till he came to whom judgement belongeth, and I will deliver it to him

49:10.note: Ezechiel's triple 'iniquity, iniquity, iniquity' over the diadem runs till he come to whom judgment belongeth — the term Jacob's sceptre-oracle set.

evidence.source: Dan shall judge his own people, as also another tribe in Israel
evidence.target: he judged Israel twenty years

49:16.note: Jacob's word on Dan is fulfilled in the one judge of Dan's stock: Samson, of Saraa, son of Manue (Judges 13:2), who judged Israel twenty years.

evidence.source: be they upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren
evidence.target: come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren

49:26.note: Moses' blessing of Joseph closes in Jacob's very words: the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, the Nazarite among his brethren.

evidence.source: You thought evil against me, but God turned that into good
evidence.target: to them that love God, all things cooperate unto good

50:20.note: Joseph's sentence is the doctrine in narrative form: evil thought against God's servant is turned by God into good, to save many peoples; Paul states it as the standing rule for them that love God.

evidence.source: God will visit you carry my bones with you out of this place
evidence.target: Moyses also took Joseph's bones with him: because he had adjured the children of Israel, saying: God shall visit you, carry out my bones from hence with you

50:24.note: Exodus records the oath kept at the going out: Moses took Joseph's bones, adjured in the words of Genesis 50.

evidence.source: God will visit you carry my bones with you out of this place
evidence.target: The bones also of Joseph which the children of Israel had taken out of Ægypt, they buried in Sichem

50:24.note: The bones carried out of Egypt under Joseph's adjuration are buried at last in Sichem, in the field Jacob bought — the oath's long journey ended where the patriarchs lie.

evidence.source: but the woman of the man
evidence.target: our Lord God built the rib which he took of Adam into a woman

11:8.note: Paul's 'woman of the man' states in a phrase what Genesis tells at length: the woman built from the rib taken out of Adam.

evidence.source: The first man of earth, earthly: the second man from Heaven, heavenly
evidence.target: formed man of the slime of the earth

15:47.note: The first man is 'of earth, earthly' because God formed him of the slime of the earth; the second man is set against him as from heaven.

evidence.source: as in Adam all die
evidence.target: dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return

15:22.note: The death that is in Adam for all men is the sentence of Genesis 3 itself: dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.

evidence.source: but in the azymes of sincerity and verity
evidence.target: Seven days shall you eat azymes: in the first day there shall be no leaven in your houses

5:8.note: Paul keeps the feast of unleavened bread in figure: the Church's azymes are sincerity and truth, against Exodus' seven days without leaven.

evidence.source: For our Pasch, Christ, is immolated
evidence.target: Go take a lamb by your families, and sacrifice the Phase

5:7.note: 'Our Pasch, Christ, is immolated': Paul names Christ himself the lamb Moses commanded Israel to take and sacrifice.

evidence.source: all in Moyses were baptized in the cloud and in the sea
evidence.target: went through the midst of the dry sea: for the water was as it were a wall on their right hand and their left

10:2.note: Paul argues that the crossing itself was Israel's baptism — 'all in Moses were baptized in the cloud and in the sea' — the doctrinal pattern on which his warning to Corinth rests.

evidence.source: nor the liers with mankind
evidence.target: He that lieth with man as if he should company with woman, both have committed abomination

6:9.note: Paul's single compound name for the vice is struck from Leviticus' own phrase — the man who 'lieth with mankind'. The list at Corinth is Paul's; the wording is the law's.

evidence.source: But the things that the heathen do immolate, to devils they do immolate, and not to God
evidence.target: and they shall no more immolate their hosts to devils, with whom they have committed fornication

10:20.note: Paul's charge that idol-sacrifice is devil-sacrifice is Leviticus 17:7's own verdict on Israel's sacrifices to the field devils, carried over to the Gentiles' tables.

evidence.source: the things that the heathen do immolate, to devils they do immolate, and not to God.
evidence.target: They immolated to devils and not to God, to gods, which they knew not

10:20.note: Paul's warning to Corinth is Moses' song turned on the nations' altars: sacrifice to devils, and not to God — the apostle keeps the lawgiver's very contrast.

evidence.source: But now Christ is risen again from the dead, the first fruits of them that sleep
evidence.target: you shall bring sheaves of ears, the first fruits of your harvest to the Priest

15:20.note: Paul names the risen Christ with the sheaf's title — the firstfruits of the harvest, which the priest lifts up before the Lord on the morrow after the sabbath (23:11): the very day of the resurrection.

evidence.source: Know you not that they which work in the holy place, eat the things that are of the holy place: and they that serve the altar, participate with the altar?
evidence.target: he shall eat it in the Holy place of the court of the tabernacle

9:13.note: Paul's case for the preacher's living rests on the Levitical arrangement itself: those who minister eat the holy things in the holy place (so also 7:6 for the priests' flesh). The argument is institutional rather than verbal — graded theme.

evidence.source: Behold Israel according to the flesh: they that eat the hosts, are they not partakers of the altar?
evidence.target: the flesh whereof shall be eaten the same day

10:18.note: Paul's altar-communion argument presupposes the peace offering's rule: the flesh is eaten by the offerers on the same day — eating the sacrifice is sharing the altar. What is true at Israel's altar is then turned against table-fellowship with idols.

evidence.source: Neither let us fornicate, as certain of them did fornicate, and there fell in one day three and twenty thousand
evidence.target: and there were slain four and twenty thousand men

10:8.note: Paul counts those who fell in one day at Phogor; Numbers gives the plague's whole toll — three and twenty thousand in the day, four and twenty thousand in all. The seed keys Paul's verse to the sin's opening (25:1); the reckoning of the dead is this verse.

evidence.source: All things are subdued to him
evidence.target: Thou hast subjected all things under his feet,

15:27.note: Paul argues from the psalm's subjection clause; the seed keys the neighbouring 1 Corinthians 15:26 and Ephesians 1:22 to this verse, not this source verse.

evidence.source: Death is swallowed up in victory.
evidence.target: He shall cast death down headlong for ever

15:54.note: Paul introduces the saying as written, and it is this verse — but stated openly: he follows the Greek form ('swallowed up in victory') where this corpus's Vulgate-based Isaias reads 'cast death down headlong for ever'. The saying is the same; the wording differs, and the difference is printed here rather than hidden.

evidence.source: the saints shall judge of the world
evidence.target: gave judgement to the saints on High

6:2.note: The saints shall judge: Paul's astonishing premise is Daniel's courtroom issue — the Ancient of days came and gave judgement to the saints of the Highest.

evidence.source: Death where is thy victory? Death where is thy sting?
evidence.target: I will be thy death o death, thy bite will I be o hell

15:55.note: Graded allusion, honestly: in this corpus Paul's taunt and Osee's promise share the address to death but not a sentence — Osee speaks God's 'I will be thy death' where Paul asks 'where is thy sting?' The seed carries the neighbouring 1 Corinthians 15:54 -> Osee 13:14 pair.

evidence.source: we curse men which are made after the similitude of God
evidence.target: Let us make Man to our image & likeness

3:9.note: James forbids cursing men on Genesis' ground: they are made after the similitude of God.

evidence.source: said also, Thou shalt not kill
evidence.target: Thou shalt not murder

2:11.note: James quotes the sixth commandment; the DR text of Exodus renders the word 'murder' where James has 'kill'.

evidence.source: For he that said, Thou shalt not commit adultery
evidence.target: Thou shalt not commit adultery

2:11.note: James quotes the seventh commandment in the Decalogue's own words, to bind the whole Law to one Speaker.

evidence.source: Behold the hire of the work-men that have reaped your fields, which is defrauded of you, cryeth
evidence.target: The work of thy hireling shall not abide with thee until morning

5:4.note: The hire kept back is Leviticus' exact case — the hireling's wage held past its day. James hears the withheld wage itself crying out. Malachias names the same offence from the same verse (entered separately); Tobias 4:15's wage rule is own-carried.

evidence.source: with prayer he prayed that it might not rain upon the earth, and it rained not for three years and six months.
evidence.target: if there shall be these years dew and rain, but according to the words of my mouth.

5:17.note: James reads the drought oracle as Elias's prayer. The seed carries James 5:17 only at chapter level (3 Kings 17); this is the verse anchor, not a collision.

evidence.source: And he prayed again: and the heaven gave rain
evidence.target: there fell great rain.

5:18.note: The seed keys James 5:18 to 3 Kings 18:41, Elias on Carmel praying; the rain's falling, which James reports, stands at 18:45.

evidence.source: The sufferance of Job you have heard, and the end of our Lord you have seen
evidence.target: our Lord added all things whatsoever had been Job's, double.

5:11.note: James names Job's sufferance and points his readers to its end; the end he means stands here, the Lord turning Job's penance into a double restoration. Tobias' naming of Job is already in our layer; James' was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Today or tomorrow we will go into that city, and there certes will spend a year, and will traffic, and make our gain
evidence.target: Boast not for tomorrow, being ignorant what the day to come may bring forth.

4:13.note: James rebukes the merchants' tomorrow in the proverb's own terms: boast not for tomorrow, being ignorant what the day may bring — James' merchants are ignorant of the very thing the proverb names (4:14).

evidence.source: And the tongue, is fire, a whole world of iniquity.
evidence.target: The impious man diggeth evil, and in his lips fire burneth.

3:6.note: James' tongue that is fire is the proverb's impious man, in whose lips fire burneth while he digs evil.

evidence.source: the sun rose with heat, & parched the grass, and the flower of it fell away
evidence.target: The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen

1:11.note: James's rich man withering in his ways reworks the grass-and-flower saying between Peter's two anchors (40:6 in the seed, 40:8 in this draft): the withered grass and fallen flower are 40:7's.

evidence.source: to visit pupils and widows in their tribulation
evidence.target: judge for the pupil, defend the widow

1:27.note: Clean religion defined as visiting pupils (orphans) and widows is Isaias's 'learn to do good' in apostolic form: judge for the pupil, defend the widow. Graded theme: the shared matter is exact, the wording is James's own.

evidence.source: God made man right, and he hath entangled himself with infinite questions
evidence.target: God created man to his own image

7:30.note: The Preacher sums up the fall in one line: God made man right — created to his image — and man has entangled himself.

evidence.source: If thou hast vowed any thing to God, defer not to pay it: for an unfaithful and foolish promise displeaseth him. But whatsoever thou hast vowed, pay it
evidence.target: he shall not make his word frustrate, but all that he promised he shall fulfill

5:3.note: The Preacher's counsel is the law's edge turned proverb: defer not to pay what thou hast vowed — the same duty this verse lays on the man who binds himself by an oath.

evidence.source: If thou hast vowed any thing to God, defer not to pay it: for an unfaithful and foolish promise displeaseth him. But whatsoever thou hast vowed, pay it:
evidence.target: When thou hast vowed a vow to our Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: because our Lord thy God will require it.

5:3.note: The Preacher's vow-counsel is Deuteronomy's law turned to wisdom: defer not to pay it, for the Lord will require it. Our layer keys Deuteronomy's own restatement of the vow law back to Numbers 30.

evidence.source: As he came forth naked from his mother's womb, so shall he return
evidence.target: Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither

5:14.note: The Preacher restates Job's confession at the loss of all things in Job's own words, turned from one man's loss into every labourer's lot. The seed carries 1 Timothy 6:7 to this verse; the Preacher's taking of it was unkeyed.

evidence.source: In the good day enjoy good things, and beware before of the evil day. For as this, so that also hath God made
evidence.target: if we have received good things of the hand of God, evil things why should we not receive?

7:15.note: The Preacher's counsel — God has made the evil day alongside the good — is Job's rebuke to his wife turned into wisdom: good received from God's hand, and evil not refused.

evidence.source: to the sinner he hath given affliction, and superfluous care, to add, and to gather together, and deliver it to him that hath pleased God
evidence.target: He shall prepare indeed, but the just man shall be clothed with them: and the innocent shall divide the silver.

2:26.note: The Preacher's sinner gathers only to deliver to him that has pleased God; Job had said it of the silver and the raiment: he shall prepare, but the just shall be clothed, the innocent shall divide.

evidence.source: in many words folly will be found.
evidence.target: In much talk there shall not want sin: but he that moderateth his lips is most wise.

5:2.note: The Preacher's warning against many words in prayer is the proverb's warning against much talk, carried into the house of God.

evidence.source: much better is obedience, than the victims of fools
evidence.target: For Better is Obedience Than Victims: and to harken rather than to offer the fat of rams.

4:17.note: The Preacher's counsel at the house of God is Samuel's sentence to Saul turned proverb: better is obedience than victims — in Ecclesiastes, than the victims of fools. The seed carries this verse of Ecclesiastes only at chapter level (1 Kings 15, with Osee 6); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: and the dust return into his earth, from whence it was, and the spirit return to God, who gave it.
evidence.target: dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.

12:7.note: The Preacher's last word on the body is Adam's sentence fulfilled at every death: dust returns into its earth, as it was taken. Our layer keys Genesis 3:19 to Ecclesiastes 3:20 besides; the closing form at 12:7 was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Fear God, and observe his commandments: for this is every man
evidence.target: what doth the Lord thy God require of thee, but that thou fear the Lord thy God

12:13.note: The end of the whole matter — fear God and observe his commandments — is Moses' 'what doth the Lord thy God require of thee' answered in two words. The keeping of the commandments stands in the next verse of Deuteronomy (10:13).

evidence.source: For there is no just man in the earth, that doth good, and sinneth not.
evidence.target: Who can say: My heart is clean, I am pure from sin?

7:21.note: The Preacher states flatly what the proverb asks as a question no man can answer yes to. The seed carries this verse of Ecclesiastes only at chapter level (Proverbs 20, among others); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: For there is no just man in the earth, that doth good, and sinneth not.
evidence.target: for there is no man which sinneth not

7:21.note: Solomon's dedication prayer confesses it first — there is no man which sinneth not — and the Preacher, Solomon's other voice, restates it of the just man himself. The seed carries Ecclesiastes 7:21 to 3 Kings 8 only at chapter level.

evidence.source: He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it
evidence.target: He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that rolleth a stone, it shall return to him.

10:8.note: The Preacher takes the proverb's first clause entire and adds the hedge and the serpent of his own. Sirach's form of the same sentence is keyed to this verse of Ecclesiastes in this draft.

evidence.source: put on the new man which according to God is created in justice, and holiness of the truth
evidence.target: to the image of God he created him

4:24.note: The new man is created according to God, as man was first created to God's image: a creation renewed.

evidence.source: setting him on his right hand in celestials
evidence.target: Sit on my right hand:

1:20.note: The resurrection session in Ephesians is the session psalm's word enacted; stated as allusion, since Paul does not quote the psalm here.

evidence.source: not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing, but that it may be holy and unspotted.
evidence.target: Thou art all fair o my love, and there is not a spot in thee.

5:27.note: Paul's glorious Church, not having spot or wrinkle but holy and unspotted, is the bridegroom's word over the bride in the Canticle: thou art all fair, and there is not a spot in thee.

evidence.source: having your loins girded in truth, and clothed with the breast-plate of justice
evidence.target: justice shall be the girdle of his loins: and faith the girdle of his reins

6:14.note: Paul arms the Church from the prophets' wardrobe: the girded loins are the shoot of Jesse's, whose girdle is justice and faith. The breastplate half of the same verse is 59:17's, carried by the seed at Ephesians 6:17.

evidence.source: having your feet shod to the preparation of the Gospel of peace
evidence.target: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that evangelizeth & preacheth peace

6:15.note: The feet shod with the Gospel of peace are the beautiful feet on the mountains, evangelizing and preaching peace. The seed keys Romans 10:15 to this verse; Paul's arming use was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Hath not one God created us?
evidence.target: male and female he created them

2:10.note: Malachias argues brotherhood from the one creation: one God created them all, male and female — one human family under one Father, which is why despising a brother violates the covenant.

evidence.source: Was not Esau brother to Jacob, saith our Lord, and I loved Jacob
evidence.target: one people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger

1:2.note: Malachias' 'I loved Jacob' is God's later word upon the oracle spoken before the twins were born: the elder shall serve the younger.

evidence.source: in every place there is sacrificing, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation
evidence.target: in every place where the memory of my name shall be: I will come to thee, and will bless thee

1:11.note: Exodus' altar law blesses 'every place where the memory of my name shall be'; Malachias sees the day when 'in every place there is offered to my name a clean oblation' among the Gentiles.

evidence.source: Behold I send mine Angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face
evidence.target: Behold I will send mine Angel, which shall go before thee

3:1.note: 'Behold I send mine Angel' — Malachias opens with the words of the promise that closes the book of the covenant: the Angel who goes before Israel into the promised place.

evidence.source: and them that calumniate the hire of the hired man, the widows, and pupils, and oppress the stranger
evidence.target: Thou shalt not calumniate thy neighbour, nor oppress him by violence. The work of thy hireling shall not abide with thee until morning

3:5.note: The prophet's witness-list is built from Leviticus 19:13 itself: 'calumniate' and the hired man's hire are the verse's own two halves, fused in one phrase.

evidence.source: If you offer the blind to be immolated, is it not evil? & if you offer the lame and the feeble is it not evil?
evidence.target: If it have a blemish, you shall not offer it, neither shall it be acceptable

1:8.note: The prophet's charge — blind, lame and feeble victims on the altar — is measured by the blemish law (spelled out at 22:22: the blind, the broken, the maimed). What would shame a governor's table profanes God's.

evidence.source: My covenant was with him of life and peace: & I gave him fear: and he feared me
evidence.target: Therefore speak to him: Behold I give him the peace of my covenant

2:5.note: The covenant 'of life and peace' Malachias recalls for Levi is this grant to Levi's zealous son: the peace of God's covenant, given to Phinees in the act of zeal.

evidence.source: For the lips of the Priest shall keep knowledge, and the law they shall require of his mouth
evidence.target: thy judgments, o Jacob, and thy law, o Israel: they shall put incense in thy fury, and holocaust upon thine altar.

2:7.note: The priest from whose mouth the law is sought is Levi under Moses' blessing: keeper of God's judgments and law for Israel, and of the altar's incense. Malachias measures a fallen priesthood by the blessing's charge.

evidence.source: She is a tree of life to them that shall apprehend her
evidence.target: the tree of life also in the middle of Paradise

3:18.note: Wisdom is praised in Eden's own title: a tree of life to them that lay hold on her.

evidence.source: When he prepared the heavens, I was present
evidence.target: In the beginning GOD created heaven and earth

8:27.note: Wisdom speaks as present when the heavens were prepared: Genesis' creation contemplated from within, by her who was with the Maker before the earth was made.

evidence.source: A deceitful balance, is abomination before God: and an equal weight is his will
evidence.target: Let the balance be just, and the weights equal, the bushel just, and the sextary equal

11:1.note: The proverb distils the holiness code's market law into one line: 'an equal weight is his will' is Leviticus' just balance in Solomon's dress. Amos and Micheas return to the same law (set aside as alternates).

evidence.source: The impious flyeth, no man pursuing: but the just confident as a lion, shall be without terror
evidence.target: You shall fly, when no man pursueth you

28:1.note: The covenant curse — flying, with no man pursuing — becomes the proverb's portrait of a guilty conscience. The just man's lion-like fearlessness is its mirror image.

evidence.source: Bind them in thy heart continually, and put them about thy throat.
evidence.target: Put these my words in your hearts and minds, and hang them for a sign on your hands, and place them between your eyes.

6:21.note: The father's commandments are to be worn as the law's words were worn: bound in the heart, hung about the body. Proverbs takes Deuteronomy's discipline for God's words and applies it to a father's — the same image stands at 6:8, the phylactery verse.

evidence.source: The light of the just maketh glad: but the candle of the impious shall be extinguished.
evidence.target: Shall not the light of the impious be extinguished, and the flame of his fire not shine?

13:9.note: Bildad's sentence on the impious — his light extinguished, his flame not shining — is distilled into the proverb's candle of the impious, set against the light of the just.

evidence.source: To do mercy and judgment, doth more please our Lord than victims.
evidence.target: because I would mercy, and not sacrifice: and the knowledge of God more than holocausts.

21:3.note: The proverb states as Solomon's settled wisdom what Osee speaks as God's desire: mercy, more pleasing than victims. Ecclesiastes 4:17 carries the same preference from Samuel's sentence (1 Kings 15:22) in this draft.

evidence.source: A most strong tower, the name of our Lord: the just runneth to it, and shall be exalted.
evidence.target: thou art made my hope: a tower of strength from the face of the enemy.

18:10.note: David's tower of strength from the face of the enemy is named in the proverb: the name of the Lord, the most strong tower to which the just man runs.

evidence.source: Reveal thy works to our Lord: and thy cogitations shall be directed.
evidence.target: Reveal thy way to our Lord, and hope in him: and he will do it.

16:3.note: The proverb takes the psalm's verb for its counsel: reveal — thy way, says David; thy works, says Solomon — to the Lord.

evidence.source: I saw a new heaven and a new earth. For the first heaven, and the first earth was gone
evidence.target: In the beginning GOD created heaven and earth

21:1.note: The last book answers the first in its own words: the heaven and earth created in the beginning give place to a new heaven and a new earth.

evidence.source: I saw a new heaven and a new earth
evidence.target: behold I create new heavens, & a new earth

21:1.note: John sees what Isaias heard promised: new heavens and a new earth. The seed points Apocalypse 21 at this verse at chapter level (and keys 2 Peter 3:13 to it at verse level); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: no curse shall be any more
evidence.target: cursed is the earth in thy work: with much toiling shalt thou eat thereof

22:3.note: The end answers the beginning: in the city of God no curse shall be any more, where Eden heard the earth cursed in man's work.

evidence.source: that great dragon was cast forth, the old serpent, which is called the devil and Satan
evidence.target: the serpent also was more subtile than all the beasts of the earth

12:9.note: The Apocalypse names Eden's serpent outright: the old serpent, the devil and Satan, the seducer of the whole world.

evidence.source: death shall be no more, nor mourning, nor crying
evidence.target: in what day soever thou shalt eat of it, thou shalt die the death

21:4.note: The death threatened at the tree, and entered by the eating of it, is abolished in the new creation: death shall be no more — the last word of the story answering the sentence of its first sin.

evidence.source: his kingdom was made dark
evidence.target: horrible darkness in the whole Land of Ægypt three days

16:10.note: The vial judgments replay the Egyptian plagues upon the beast's kingdom: the fifth vial's darkness, in which men gnaw their tongues, answers the ninth plague's three days of darkness over Egypt.

evidence.source: singing the song of Moyses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb
evidence.target: Then sang Moyses and the children of Israel this song to our Lord

15:3.note: The victors by the sea of glass sing 'the song of Moses the servant of God' — the song first sung on the far shore of the Red Sea — joined now to the song of the Lamb.

evidence.source: and singing the song of Moyses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying: Great and marvelous are thy works Lord God omnipotent: just and true are thy ways King of the worlds.
evidence.target: The works of God be perfect, and all his ways judgments: God is faithful, and without any iniquity, just and right.

15:3.note: The redeemed name the song they sing — Moses' — and the Lamb's together; and its words take up the song's own confession, that God's works are great and his ways just. Keyed at the song's first confession of God's ways; the song as a whole stands behind the naming.

evidence.source: hath made us a Kingdom and Priests to God
evidence.target: you shall be unto me a Priestly Kingdom

1:6.note: What God promised Israel at Sinai — 'you shall be unto me a priestly kingdom' — John blesses Christ for having made of his redeemed: 'a kingdom and priests to God'.

evidence.source: Behold the tabernacle of God with men, and he will dwell with them. And they shall be his people: and he God with them shall be their God
evidence.target: they shall make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in the midst of them

21:3.note: The promise first spoken for the tabernacle — 'I will dwell in the midst of them' — is the last word of the new creation, where the tabernacle of God is with men (John also gathers Leviticus 26 and Ezechiel 37 into it).

evidence.source: Behold the tabernacle of God with men, and he will dwell with them. And they shall be his people: and he God with them shall be their God
evidence.target: I will walk among you, & will be your God, & you shall be my people

21:3.note: The covenant formula of Leviticus 26:12 reaches its last form in the new Jerusalem: God dwelling with men, they his people, he their God. Ezekiel 37:27 stands between (entered at 26:11).

evidence.source: Behold the tabernacle of God with men, and he will dwell with them. And they shall be his people
evidence.target: my tabernacle shall be in them: & I will be their God, and they shall be my people

21:3.note: The loud voice's proclamation — God's tabernacle with men, he dwelling with them, they his people — is Ezechiel's covenant formula sounded at the end of all things.

evidence.source: them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a scandal before the children of Israel, to eat and commit fornication
evidence.target: that deceived the children of Israel at the suggestion of Balaam, and made you prevaricate against our Lord upon the sin of Phogor

2:14.note: Moses' own indictment names the teacher John condemns: the eating and fornication at Phogor were Balaam's suggestion. The seed keys this verse of John to Balaam's parting counsel (24:14) and to the sin itself (25:2), but not to the verse that names its author.

evidence.source: If any man shall add to these things, God shall add upon him the plagues written in this book.
evidence.target: You shall not add to the word, that I speak to you, neither shall you take away from it

22:18.note: The last book of Scripture seals itself with the law's own seal: you shall not add to the word. Deuteronomy speaks the command twice (here, and at 12:32); the first stands as the anchor. Proverbs 30:6's 'add not to his words' is set aside — it cannot be told apart between the twin commands.

evidence.source: These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy
evidence.target: if there shall be these years dew and rain, but according to the words of my mouth.

11:6.note: The two witnesses wield Elias's own sign: heaven shut against rain for the days of their prophecy, as it was shut at his mouth.

evidence.source: thou permittest the woman Jezabel, who calleth herself a prophetess, to teach, and to seduce my servants
evidence.target: he took to wife Jezabel the daughter of Ethbaul the king of the Sidonians. And he went, and served Baal, and adored him.

2:20.note: Thyatira's prophetess bears the name of Ahab's queen, introduced here as the Sidonian bride who turned Israel to Baal. The seed carries Apocalypse 2:20 only at chapter level (3 Kings 18).

evidence.source: all nations shall come, and adore in thy sight,
evidence.target: All nations whatsoever thou hast made, shall come, and shall adore before thee, o Lord:

15:4.note: The song before the plagues takes up the psalm's promise that all nations shall come and adore.

evidence.source: Behold I stand at the door and knock. If any man shall hear my voice, and open to me the gate, I will enter in to him
evidence.target: the voice of my beloved knocking: Open to me my sister, my love, my dove, mine immaculate

3:20.note: The risen Lord's word to Laodicea is the Canticle's night scene fulfilled: the beloved's voice knocking — open to me — become 'Behold I stand at the door and knock; if any man shall hear my voice and open, I will enter in to him'.

evidence.source: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet
evidence.target: What is she, that cometh forth as the morning rising, fair as the moon, elect as the sun, terrible as the army of a camp set in array?

12:1.note: The great sign in heaven — a woman clothed with the sun, the moon under her feet — gathers the Canticle's question over the bride: what is she that cometh forth, fair as the moon, elect as the sun, terrible as an army set in array?

evidence.source: the Lion of the Tribe of Juda, the root of David
evidence.target: the root of Jesse, that standeth for a sign of peoples

5:5.note: The elder's consolation names the root of David; Isaias's root of Jesse stands for a sign to the peoples whom the nations beseech. Romans 15:12's use of this verse is the seed's; the throne-room use was unkeyed.

evidence.source: I am the root and stock of David
evidence.target: a rod shall come forth of the root of Jesse

22:16.note: Jesus' self-naming at the book's close — root and stock of David — takes up the oracle's first verse, the rod from Jesse's root.

evidence.source: heaven departed as a book folded together
evidence.target: the heavens shall be folded together as a book

6:14.note: The sixth seal takes the image verbatim: heavens folded together as a book.

evidence.source: Fallen fallen is Babylon the great
evidence.target: Fallen, fallen is Babylon

18:2.note: The doubled cry is Isaias's watchman's, word for word, sounded twice in the Apocalypse (also at 14:8, entered separately).

evidence.source: it is become the habitation of devils, and the custody of every unclean spirit, & the custody of every unclean & hateful bird
evidence.target: beasts shall rest there, and their houses shall be filled with dragons, and ostriches shall dwell there

18:2.note: Fallen Babylon become a haunt of unclean spirits and hateful birds is Isaias's Babylon become a rest for beasts, houses filled with dragons, ostriches dwelling: the desolation menagerie is shared, the wording is each book's own.

evidence.source: Fallen fallen is that great Babylon
evidence.target: Fallen, fallen is Babylon

14:8.note: The first sounding of the watchman's doubled cry in the Apocalypse. The seed points Apocalypse 14 at this verse; the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: Go out from her my people: that you be not partakers of her sins
evidence.target: go out of the midst of her, be cleansed ye that carry the vessels of our Lord

18:4.note: The voice from heaven reissues the exiles' departure charge — go out of her midst, be cleansed — to Babylon's latter-day hearers. The seed keys 2 Corinthians 6:17 to this verse; the Apocalypse use was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Go out from her my people: that you be not partakers of her sins
evidence.target: Go out of the midst of her my people: that every one may save his life

18:4.note: The heavenly voice's first words are Jeremias's Babylon charge, opening syllable for syllable: go out of her, my people. The Isaias 52:11 form of the same charge is entered separately at this verse.

evidence.source: he treadeth the wine press of the fury of the wrath of God omnipotent
evidence.target: I have trodden the press alone, and of the Gentiles there is not a man with me: I have trodden them in my fury

19:15.note: The rider treads the winepress of fury that the Edom victor trod alone. The seed keys Apocalypse 19:13 to 63:2 (the sprinkled garments); the treading itself is 63:3's.

evidence.source: out of his mouth proceedeth a sharp sword: that in it he may strike the Gentiles
evidence.target: he hath made my mouth as a sharp sword

19:15.note: The sharp sword proceeding from the mouth is the Servant's endowment: my mouth made as a sharp sword.

evidence.source: the press was trodden without the city, and blood came forth out of the press
evidence.target: their blood is sprinkled upon my garments

14:20.note: The vintage of wrath: a press trodden and blood coming forth, as in the Edom oracle where the trodden nations' blood sprinkles the victor's garments. The agent differs (angels reap, the rider of ch. 19 treads), stated rather than merged.

evidence.source: he also shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is mingled with pure wine in the cup of his wrath
evidence.target: which hast drunken of the hand of our Lord the cup of his wrath

14:10.note: The cup Jerusalem drank to the dregs is handed on to Babylon's worshippers: wine of wrath, in the cup of his wrath.

evidence.source: her sins are come even to heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities
evidence.target: her judgement hath reached even to the heavens

18:5.note: Babylon's measure mounting to heaven: her sins come even to heaven in John, her judgement reached even to the heavens in Jeremias.

evidence.source: having a golden cup in her hand, full of the abomination
evidence.target: Babylon is a golden cup in the hand of our Lord, inebriating all the earth

17:4.note: The woman's golden cup in her hand is Jeremias's image first: Babylon a golden cup in the Lord's hand, making all the earth drunk.

evidence.source: seduce the nations that are upon the four corners of the earth, Gog, and Magog
evidence.target: set thy face against Gog, and the Land of Magog

20:7.note: Gog and Magog, named together only here and in Ezechiel: John gathers them for the last battle as Ezechiel mustered them against Israel. The seed keys this verse of the Apocalypse to Ezechiel 39:2 and Ezechiel 38:14 to it; the naming oracle itself, 38:2, is entered here.

evidence.source: a river of living water, clear as crystal, proceeding from the seat of God and of the Lamb
evidence.target: waters issued forth under the threshold of the house toward the East

22:1.note: The river of life flows from God's seat as Ezechiel's waters issued from under the temple threshold: the sanctuary is the river's source in both visions.

evidence.source: a river of living water, clear as crystal, proceeding from the seat of God and of the Lamb
evidence.target: living waters shall issue forth out of Jerusalem

22:1.note: The last chapter's river answers Zacharias' living waters out of Jerusalem; Zacharias' own vision in turn parallels Ezechiel 47, entered separately in this draft.

evidence.source: the tree of life, yielding twelve fruits, rendering his fruit every month, & the leaves of the tree for the curing of the Gentiles
evidence.target: every month shall it bring forth first fruits, because the waters thereof shall issue out of the sanctuary: & the fruits thereof shall be for meat, & the leaves thereof for medicine

22:2.note: Fruit every month, leaves for medicine: John's tree of life on both river banks is Ezechiel's orchard on the torrent's banks, its leaves become the curing of the nations.

evidence.source: I took the book of the hand of the Angel, and devoured it: and it was in my mouth as it were honey, sweet
evidence.target: I did eat it: and it was made in my mouth sweet as honey

10:10.note: John eats the little book and finds it honey-sweet in the mouth, as Ezechiel ate the volume. The bitterness in the belly is John's own addition and is not claimed for Ezechiel. The seed keys Apocalypse 10:9 to Ezechiel 3:1; the eating-and-sweetness verse is 3:3's.

evidence.source: there was a rain-bow round about the seat, like to the sight of an Emerald
evidence.target: As the form of the bow when it is in a cloud on a day of rain, this was the form of the brightness round about

4:3.note: The rainbow round the throne: John's emerald bow round the seat answers the bow in the rain-cloud that was the form of the brightness round Ezechiel's glory. Graded parallel: the vision element is shared, the sentences are each seer's own.

evidence.source: the first beast, like to a lion: and the second beast, like to a calf, and the third beast, having the face as it were of a man: and the fourth beast, like to an eagle flying
evidence.target: the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right hand of them four: and the face of an oxe, on the left hand of them four: and the face of an eagle over them four

4:7.note: Lion, calf (Ezechiel's ox), man, eagle: John's four living creatures distribute among four beings the four faces Ezechiel saw on each of his. The redistribution is stated, not hidden.

evidence.source: a book written within and without, sealed with seven seals
evidence.target: which was written within and without: and there were written in it lamentations, and a song, and woe

5:1.note: A book written within and without: John's sealed book in the right hand of him on the throne repeats Ezechiel's rolled book spread before him, in nearly the same words. In this corpus the within-and-without writing stands at 2:9 (the roll's spreading), not 2:10 as in some modern verse divisions.

evidence.source: he that spake with me, had a measure of a reed, of gold, to measure the city
evidence.target: a linen cord in his hand, and a reed of measure in his hand

21:15.note: The golden reed for measuring the city answers the man of brass-like form with the reed of measure in his hand at the temple gate: both visions are surveyed by a reed-bearer.

evidence.source: there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and it was said to me: Arise, and measure the Temple of God
evidence.target: a linen cord in his hand, and a reed of measure in his hand

11:1.note: John is handed the reed and told to measure the temple, as Ezechiel was brought to the man with the reed of measure: the measuring-commission is shared, the sentences are distinct.

evidence.source: What other is like to this great city?
evidence.target: What city is as Tyre, which is become silent in the midst of the sea?

18:18.note: The mourners' cry over burning Babylon takes the form of the lament over Tyre: what city is as this city? — Tyre silent in the midst of the sea, Babylon burning within sight of the sea.

evidence.source: Behold he cometh with the clouds, and every eye shall see him
evidence.target: with the clouds of heaven there came in, as it were the son of man

1:7.note: He cometh with the clouds: the Apocalypse's opening blessing takes Daniel's coming figure for its first Christ-word. The pricked-through half of the verse is Zacharias 12:10's, belonging to the minor-prophets stage, and is not claimed here.

evidence.source: every eye shall see him, and they that pricked him. And all the tribes of the earth shall bewail themselves upon him
evidence.target: they shall look toward me, whom they pierced: and they shall lament him with lamentation as it were upon an only begotten

1:7.note: John's opening vision gathers Zacharias' pierced one and the tribes' mourning. The seed carries this only at chapter level (Apocalypse 1:7 -> Zacharias 12); John 19:37 -> 12:10 is the seed's at verse level.

evidence.source: upon the cloud one sitting like to the Son of man
evidence.target: with the clouds of heaven there came in, as it were the son of man

14:14.note: One sitting on the white cloud like to the Son of man, sickle in hand: Daniel's cloud-borne figure enthroned for the harvest.

evidence.source: his head & hairs were white, as white wool, and as snow
evidence.target: the ancient of days sat: his vesture white as snow, and the hairs of his head as clean wool

1:14.note: The white head and hairs as wool and snow belong first to the Ancient of days; John sees them on the Son of man — the transfer is the vision's own claim and is stated here, not softened.

evidence.source: one like to the Son of man, vested in a priestly garment to the foot
evidence.target: there came in, as it were the son of man

1:13.note: John's first sight among the candlesticks is Daniel's figure — one like, as it were, the Son of man — now vested as priest. The vesture's linen-and-gold colouring is Daniel 10:5–6's, anchored at Apocalypse 1:15.

evidence.source: books were opened: and another book was opened, which is of life: and the dead were judged of those things which were written in the books
evidence.target: judgement sat, and the books were opened

20:12.note: Judgement sat, and the books were opened: John's great-white-throne scene opens Daniel's courtroom books. The seed keys Apocalypse 5:11 to this verse (the thousands of thousands); the books themselves are 20:12's anchor.

evidence.source: his feet like to latten, as in a burning furnace. And his voice as the voice of many waters
evidence.target: the parts that are downward even to the feet, as it were the form of glistering brass: and the voice of his word as the voice of a multitude

1:15.note: Feet as glistering brass, voice as a multitude's voice: John's glorious figure wears the features of Daniel's man by the Tigris.

evidence.source: he sware by him that liveth for ever and ever
evidence.target: when he had lifted up his right hand, & his left hand unto heaven, and had sworn by him that liveth for ever

10:6.note: The mighty angel's oath — by him that liveth for ever — repeats the linen-clothed man's oath on the river, both hands lifted to heaven. The seed keys Daniel 12:7 to Apocalypse 10:5 (the stance); the oath itself is 10:6's.

evidence.source: Michael and his Angels fought with the dragon
evidence.target: Michael one of the chief princes came to aid me

12:7.note: Michael at war: in Daniel, the chief prince who comes to aid against the prince of Persia (and rises for God's people at 12:1); in John, Michael and his angels fighting the dragon in heaven. Graded parallel: the combatant and the war are shared, the sentences are not.

evidence.source: he is Lord of lords, and King of kings
evidence.target: your God is the God of gods, and Lord of kings

17:14.note: The Lamb's war-titles gather Nebuchadnezzar's confession to Daniel: God of gods and Lord of kings. John gives the kingship title to the Lamb in the doubled form (King of kings, Lord of lords); the confession's wording is the anchor's limit, and the entry claims no more.

evidence.source: The kingdom of this world is made our Lord's & his Christ's, and he shall reign for ever and ever
evidence.target: kingdom, and power, and the greatness of the kingdom, that is under all the heaven, be given to the people of the saints of the Highest: whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom

11:15.note: The seventh trumpet's loud voices announce Daniel's transfer: the kingdom under all heaven given, an everlasting kingdom that shall not pass — now made our Lord's and his Christ's, reigning for ever.

evidence.source: The kingdom of this world is made our Lord's & his Christ's, and he shall reign for ever and ever
evidence.target: the kingdom shall be to our Lord

11:15.note: The seventh trumpet's acclamation takes up Abdias' closing word — the kingdom the Lord's — the whole of Abdias' one chapter ending on the same sentence the Apocalypse sounds.

evidence.source: they sat upon them, and judgement was given them
evidence.target: gave judgement to the saints on High

20:4.note: Seats set, they sat, judgement was given them: John's millennial thrones are Daniel's judgement given to the saints, sat in.

evidence.source: she is nourished for a time & times, & half a time, from the face of the serpent
evidence.target: they shall be delivered into his hand even to a time, & times, & half a time

12:14.note: Daniel's measure — a time, and times, and half a time — becomes the woman's wilderness nourishment in the Apocalypse, phrase for phrase.

evidence.source: there was given to it a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies: and power was given to it to work two and forty months
evidence.target: he shall speak words against the High one

13:5.note: The beast's mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, for forty-two months (Daniel's time-times-and-half reckoned in months), is the little horn speaking words against the Highest. The month-count is the entry's arithmetic, stated as such; the speaking mouth is the verbal anchor.

evidence.source: I saw a beast coming up from the sea, having seven heads, and ten horns
evidence.target: four great beasts came up, out of the sea diverse one from another

13:1.note: A beast coming up from the sea: John's single beast gathers Daniel's four sea-beasts into one, ten horns and all — the compositing is the seer's own and is stated here, the sea-rising and the horns being what the entry claims.

evidence.source: These are the two olive trees & the two Candlesticks that stand in the sight of the Lord of the earth
evidence.target: two olive-trees upon it: one on the right hand of the lamp, and one on the left hand thereof

11:4.note: John names Zacharias' vision outright: the two olive trees flanking the candlestick (4:2) are his two witnesses.

evidence.source: I beheld the earth, and lo it was void, and a thing of nothing: and the heavens, & there was no light in them
evidence.target: the earth was void and vacant, and darkness was upon the face of the depth

4:23.note: Jeremias sees judgment as un-creation: the earth void again as before the first day, and the heavens without the light God made.

evidence.source: the mourning, and weeping of Rachel weeping for her children
evidence.target: Rachel therefore died, and was buried in the high way that leadeth to Ephrata

31:15.note: Rachel weeps in Jeremias from the grave Genesis records for her, on the high way that leadeth to Ephrata — the Bethlehem road.

evidence.source: You have not heard me, to proclaim liberty every man to his brother, and every one to his friend
evidence.target: shalt proclaim remission to all the inhabitants of thy land

34:17.note: Jerusalem's masters made the jubilee proclamation — liberty to their Hebrew slaves — and then took it back. Jeremiah answers with God's counter-proclamation of 'liberty' to the sword, the pestilence and the famine, turning Leviticus 25:10's word against them.

evidence.source: because there came a fire out of Hesebon, and a flame out of the midst of Sehon, and it hath devoured part of Moab, and the top of the children of tumult
evidence.target: Afire went forth from Hesebon, a flame from the town of Sehon, & devoured Ar of the Moabites, and the inhabitants of the high places of Arnon

48:45.note: Jeremiah takes up the ancient proverb of Hesebon and turns it on Moab itself: the fire that once went forth from Sehon's town for Israel now devours Moab's own children of tumult.

evidence.source: Woe to thee Moab, thou hast perished, o people of Chamos: because thy sons are taken, and thy daughters into captivity
evidence.target: Woe to thee Moab, thou art undone people of Chamos. He hath given his sons into flight, and his daughters into captivity to Sehon the King of the Amorrheites

48:46.note: The proverb's woe over Moab stands word for word in Jeremiah's mouth; only the flight of the sons has ripened into captivity.

evidence.source: The Prophet, that hath prophesied peace: when his word shall come to pass, the Prophet shall be known, whom our Lord hath sent in truth.
evidence.target: That which the same Prophet foretelleth, in the name of the Lord, & cometh not to pass: that our Lord hath not spoken

28:9.note: Jeremias answers Hananias with Deuteronomy's own test: the prophet is known by whether his word comes to pass. He states the sign from its positive side; the law states it from the false side.

evidence.source: You shall seek me, and shall find: when you shall seek me with all your heart.
evidence.target: thou shalt find him, yet so, if thou seek him with all thy heart, & all tribulation of thy soul.

29:13.note: The letter to the exiles promises in Deuteronomy's own condition: seek with all the heart, and find. Moses spoke it of the return from exile before the exile came.

evidence.source: If a man put away his wife, and she departing from him marry another man, will he return to her any more? Shall not that woman be polluted and contaminated?
evidence.target: the former husband cannot take her again to wife: because she is polluted

3:1.note: Jeremias preaches God's plea out of the divorce law's own case: the wife taken by another cannot return to the former husband, for she is polluted — and yet, saith the Lord, return unto me.

evidence.source: I had put her away, and given her a bill of divorce
evidence.target: he shall write a bill of divorce, and shall give it in her hand, and dismiss her out of his house.

3:8.note: God speaks of Israel's dismissal in the law's own instrument: the bill of divorce, written and given into the hand. The seed keys the Gospel divorce sayings to this verse; Jeremias' use of the bill itself was unkeyed.

evidence.source: An iron yoke have I put upon the neck of all these Nations, to serve Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon, and they shall serve him
evidence.target: Thou shalt serve thine enemy, whom our Lord will send upon thee, in hunger, and thirst, and nakedness, and all penury, and he shall put an iron yoke upon thy neck

28:14.note: Hananias broke the wooden yoke; Jeremias answers with Deuteronomy's curse made iron: serve thine enemy, and an iron yoke upon thy neck. The curse's words become the prophet's sentence on the nations.

evidence.source: If Moyses & Samuel shall stand before me, my soul is not toward this people
evidence.target: And far from me be this sin in our Lord, that I should cease to pray for you,

15:1.note: God names Samuel, with Moses, as the intercessor who would ordinarily stand before him for the people. Samuel's own vow is exactly that standing: far be it from him to cease to pray for them. Jeremias is told even that prayer would now be refused.

evidence.source: And he burnt the house of our Lord. And the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem
evidence.target: And he burnt the house of our Lord, the king's house, and the houses of Jerusalem

52:13.note: Jeremias's closing chapter retells the fall of Jerusalem from Kings; the burning of the house stands in both.

evidence.source: because of Manasses the son of Ezechias the king of Juda, for all things that he did in Jerusalem.
evidence.target: Because Manasses the king of Juda hath done these most wicked abominations

15:4.note: Jeremias names the cause Kings recorded: Manasses' abominations are why the rage falls a generation later. The seed carries Jeremias 15:4 only at chapter level (4 Kings 21).

evidence.source: every one shall say to his neighbour: Why hath the Lord done so to this great city?
evidence.target: every one that shall pass by it, shall wonder, and hiss, and say: Why hath the Lord done thus to this land, and to this house?

22:8.note: Jeremias preaches the byword the Lord himself pronounced over the finished house. The seed carries Jeremias 22:8 only at chapter level (3 Kings 9).

evidence.source: he shall be as a tree that is planted upon the waters, that spreadeth his roots towards moisture:
evidence.target: he shall be as a tree, that is planted nigh to the streams of waters, which shall give his fruit in his time.

17:8.note: Jeremias' blessed man is the psalter's opening tree, leaf and fruit included; the seed keys Jeremias 17 to Psalm 1 at chapter level and 17:7 to the psalm as a whole.

evidence.source: Why doth the way of the impious prosper: why is it well with all that transgress, and do wickedly?
evidence.target: Why then do the impious live, are they advanced, & strengthened with riches?

12:1.note: Jeremias opens his dispute with God in Job's own question — why do the impious prosper? The seed carries this verse of Jeremias only at chapter level (Job 21); the verse anchor is entered here. Habacuc's form of the same question is set aside as mediated through this one.

evidence.source: the turtle, and the swallow, and the stork have observed the time of their coming
evidence.target: the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land:

8:7.note: Jeremias shames the people with the Canticle's spring sign: the turtle-dove whose voice is heard in the land has observed the time of her coming, but my people have not known the judgment of the Lord.

evidence.source: We have heard the pride of Moab, he is proud exceedingly: his haughtiness, and arrogancy, and pride
evidence.target: We have heard the pride of Moab, he is proud exceedingly: his pride and his arrogancy

48:29.note: Jeremias's Moab oracle opens by quoting Isaias's Moab oracle in its own first words, then turns the hearing to judgement. The seed points Jeremias 48 at Isaias 16 at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: Sion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as an heap of stones
evidence.target: Sion shall be ploughed as a field, & Jerusalem be as an heap of stones

26:18.note: Jeremias's defenders quote Micheas by name and office — a prophet in Ezechias's days — and reproduce his sentence nearly word for word (this corpus prints Jeremias's form 'plowed', Micheas's 'ploughed'). It is the Old Testament's own clearest act of quoting a prophet.

evidence.source: When seven years shall be accomplished, let every man dismiss his brother an Hebrew, that was sold to him, and he shall serve thee six years: and thou shalt dismiss him free from thee
evidence.target: When thy brother an Hebrew man, or Hebrew woman is sold to thee, and hath served thee six years, in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free

34:14.note: Jeremias indicts Jerusalem by the release law itself: Hebrew brother, six years' service, dismissed free in the seventh. The seed points Jeremias 34:14 at Deuteronomy 15 at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here. Our layer already carries Jeremias 34:17 to Leviticus 25:10 for the proclaimed liberty; this entry anchors the statute Jeremias recites.

evidence.source: sanctify the Sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers
evidence.target: Remember that thou sanctify the Sabbath day

evidence.source: Which doest mercy on thousands, and renderest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them
evidence.target: which keepest mercy unto thousands: which takest away iniquity, and wicked facts, and sins, and no man of himself is innocent before thee. Which doest render the iniquity of the fathers to the children

32:18.note: Jeremias's prayer at the field purchase opens by reciting the Sinai proclamation — mercy on thousands, iniquity of fathers rendered to children — nearly in its words. The seed points Jeremias 32:18 at Exodus 34 at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: the Heavens were before, and the earth, out of water, and through water, consisting by the word of God
evidence.target: the Spirit of God moved over the waters

3:5.note: Peter's scoffers wilfully forget the first world as Genesis shews it: earth consisting out of water and through water, by the word of God.

evidence.source: that world then, being overflowed with water perished
evidence.target: all flesh was consumed that moved upon the earth

3:6.note: The world that then perished, overflowed with water, is the flood of Genesis, when all flesh that moved upon the earth was consumed.

evidence.source: having followed the way of Balaam of Bosor, which loved the reward of iniquity
evidence.target: having the price of divination in their hands

2:15.note: The reward Balaam loved is here in the elders' hands — the price of divination carried out to him. The 'way' Peter names is the road the angel meets at 22:32 ('thy way is perverse'). The seed carries Peter's next verse, the speaking ass, at 22:23.

evidence.source: gathering the fowls of the heaven, and fishes of the sea
evidence.target: rule over the fishes and the sea, and fowls of the air

1:3.note: Sophonias' gathering-away of man, beast, fowl, and fish unmakes the order of Genesis 1 in reverse: judgment as de-creation.

evidence.source: their silver, and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of our Lord
evidence.target: Riches shall not profit in the day of revenge: but justice shall deliver from death.

1:18.note: Sophonias preaches the proverb at the nations: riches shall not profit in the day of wrath — silver and gold shall not be able to deliver them — where the proverb's other half promises that justice shall deliver.

evidence.source: their silver, and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of our Lord
evidence.target: Their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the fury of our Lord

1:18.note: The undelivering silver-and-gold sentence, near-verbatim in both day-of-wrath oracles. The seed carries Sophonias 1:18 -> Ezechiel 7 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: a day of darkness and mist, a day of cloud & whirlwind
evidence.target: the day of darkness, and of mist is near, the day of cloud, & whirlwind

1:15.note: Sophonias' day-of-wrath litany repeats Joel's darkness-mist-cloud-whirlwind wording. The seed carries Sophonias 1:15 -> Joel 2 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: they shall build houses, and shall not inhabit them: and shall plant vineyards, & shall not drink the wine of them

evidence.source: we clay: and thou art our maker, and all we the works of thy hands
evidence.target: formed man of the slime of the earth

evidence.source: his rod upon the sea, and he shall lift it up in the way of Ægypt
evidence.target: lift up thy rod, and stretch forth thy hand upon the sea, and divide it

evidence.source: according to the plague of Madian in the Rock Oreb,
evidence.target: Oreb he slew in the Rock of Oreb,

10:26.note: Isaias threatens Assur with a scourge according to the plague of Madian in the rock Oreb — the place takes its name from this verse, where Oreb the Madianite prince was slain in the rock called for him. The seed carries Isaias toward Judges 7 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: there shall be a way to the remnant of my people, which shall be left of the Assyrians: as there was to Israel in the day, that he came up out of the Land of Ægypt
evidence.target: went through the midst of the dry sea

11:16.note: The remnant's highway out of Assyria is promised in Exodus' own terms: a way through the sea 'as there was to Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt'.

evidence.source: Which brought forth the chariot & the horse, the arm and the strong: they slept together, neither shall they rise again
evidence.target: the waters returned, and overwhelmed the chariots & the horsemen of all Pharao's army, who following were entered into the sea, neither did there so much as one of them remain

43:17.note: Isaias' new-Exodus song names the drowned host exactly as Exodus does: chariot and horse, and not one of them remaining.

evidence.source: and our Lord hath put upon him the iniquity of all us
evidence.target: let him confess all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their offences and sins: which praying to light on his head

53:6.note: All Israel's iniquities, confessed over the goat's head to light on him and be carried away — Isaiah sees that laying-on concentrated on the Servant: the Lord 'put upon him the iniquity of all us'.

evidence.target: And when the goat hath carried all their iniquities into the solitary ground
