evidence.source: Is this such a fast, as I have chosen: for a man by the day to afflict his soul?
evidence.target: The seventh month, the tenth day of the month you shall afflict your souls

58:5.note: Isaiah's question is aimed at the Day of Atonement's own phrase — 'afflict your souls', the one commanded soul-affliction of the year. The prophet asks whether bowing the head like a rush is the affliction God chose.

evidence.source: preach indulgence to the captives, and deliverance to them that are shut up
evidence.target: Thou shalt sanctify the fiftieth year, and shalt proclaim remission to all the inhabitants of thy land: for it is the year of Jubilee

61:1.note: The anointed one's proclamation to captives is the jubilee act itself: in the fiftieth year remission is proclaimed to all the land's inhabitants, and every man returns to his possession. Jesus reads this text at Nazareth (Luke 4) — that link runs through Isaiah and is set aside as mediated.

evidence.source: they that did eat swine's flesh, and abomination, and the mouse
evidence.target: the swine: which though it divideth the hoof, cheweth not the cud

66:17.note: Isaiah's condemned garden-rites feast on Leviticus 11's own unclean list — the swine named at 11:7, the mouse following at 11:29 among the creeping things.

evidence.source: Hear ye heavens, & give ear o earth, because our Lord hath spoken.
evidence.target: Hear ye heavens what things I speak, the earth hear the words of my mouth.

1:2.note: Isaias opens his prophecy by taking up the witnesses Moses summoned at the opening of his song: heavens and earth, called to hear.

evidence.source: We have groped as blind men for the wall, and as without eyes have feeled: we have stumbled at noon day as in darkness
evidence.target: & grope thou at midday as the blind is wont to grope in the dark, and direct not thy ways.

59:10.note: Isaias' confession takes up the curse's doubled image entire: groping like the blind, and stumbling at midday as in darkness. The curse is confessed as the people's present state.

evidence.source: thou hast overcome, as in the day of Madian.
evidence.target: But Madian was humbled before the children of Israel, neither could they any more lift up their necks

9:4.note: The child prophecy measures the coming victory by the day of Madian: yoke, rod and sceptre overcome as then. The day itself closes at this verse, Madian humbled and unable to lift its neck under Gedeon. The seed carries this verse of Isaias to Judges 7 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: For our Lord shall stand as in the mount of divisions: as in the valley, which is in Gabaon, shall he be angry
evidence.target: Our Lord hath divided mine enemies before me, as waters are divided, therefore the name of the place was called Baal Pharasim.

28:21.note: Isaias's strange work is measured by the mount of divisions — Baal Pharasim, the lord of divisions, where David said the Lord divided his enemies as waters are divided, and named the place for it. The valley of Gabaon in the same verse of Isaias belongs to Josue's history; the mount belongs to this verse. The seed carries the pair at chapter level only.

evidence.source: Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came up against all the fenced cities of Juda, and took them.
evidence.target: came up Sennacherib the king of Assyrians to all the fenced cities of Juda: and took them.

36:1.note: Isaias 36-39 retells the Kings history of Ezechias; this is its opening verse against Kings' own. The seed carries the pair only at chapter level (4 Kings 18).

evidence.source: Ezechias was sick even to death: and Isaie the son of Amos the Prophet, went in unto him
evidence.target: Ezechias was sick even to death: & Isaie the son of Amos the prophet came and said to him

38:1.note: The sickness oracle in the prophet's own book and in Kings, nearly word for word. The seed carries Isaias 38:1 only at chapter level (4 Kings 20).

evidence.source: Merodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters & gifts to Ezechias
evidence.target: Berodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, the king of the Babylonians sent letters & gifts to Ezechias

39:1.note: The Babylonian embassy in both tellings. The envoy's name is printed Merodach in Isaias and Berodach in Kings, as the corpus stands; the difference is noted, not smoothed.

evidence.source: which sittest upon the Cherubs, thou art the only God of all the kingdoms of the earth, thou hast made heaven and earth.
evidence.target: which sittest upon the cherubins, thou art the only God of all the kings of the earth: thou madest heaven and earth:

37:16.note: Ezechias's prayer before the letter, in Isaias's telling and in Kings'. Small wording differences (Cherubs/cherubins, kingdoms/kings) stand as printed.

evidence.source: the Angel of our Lord came forth, and struck in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred eighty five thousand.
evidence.target: an Angel of our Lord came, and struck in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred eighty five thousand.

37:36.note: The deliverance itself, in both tellings. Machabees' prayers recalling the same night are keyed to the Kings verse separately.

evidence.source: hell shall not confess to thee, neither shall death praise thee:
evidence.target: in hell who shall confess to thee?

38:18.note: Ezechias' canticle argues with the psalm's own argument: in hell, who shall confess thee?

evidence.source: The living the living he shall confess to thee, as I also this day:
evidence.target: I shall not die, but shall live: and I will tell the works of our Lord.

38:19.note: Ezechias, turned back from death, takes up the psalm's I shall not die but live.

evidence.source: our Lord is my strength, and my praise, & he is become my salvation.
evidence.target: Our Lord is my strength, and my praise: and he is made my salvation.

12:2.note: Isaias' short canticle sings this verse of the festal psalm (itself Exodus 15:2's word); the seed keys Isaias 12:2 to Psalm 117 only at chapter level.

evidence.source: they have conceived labour, and brought forth iniquity.
evidence.target: He conceived sorrow, and hath brought forth iniquity

59:4.note: Eliphaz's sentence on the wicked man becomes Isaias' sentence on the whole people. The seed carries this verse of Isaias only at chapter level (Job 15); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: our Lord will visit with his sore, and great, and strong sword upon Leviathan the serpent
evidence.target: Canst thou draw out the Leviathan with a hook

27:1.note: The Leviathan no man can draw out with a hook is the serpent the Lord himself will visit with his great sword in that day. The seed carries this verse of Isaias only at chapter level (Job 40); in this corpus the Leviathan discourse opens at 40:20.

evidence.source: My life is cut off, as by a weaver; whilst I yet began he cut me off
evidence.target: My days have passed more swiftly, than the web is cut of the weaver

38:12.note: Ezechias on his sickbed laments in Job's figure: a life cut off as by a weaver, the web severed before its time.

evidence.source: a rod shall come forth of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root.
evidence.target: A tree hath hope: if it be cut, it waxeth green again, and the boughs thereof spring.

11:1.note: Job's hope for a cut tree — it waxes green again and its boughs spring — is the shape of Isaias' promise: a rod coming forth from the cut root of Jesse. Graded parallel: the hope is the same, the wording is not.

evidence.source: Hast not thou strucken the proud, & wounded the dragon?
evidence.target: with his wisdom he struck the proud man.

51:9.note: The arm of the Lord is asked whether it has not struck the proud and wounded the dragon — Job's hymn says his wisdom struck the proud one, and the winding serpent follows in the next verse (26:13).

evidence.source: Thy dead shall live, my slain shall rise again: awake, and praise ye that dwell in the dust
evidence.target: I know that my Redeemer liveth, & in the last day I shall rise out of the earth.

evidence.source: Their feet run to evil, & hasten to shed innocent blood
evidence.target: For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.

evidence.source: because I called, and you have not answered: I spake, and you have not heard
evidence.target: Because I called, and you refused: I stretched out my hand, and there was none that regarded.

evidence.source: he is a liar, & the father thereof

evidence.source: before that Abraham was made, I am
evidence.target: I am Which AM

evidence.source: God no man hath seen at any time
evidence.target: Thou canst not see my face: for man shall not see me, & live

evidence.source: That this is the Prophet indeed that is to come into the world.
evidence.target: A prophet of thy nation & of thy brethren like unto me, will our Lord thy God raise up to thee: him thou shalt hear,

evidence.source: the Father that sent me, he gave me commandment what I should say, and what I should speak.
evidence.target: I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak all things that I shall command him.

evidence.source: that the bodies might not remain upon the cross on the Sabboth

evidence.source: You shall not break a bone of him.
evidence.target: Our Lord keepeth all their bones: there shall not one of them be broken.

evidence.source: they hated me gratis.
evidence.target: that hate me without cause,

evidence.source: thou hearest his voice, but thou knowest not whence he cometh and whither he goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.

evidence.source: the house was filled of the odour of the ointment.
evidence.target: we will run after thee in the odour of thine ointments.

evidence.source: He hath blinded their eyes, and indurated their heart: that they may not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I heal them

evidence.source: when he saw his glory, & spake of him
evidence.target: I saw our Lord sitting upon an high throne and elevated

12:41.note: John says Esaias spoke of Christ because he saw his glory — the temple vision of chapter 6, where the prophet saw the Lord on the high throne.

evidence.source: Behold the lamb of God, behold him that taketh away the sin of the world
evidence.target: he shall bear their iniquities

1:29.note: The Baptist's title joins the lamb (53:7's image, carried by the seed at Acts 8:32) to the sin-bearing that is 53:11's own words: the just servant justifies many, bearing their iniquities.

evidence.source: If any man thirst, let him come to me, and drink
evidence.target: All ye that thirst come to the waters

7:37.note: At the feast's great day Jesus stands and cries Isaias's market invitation — all ye that thirst, come — and names himself its waters. The seed keys Apocalypse 22:17 to this verse; the feast-day cry was unkeyed.

evidence.source: all that are in the graves, shall hear his voice
evidence.target: Thy dead shall live, my slain shall rise again: awake, and praise ye that dwell in the dust

5:28.note: The hour when all in the graves hear his voice stands on the prophets' resurrection word; its judgement half is Daniel 12:2's, entered at John 5:29. This verse's half — the dead living, dust-dwellers awaking — is Isaias 26:19's. Graded theme: no phrase is carried over, the hope is.

evidence.source: I am the good Pastor
evidence.target: One Pastor: who shall feed them, my servant David

10:11.note: Ezechiel promises one shepherd raised up over the flock, God's servant David; Jesus takes the office in the first person: I am the good Shepherd. The seed keys John 10:16 to Ezechiel 37:24 for the one-flock close of the same discourse; the office itself is 34:23's.

evidence.source: unless a man be born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the Kingdom of God
evidence.target: I will pour out upon you clean water, and you shall be cleansed from all your contaminations

3:5.note: Born of water and the Spirit answers Ezechiel's restoration in its two movements: clean water poured out and cleansing from all contaminations (36:25), and a new spirit put within (36:27, the verse after the new heart). Graded theme honestly: the link is the cleansing water and the given Spirit together, not a carried phrase.

evidence.source: he hath given him power to do judgement also because he is the Son of man
evidence.target: And he gave him power, and honour, and kingdom: and all peoples, tribes, & tongues shall serve him

5:27.note: Judgement-power given to the Son of man: Daniel sees power, honour and kingdom given to the cloud-borne figure; John hears the Father say the judgement was given because he is the Son of man. Graded theme: the given authority and the title are shared, no phrase is carried.

evidence.source: they that have done good things, shall come forth into the resurrection of life: but they that have done evil into the resurrection of judgement
evidence.target: many of those, that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake: some unto life everlasting, & others unto reproach to see it always

5:29.note: The resurrection sorted two ways — to life, to judgement — is Daniel's first clear word of it: sleepers in the dust awaking, some to life everlasting, others to reproach. Our layer carries this verse to the Machabean martyrs; the Lord's own use was unkeyed.

evidence.source: God sent his Son made of a woman, made under the Law
evidence.target: I will put enmity between thee & the woman, & thy seed and the seed of her

4:4.note: The promise in Eden ran between the serpent and the woman, her seed against his: in the fullness of time God sent his Son made of a woman, the woman's seed come to end the enmity.

evidence.source: on the Gentiles the blessing of Abraham might be made in Christ Jesus
evidence.target: IN Thee shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed

3:14.note: Paul names the blessing of Abraham made upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus: the kindreds of the earth blessed in Abraham, as was promised.

evidence.source: which is Agar
evidence.target: having an handmaid, an Ægyptian named Agar

4:24.note: Paul's allegory takes its figure from Genesis' plain introduction: Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, named Agar.

evidence.source: are the two testaments. The one from mount Sina, gendering unto bondage; which is Agar
evidence.target: our Lord descended upon the mount Sinai

4:24.note: Paul's allegory of the two covenants turns entirely on Sinai as the mountain where the covenant 'gendering unto bondage' was given — the descent of the Lord upon the mount in Exodus 19.

evidence.source: we brethren, according to Isaac, are the children of promise
evidence.target: she conceived & bare a son in her old age, at the time that God had foretold her

4:28.note: To be children of promise 'according to Isaac' is to be born as Isaac was: by promise, at the time God foretold, to parents in their old age.

evidence.source: the Law which was made after four hundred and thirty years
evidence.target: that they abode in Ægypt, was four hundred thirty years

3:17.note: Paul's whole argument from chronology hangs on Exodus' own figure: the sojourn was four hundred thirty years, and the Law came after.

evidence.source: Cursed be every one that abideth not in all things that be written in the book of the Law, to do them.
evidence.target: Cursed be he that abideth not in the words of this law, and fulfilleth them not in work

3:10.note: Paul quotes the last of Ebal's curses, the one that seals all the rest: abiding in all the words of the law, and fulfilling them in work.

evidence.source: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree
evidence.target: he is accursed of God that hangeth on a tree

3:13.note: Paul's parenthesis is Deuteronomy's sentence on the hanged man, quoted as written. The seed carries this verse of Galatians only at chapter level (Deuteronomy 21); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: For what things a man shall sow, those also shall he reap.
evidence.target: I have seen them that work iniquity, and sow sorrows, and reap them,

6:8.note: Eliphaz's observed law — they that sow sorrows reap them — is the root of Paul's 'what things a man shall sow, those also shall he reap', turned from the wicked's sorrows to flesh and spirit.

evidence.source: that separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace
evidence.target: The Lord hath called me from the womb, from my mother's belly he hath been mindful of my name

1:15.note: Paul's separation and calling from the womb speak the Servant's opening words. The companion anchor in Jeremias 1:5 is entered separately; Paul's sentence carries both prophets' womb-calling language.

evidence.source: that separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace
evidence.target: Before I formed thee in the womb, I knew thee: and before thou camest forth of the matrice, I sanctified thee

1:15.note: Paul, separated from his mother's womb and called, takes Jeremias's own call as his pattern — known, sanctified, given to the Gentiles before birth. The Isaias 49:1 anchor of the same sentence is entered separately.

evidence.source: the just liveth by faith
evidence.target: the just shall live in his faith

3:11.note: Paul's Habacuc anchor. The seed carries this only at chapter level (Habacuc 2:5 -> Galatians 3, and Romans 1:17 -> Habacuc 2:4 at verse level); the Galatians verse-level entry is filled here.

evidence.source: all that take the sword shall perish with the sword
evidence.target: Whosoever shall shed man's blood, his blood shall be shed: for to the image of God man was made

26:52.note: The Lord's word in Gethsemane restates the flood covenant's law: blood for blood, and its reason — man made to the image of God.

evidence.source: Judas begat Phares and Zaram of Thamar
evidence.target: the other came forth: and the woman said: Why is the partition divided for thee? And for this cause called his name Phares

1:3.note: Matthew's genealogy keeps Thamar and her twins in the royal line: Phares, named for the partition divided at his birth.

evidence.source: they are dead that sought the life of the child
evidence.target: they are all dead that sought thy life

2:20.note: The angel's word to Joseph repeats, nearly word for word, God's word to Moses in Madian; Matthew draws the parallel between the two children himself.

evidence.source: He that shall curse father or mother, dying let him die
evidence.target: He that curseth his father, or mother, dying let him die

15:4.note: The Lord quotes the law of the cursing child in its own words, beside the fifth commandment (which the seed already carries at 20:12).

evidence.source: there came they that received the didrachmes
evidence.target: half a sicle according to the measure of the temple. A sicle hath twenty oboles. The half part of a sicle shall be offered to the Lord

17:23.note: The didrachma the collectors seek from the Lord is the half-shekel first imposed at the numbering in Exodus — every man's ransom 'offered to the Lord'; the Lord's answer turns on who truly owes it. (In this corpus the collectors' question stands at Matthew 17:23.)

evidence.source: You have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.
evidence.target: eye for eye, tooth for tooth he shall restore

5:38.note: The Lord quotes the talion clause of Leviticus 24 — the law of retaliation that follows the blasphemer's case — before his own 'But I say to you not to resist evil'.

evidence.source: Again you have heard that it was said to them of old, Thou shalt not commit perjury: but thou shall perform thy oaths to our Lord.
evidence.target: Thou shalt not forswear thyself in my name, nor pollute the name of thy God

5:34.note: The old saying the Lord cites is Leviticus' ban on swearing falsely by God's name; its second half also gathers the law of vows performed (Numbers 30). In this corpus the oath saying stands at Matthew 5:34; the seed keys that verse to the neighbouring 19:11, but the perjury clause itself is 19:12.

evidence.source: but thou shall perform thy oaths to our Lord
evidence.target: all that he promised he shall fulfill

5:34.note: The second half of the old saying in the Sermon — perform thy oaths to the Lord — is the vow law of this verse. Its perjury half is already keyed to Leviticus 19:12 in our layer; in this corpus the saying stands at Matthew 5:34.

evidence.source: I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us if thou be Christ the Son of God
evidence.target: If a soul sin, and hear the voice of one swearing, and be witness, because either he himself saw, or is privy to it: unless he utter it, he shall bear his iniquity

26:63.note: Caiaphas puts Jesus under adjuration — the solemn 'voice of one swearing' of Leviticus 5:1, which binds the hearer who is privy to the matter to utter it or bear his iniquity. Jesus, who had held his peace, answers under it.

evidence.source: Then the high Priest rent his garments, saying: He hath blasphemed
evidence.target: he shall not rent his garments

26:65.note: At the verdict the high priest does the one thing Leviticus forbids the anointed high priest to do, even in mourning: he rents his garments.

evidence.source: For we have seen his star in the East, and are come to adore him.
evidence.target: A star Shall Rise out of Jacob, and a rod shall arise from Israel

2:2.note: The star the Sages follow to Bethlehem is Balaam's star, risen out of Jacob in the last of his parables. Our Genesis stage already keys Jacob's own blessing (Gen 49:10) to this verse; the sighting itself was still unkeyed.

evidence.source: And seeing the multitudes, he pitied them; because they were vexed, and lay like sheep that have not a shepherd
evidence.target: lest the people of our Lord be as sheep without a pastor

9:36.note: The compassion of Jesus over the multitudes speaks Moses' prayer back to him — sheep without a shepherd — and answers it in his own person, the man provided to go in and out before them.

evidence.source: they were vexed, and lay like sheep that have not a shepherd
evidence.target: my sheep were dispersed, because there was no Pastor

9:36.note: Sheep with no shepherd, dispersed for want of a pastor: Matthew's compassion sentence is Ezechiel's diagnosis. Our layer carries this verse of Ezechiel to Numbers 27:17 (Moses' prayer) from the other side; the evangelist's use was unkeyed.

evidence.source: For the poor you have always with you: but me you have not always.
evidence.target: There shall not want poor in the land of thy habitation: therefore I command thee that thou open thy hand to thy needy and poor brother

26:11.note: The Lord's 'the poor you have always with you' is Deuteronomy's standing fact — the poor shall not cease out of the land — spoken over the ointment at Bethany. Mark's telling of the same saying is set aside; this entry carries it.

evidence.source: and his Disciples being hungry, began to pluck the ears, and to eat.
evidence.target: If thou enter into thy friend's corn, thou shalt break the ears, and rub them in thy hand: but with a sickle thou shalt not reap.

12:1.note: What the disciples do in the cornfield is exactly what this law permits: ears broken by hand and eaten on the spot, no sickle. The day's controversy is the sabbath, not the plucking — the plucking was always lawful.

evidence.source: And Salmon begat Booz of Rahab.
evidence.target: But Rahab the harlot and the house of her father, and all that she had, Josue caused to live, and they dwelt in the midst of Israel until this present day

1:5.note: The genealogy names Rahab as Booz's mother; Josue's book is where she is spared and dwells in Israel to this day, which is how she stands in the line at all. Her faith is keyed by the seed at Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25 to chapter 2; her preservation into the genealogy is this verse.

evidence.source: And Booz begat Obed of Ruth. And Obed begat Jesse.
evidence.target: called his name Obed: this is the father of Isai, the father of David.

1:5.note: Matthew's line runs Booz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse; Ruth's book closes on that same birth, the neighbours naming Obed, father of Isai (Jesse), father of David. The seed carries Matthew 1:3 to Ruth 4:18's genealogy list; the birth verse itself was unkeyed.

evidence.source: And David the king begat Salomon of her that was the wife of Urias.
evidence.target: David sent and brought her in into his house, & she became his wife, and she bare him a son:

1:6.note: Matthew refuses Bethsabee's name and calls her her that was the wife of Urias — the genealogy itself points at the adultery. The verse it points to is this one: David bringing Urias's wife into his house after the mourning. Solomon's later birth to her is keyed by the seed at 2 Kings 12:24; the Urias clause belongs here.

evidence.source: there appeared to them Moyses and Elias talking with him.
evidence.target: Elias ascended by a hurl wind into heaven.

17:3.note: Elias appears on the mountain because his earthly exit was not death but being taken up; the parallel rests on that, and shares no wording beyond his name.

evidence.source: unto the blood of Zacharias the son of Barachias, whom you murdered between the temple & the altar.
evidence.target: they threw stones according to the king's commandment, in the court of the house of our Lord.

23:35.note: The Zacharias stoned in the temple court is Joiada's son in Chronicles. Stated openly: Matthew names him son of Barachias, Chronicles son of Joiada — the texts are not harmonised here. The seed keys both Matthew 23:35 and Luke 11:51 to the dying words at 24:22; the stoning itself stands at 24:21.

evidence.source: she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Salomon
evidence.target: And all the earth desired to see Salomon's face, that they might hear his wisdom, which God had given in his heart.

12:42.note: The seed keys the queen's coming itself (Matthew 12:42 and Luke 11:31 to 3 Kings 10:1); this anchors the hearing of the wisdom, which is the Lord's own point, in the chapter's summary verse. Luke's telling is set aside as this entry's duplicate.

evidence.source: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
evidence.target: God my God have respect to me: why hast thou forsaken me?

27:46.note: The cry from the cross. This corpus counts the psalm's title as verse 1, so the cry stands at 21:2; the seed keys Mark 15:34 to the title verse 21:1.

evidence.source: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of our Lord.
evidence.target: Blessed be he that cometh in the name of our Lord.

23:39.note: Jesus takes the festal greeting on his own lips as the condition of Jerusalem seeing him again; on the corpus numbering see the Luke 19:38 entry.

evidence.source: they gave him wine to drink mingled with gall.
evidence.target: And they gave gall for my meat:

27:34.note: Matthew's gall answers the psalm's gall; the vinegar half of the same psalm verse is keyed from John 19:28 in the seed.

evidence.source: he came unto them walking upon the sea.
evidence.target: He that alone spreadeth the heaven, & goeth upon the waves of the sea.

14:25.note: What Job confesses of God alone — going upon the waves of the sea — the Lord does on the lake in the fourth watch. Mark's and John's tellings of the same walking are set aside; Matthew's carries the verse.

evidence.source: whosoever shall see a woman to lust after her, hath already committed adultery with her in his heart.
evidence.target: I have made a covenant with mine eyes, that I would not so much as think of a virgin.

5:29.note: Job's defence begins with the covenant he made with his eyes not so much as to think of a virgin; the Lord's sermon names the same look adultery already committed in the heart. Corpus numbering: the looking saying stands at Matthew 5:29 in this text, one verse later than in modern editions.

evidence.source: as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.
evidence.target: He lendeth our Lord that hath mercy on the poor: and he will repay him the like.

25:40.note: Graded theme, honestly: the link is the identification, not shared wording. The proverb says mercy to the poor is a loan to the Lord, repaid by him; the King in the judgment names the mechanism — done to the least brethren, it was done to me.

evidence.source: Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the Kingdom of their Father.
evidence.target: the path of the just, as shining light, proceedeth even to perfect day.

13:43.note: The proverb's path of the just, shining light proceeding to perfect day, reaches its day in the Lord's word: then shall the just shine as the sun in the Father's kingdom.

evidence.source: Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the Kingdom of their Father
evidence.target: they that be learned shall shine as the brightness of the firmament: and they that instruct many to justice, as stars unto perpetual eternities

13:43.note: The just shining at the harvest's end: Daniel's learned who instruct many to justice shine as the firmament's brightness and as stars; Jesus gathers the shining into one sun-like blaze in the Father's kingdom.

evidence.source: And when you are praying, speak not much, as the Heathen. For they think that in their much-speaking they may be heard.
evidence.target: For God is in heaven, and thou upon the earth: therefore let thy words be few.

6:7.note: The Lord's prayer-teaching — speak not much, for the heathen think they are heard for much-speaking — is the Preacher's ground stated from heaven's side: God is in heaven, thou upon earth, therefore let thy words be few.

evidence.source: planted a vineyard, and made a hedge round about it, and digged in it a press, and builded a tower, and let it out to husbandmen
evidence.target: The peace-maker had a vineyard, in that which hath peoples: he delivered the same to keepers

21:33.note: Graded parallel, with the parable's other source named: the hedge, press and tower are Isaias 5's; what the Canticle shares with the parable is the vineyard delivered to keepers — the peace-maker's (Solomon's) vineyard let out, as the householder lets his out to husbandmen.

evidence.source: Consider the lilies of the field how they grow
evidence.target: I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys.

6:28.note: The Lord bids his disciples consider the lilies of the field; the bride names herself with the field's own flower — the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys. Graded allusion on the field-and-lily pairing, stated as such.

evidence.source: the people that sat in darkness, hath seen great light
evidence.target: The people that walked in darkness, hath seen great light

4:16.note: Matthew completes his Galilee citation (the seed keys 4:15 to 9:1): the people in darkness see the great light, in both tellings risen on those in the shadow of death.

evidence.source: With hearing shall you hear; and you shall not understand
evidence.target: Hear ye that hear, and understand not

13:14.note: Matthew names the prophecy fulfilled in the parables' hearers. The seed carries Mark's, Luke's and Acts' forms of the hardening word; Matthew's own full citation was unkeyed.

evidence.source: the heart of this people is waxed gross, and with their ears they have heavily heard, and their eyes they have shut
evidence.target: Blind the heart of this people, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes

13:15.note: The second half of Matthew's citation: gross heart, heavy ears, shut eyes, lest they see, hear, understand and be healed.

evidence.source: He shall not contend, nor cry out, neither shall any man hear in the streets his voice
evidence.target: He shall not cry, nor accept person, neither shall his voice be heard abroad

12:19.note: Matthew's long Servant citation, verse by verse: the seed keys only its opening (12:18 to 42:1). The quiet voice, heard by no man abroad, is 42:2's.

evidence.source: The reed bruised he shall not break, & smoking flax he shall not extinguish
evidence.target: The bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench

12:20.note: The bruised reed and smoking flax, carried over almost word for word.

evidence.source: And in his name the Gentiles shall hope
evidence.target: and the islands shall expect his law

12:21.note: The citation's close. Matthew, following the Greek, reads hope in his name where this corpus's Isaias reads the islands expecting his law — the divergence is stated, not smoothed; the verse and the expectation are the same.

evidence.source: And he answered him not to any word
evidence.target: he shall be dumb, & shall not open his mouth

27:14.note: Before Pilate the silence itself fulfils the portrait: as a lamb before his shearer, dumb, opening not his mouth. Mark 15:5's parallel silence is set aside as this entry's synoptic duplicate.

evidence.source: Then did they spit on his face, and buffeted him
evidence.target: my cheeks to the pluckers: I have not turned away my face from the rebukers & spitters

26:67.note: Spit upon, buffeted, smitten on the face before the council: the Servant gave his cheeks to the pluckers and did not turn his face from the spitters.

evidence.source: I was an hungered, and you gave me to eat
evidence.target: Break thy bread to the hungry

25:35.note: The King's reckoning — I was hungry and you gave me to eat — is Isaias's true fast read back as judgement: break thy bread to the hungry. The seed points Matthew 25 at this verse at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light
evidence.target: the sun is darkened in his rising, and the moon shall not shine in her light

24:29.note: The tribulation discourse's darkened sun and lightless moon are Babylon's oracle astronomy. The seed keys this verse of Matthew to Ezechiel 32:7; Isaias 13:10 is the saying's first home, and Ezechiel's reuse of it is entered in this draft.

evidence.source: the stars shall fall from Heaven
evidence.target: all their host shall fall away as the leaf falleth from the vine

24:29.note: The falling stars of the same sentence are Edom's oracle: the host of heaven falling away as leaves from vine and fig tree.

evidence.source: Heaven and earth shall pass, but my words shall not pass
evidence.target: the heavens shall melt as smoke, and the earth shall be worn away as a garment

24:35.note: Heaven and earth passing, while what God speaks stands for ever: Isaias's heavens melting as smoke and earth wearing away, his salvation and justice never failing.

evidence.source: you shall find rest to your souls
evidence.target: you shall find refreshing for your souls

11:29.note: Find rest for your souls: Jesus' yoke saying closes with Jeremias's old-paths promise, refreshing for your souls to those who walk the good way. The seed points Matthew 11 at this verse at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here. Ecclesiasticus 51:34's yoke, in our layer, points to the same verse of Matthew from the other side.

evidence.source: he shall separate them one from another, as the pastor separateth the sheep from the goats
evidence.target: Behold I judge between beast & beast, of rams, & of buck goats

25:32.note: The Son of man separating sheep from goats enacts Ezechiel's judgement between beast and beast, rams and buck-goats, within the shepherd oracle whose scattered-flock half the seed and our layer already key.

evidence.source: goeth to seek that which is strayed
evidence.target: That which was lost, I will seek: & that which was cast away, I will bring again

18:12.note: The shepherd leaving the ninety-nine to seek the strayed sheep walks Ezechiel's promise. Luke 15:4's form of the parable is set aside as this entry's synoptic duplicate.

evidence.source: the graves were opened: and many bodies of the saints that had slept, rose
evidence.target: Behold I will open your graves, and will bring you out of your sepulchres o my people

27:52.note: At the crucifixion the graves opening and saints rising enact, ahead of the general resurrection, Ezechiel's promise over the dry bones: I will open your graves and bring you out of your sepulchres.

evidence.source: they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of Heaven with much power and majesty
evidence.target: with the clouds of heaven there came in, as it were the son of man

24:30.note: The Olivet sign itself: the Son of man coming in heaven's clouds is Daniel's night vision seen from its far side. The seed keys Matthew 26:64 and Mark 13:26 to this verse; the discourse's own occurrence was unkeyed.

evidence.source: when the Son of man shall come in his majesty, and all the Angels with him, then shall he sit upon the seat of his majesty
evidence.target: thrones were set, and the ancient of days sat

25:31.note: Thrones set for judgement in Daniel; the Son of man come in majesty and sitting on his majesty's seat in Matthew: the judgement session is one scene in two tellings.

evidence.source: the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing in the holy place
evidence.target: the abomination to desolation shall be set up

24:15.note: Jesus names Daniel the prophet for the abomination of desolation; Daniel speaks it three times. The seed keys this verse of Matthew to 9:27; the set-up of the abomination after the continual sacrifice is taken away is 12:11's form, and 11:31's is entered next.

evidence.source: the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing in the holy place
evidence.target: shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the continual sacrifice: and they shall give abomination into desolation

24:15.note: The sanctuary polluted, the continual sacrifice taken away, the abomination given into desolation: 11:31 is the form of Daniel's saying that the Machabean fulfilment (in our layer at 1 Machabees 1:57) enacted.

evidence.source: these shall go into punishment everlasting: but the just, into life everlasting
evidence.target: some unto life everlasting, & others unto reproach to see it always

25:46.note: Life everlasting against everlasting reproach: Matthew's closing sentence of the judgement is Daniel's two awakenings in the Lord's own words.

evidence.source: great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the world until now, neither shall be
evidence.target: a time shall come such as hath not been from the time since nations began even until that time

24:21.note: A tribulation such as hath not been: Daniel's time of trouble, unexampled since nations began, taken up by the Lord as the measure of the last distress.

evidence.source: they gave them into the potter's field, as our Lord did appoint to me
evidence.target: cast it forth to the statuary, a goodly price, that I was priced at by them

27:10.note: Matthew's fulfilment note: the seed carries Matthew 27:9 -> Zacharias 11:12 (the thirty pieces weighed); the disposal of the price — to the statuary/potter, in the Lord's house — is 11:13's, entered here. 'Statuary' is this corpus's word where Matthew says the potter's field.

evidence.source: he made of one, all mankind, to inhabit upon the whole face of the earth
evidence.target: of these was all mankind spread over the whole earth

17:26.note: Paul at Athens teaches Genesis 9: of Noe's three sons was all mankind spread over the whole earth.

evidence.source: every man heard them speak in his own tongue
evidence.target: let us go down, and there confound their tongue, that none may hear his neighbour's voice

2:6.note: Pentecost is Babel answered: there the tongue was confounded so that none might hear his neighbour's voice; here every man hears the great works of God in his own tongue.

evidence.source: called thither Jacob his father and all his kindred in seventy five souls
evidence.target: All the souls of the house of Jacob, that entered into Ægypt, were seventy

7:14.note: Stephen reckons the kindred at seventy-five souls, following the Greek reckoning; Genesis as here printed numbers the house that entered Egypt at seventy.

evidence.source: called thither Jacob his father and all his kindred in seventy five souls
evidence.target: all the souls that came out of Jacob's thigh were seventy

7:14.note: Stephen counts the kindred at seventy-five souls, following the Greek reckoning; Exodus counts seventy. The difference is printed openly in both texts, not smoothed over.

evidence.source: another king arose in Ægypt, that knew not Joseph
evidence.target: there arose a new king over Ægypt, that knew not Joseph

7:18.note: Stephen's history begins where Exodus begins: a new king in Egypt who did not know Joseph.

evidence.source: Pharao's daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son
evidence.target: Whom she adopted into the place of a son

7:21.note: Stephen: Pharaoh's daughter took the exposed child up and nourished him as her own son; Exodus: she adopted him into the place of a son.

evidence.source: Who hath appointed thee prince and judge over us
evidence.target: Who hath appointed thee Prince and Judge over us?

7:27.note: Stephen quotes the Hebrew workman's rebuff of Moses word for word.

evidence.source: whom they denied, saying: Who hath appointed thee prince and Captain?
evidence.target: Who hath appointed thee Prince and Judge over us?

7:35.note: Stephen re-deploys the question against his hearers: the Moses they denied with these words is the one God sent as prince and redeemer. The Acts text here prints 'Captain' where 7:27 has 'judge'.

evidence.source: Moyses fled upon this word: and he became a sojourner in the land of Madian
evidence.target: who flying from his sight, abode in the Land of Madian

7:29.note: Moses' flight from Pharaoh's sight and his sojourning in Madian, retold by Stephen.

evidence.source: Loose off the shoe of thy feet, for the place wherein thou standest, is holy ground
evidence.target: loose off thy shoe from thy feet: for the place wherein thou standest is holy ground

7:33.note: Stephen quotes the word at the bush: the shoe loosed, the ground holy.

evidence.source: I am the God of thy fathers; the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob
evidence.target: I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob

7:32.note: Stephen quotes God's self-naming at the bush, 'thy fathers' for Exodus' 'thy father'.

evidence.source: Seeing I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Ægypt, and I have heard their groaning
evidence.target: I have seen the affliction of my people in Ægypt, and I have heard their cry

7:34.note: Stephen quotes the opening of the call: God has seen the affliction and heard the cry (his 'descended to deliver' is 3:8).

evidence.source: And now come, and I will send thee into Ægypt
evidence.target: come, and I will send thee to Pharao

7:34.note: The same verse of Stephen quotes the commission itself: 'come, and I will send thee' — in Exodus, to Pharaoh; in Stephen's retelling, into Egypt.

evidence.source: in a mighty arm brought them out thereof
evidence.target: redeem you in a high arm, and great judgments

13:17.note: Paul at Antioch: God brought Israel out 'in a mighty arm' — Exodus' own word for the redemption, 'in a high arm, and great judgments'.

evidence.source: they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice to the idol
evidence.target: made of them a molten calf. And they said: These are thy gods Israel

7:41.note: Stephen's indictment: in those days they made the calf and offered sacrifice to the idol, as Exodus tells it.

evidence.source: for I did never eat any common and unclean thing
evidence.target: that you may know the differences of the clean, and the unclean, and know what you ought to eat, and what to refuse

evidence.source: That you abstain from the things immolated to idols, and blood, and that which is strangled
evidence.target: Any man whosoever of the house of Israel, and of the strangers, that sojourn among them, if he eat blood, I will set my face against his life

evidence.source: a certain wench having a Pythonical spirit, met us, that brought great gain to her masters by divining

evidence.source: whereas now it was not safe sailing, because the fast now was past
evidence.target: upon the tenth day of this seventh month shall be the day of expiations most solemn

evidence.source: And when the days of Pentecost were accomplished, they were all together in one place
evidence.target: unto the morrow after the seventh week be expired, that is to say fifty days, and so you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord

2:1.note: Pentecost is Leviticus' fiftieth day, counted out from the firstfruits sheaf. The Spirit falls on the feast's own day — the church is gathered at the hour the law's count appointed.

evidence.source: A Prophet will God raise up to you of your own brethren as myself: him you shall hear.
evidence.target: A prophet of thy nation & of thy brethren like unto me, will our Lord thy God raise up to thee: him thou shalt hear,

7:37.note: Stephen quotes Moses' promise nearly word for word. The seed carries this verse of Acts only at chapter level (Deuteronomy 18); the verse anchor is entered here. Peter's quotation of the same promise (Acts 3:22) is the seed's at verse level.

evidence.source: In very deed I perceive that God is not an accepter of persons.
evidence.target: that accepteth not person nor gifts.

10:34.note: Peter's discovery at Cesarea is Moses' confession: the God of gods accepts no person's face. The seed carries the same verse for Romans 2:11, Galatians 2:6, Colossians 3:25 and Ephesians 6:9; Peter's preaching of it was unkeyed.

evidence.source: by lot he divided their land among them,
evidence.target: dividing all things by lot, as our Lord had commanded in the hand of Moyses, to the nine tribes, and the half tribe.

evidence.source: I have found David the son of Jesse, a man according to my heart, who shall do all my wills.
evidence.target: Our Lord hath sought him a man according to his heart: and him hath our Lord commanded to be Prince over his people,

evidence.source: And all the Prophets from Samuel and afterward that have spoken, told of these days.
evidence.target: that faithful Samuel was the Prophet of our Lord.

evidence.source: he gave them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, forty years.
evidence.target: And he had a son called Saul, chosen and good: and there was not a man of the children of Israel better than he

evidence.source: But the Highest dwelleth not in houses made by hand
evidence.target: if heaven, and the heavens of heavens cannot contain thee, how much more this house, which I have built?

evidence.target: And he died in a good old age, full of days, and riches, & glory. And Salomon his son reigned for him.

evidence.source: thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, nor give thy Holy one to see corruption.
evidence.target: thou wilt not leave my soul in hell: neither wilt give thy holy one to see corruption

2:27.note: Peter's Pentecost citation at its first member; Acts 13:35 to this verse is the seed's, this source verse is not.

evidence.source: Thou hast made known to me the ways of life: thou shalt make me full of joyfulness with thy face.
evidence.target: Thou hast made the ways of life known to me, thou shalt make me full of joy with thy countenance

evidence.source: the kings of the earth stand up, and the Princes assemble together against our Lord, and against his Christ?
evidence.target: The kings of the earth stood up, and the Princes came together in one against our Lord, and against his Christ.

evidence.source: the heart of this people is waxen gross, and with their ears have they heavily heard, and their eyes they have shut
evidence.target: shut their eyes: lest perhaps they may see with their eyes, and hear with their ears

evidence.source: In humility his judgement was taken away. His generation who shall declare
evidence.target: from distress and from judgement he was taken up: who shall declare his generation?

evidence.source: Hath not my hand made all these things?
evidence.target: My hand hath made all these things

7:50.note: Stephen's citation, second half. The seed keys Acts 7:49 to 66:1 (heaven my throne); the rhetorical question that follows is 66:2's opening.

evidence.source: I am clear from the blood of all
evidence.target: his blood I will require at thy hand

evidence.source: Behold I see the Heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God
evidence.target: with the clouds of heaven there came in, as it were the son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days

evidence.source: upon my servants truly, and upon my handmaids will I pour out in those days, of my Spirit
evidence.target: upon my servants, and handmaids in those days I will pour out my spirit

2:18.note: Peter's Pentecost quotation of Joel, verse by verse. The seed carries only Acts 2:17 -> Joel 2:28 at verse level; the servants-and-handmaids verse is entered here.

evidence.source: I will give wonders in the Heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath, blood and fire, and vapour of smoke
evidence.target: I will give wonders in heaven, and in earth, blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke

2:19.note: The wonders verse of the same Pentecost quotation; uncarried at verse level before this draft.

evidence.source: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood
evidence.target: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood

2:20.note: Near-verbatim in this corpus; Joel calls the day 'horrible', Acts 'manifest' — the divergence is in the verses' tails, not in the quoted signs.

evidence.source: every one whosoever calleth upon the name of our Lord, shall be saved
evidence.target: every one that shall invocate the name of the Lord, shall be saved

evidence.target: you carried a tabernacle for your Moloch, and the image of your idols, the star of your god

evidence.source: he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people

The shared wording is the wine-and-sicer abstinence.

evidence.source: The hungry he hath filled with good things:
evidence.target: the hungry soul he hath filled with good things.

1:53.note: The Magnificat's filled-hungry line; Psalm 106 is the psalter's great thanksgiving for exactly such reversals.

evidence.source: our Lord God shall give him the seat of David his father:

evidence.source: hath erected the horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant.
evidence.target: Thither will I bring forth a horn to David,

evidence.source: when the Heaven was shut three years and six months
evidence.target: if there shall be these years dew and rain, but according to the words of my mouth.

evidence.source: Lord wilt thou we say that fire come down from Heaven and consume them?

evidence.source: he shall go before him in the spirit and virtue of Elias
evidence.target: The spirit of Elias hath rested upon Eliseus.

evidence.source: that he may convert the hearts of the fathers unto the children

evidence.source: in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest perhaps thou knock thy foot against a stone.
evidence.target: In their hands they shall bear thee: lest perhaps thou knock thy foot against a stone.

4:11.note: The second half of Satan's Psalm 90 citation in Luke; the seed carries Luke 4:10 to 90:11 and Matthew 4:6 to this verse.

evidence.source: Blessed is he that cometh King in the name of our Lord
evidence.target: Blessed be he that cometh in the name of our Lord.

19:38.note: The entry into Jerusalem in Luke. This corpus prints the Blessed-is-he at 117:25, not 26; the seed keys this verse of the psalm only from chapter-level Gospel sources.

evidence.source: his mercy from generation unto generations, to them that fear him.
evidence.target: the mercy of our Lord from everlasting, and unto everlasting upon them that fear him.

evidence.source: Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us:

evidence.source: To illuminate them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death:
evidence.target: Them that sat in darkness, and in the shadow of death:

evidence.source: Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years, take thy rest, eat, drink, make good cheer.

evidence.source: to preach the acceptable year of the Lord

evidence.source: to dismiss the bruised unto remission

evidence.source: I am Gabriel that assist before God
evidence.target: Gabriel make this man understand the vision

1:19.note: Gabriel is named in Scripture only in Daniel and in Luke: the voice between Ulai's banks commissions him to make Daniel understand the vision, and he stands before God announcing to Zacharias and to Mary. Graded parallel: a person, not a phrase, is what is shared.

evidence.source: to whom thou swarest by thine own self, saying: I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven
evidence.target: I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand that is by the sea shore

32:13.note: Moses intercedes by pleading the sworn promise back to God: the stars of heaven, in the oath's own words.

evidence.source: Our Lord make this woman, which entereth into thy house, as Rachel, and Lia, which builded the house of Israel
evidence.target: opened her womb, her sister remaining barren

4:11.note: Bethlehem's elders bless Ruth in the names of Rachel and Lia, the two mothers who builded the house of Israel out of barren and opened wombs.

evidence.source: thy house may be, as the house of Phares, whom Thamar bare to Judas
evidence.target: for this cause called his name Phares

4:12.note: The blessing on Booz's house names its own ancestor: Phares, whom Thamar bare to Judas, named for the breach at his birth.

evidence.source: that I may raise up the name of the deceased in his inheritance, lest his name be abolished out of his family and brethren and people.
evidence.target: But his brother shall take her, & raise up the seed of his brother:

4:10.note: Booz takes Ruth 'to raise up the name of the deceased' — the end Deuteronomy's levirate law exists for. Graded parallel, honestly: Booz is a kinsman redeeming, not the brother the law names, and the sandal of 25:7–9 is drawn off in the gate (Ruth 4:7–8) without the widow's spitting.

evidence.source: all the people that dwelleth within the gates of my city know, that thou art a woman of virtue.
evidence.target: A valiant woman who shall find?

3:11.note: Booz confesses before all the gates what the acrostic asks: a valiant woman — who shall find? Ruth is the portrait's living instance, her works praising her in the same gates (31:31). Graded parallel: the DR wording differs ('woman of virtue' against 'valiant woman'), and no quotation is claimed.

evidence.source: He turned their heart that they hated his people: and to work guile toward his servants
evidence.target: Come, let us wisely oppress the same, lest perhaps it multiply

104:25.note: The psalm reads Egypt's oppression as God's turning of their heart; its 'work guile' answers the king's 'let us wisely oppress' — the same craft, seen from heaven's side.

evidence.source: he brought them forth with gold and silver
evidence.target: they asked of the Ægyptians vessels of silver and gold

104:37.note: The psalm's Exodus litany: God brought Israel forth laden with the silver and gold they had asked of the Egyptians.

evidence.source: they believed his words: and they sang his praises
evidence.target: the people feared our Lord, and they believed our Lord, and Moyses his servant

105:12.note: The psalm compresses the shore of the sea into one line: they believed — as Exodus says, 'the people feared our Lord, and they believed' — and then they sang.

evidence.source: Our Lord is my strength, and my praise: and he is made my salvation
evidence.target: My strength, and my praise is our Lord, and he is made unto me a salvation

117:14.note: The Hallel psalm takes the song of Moses for its own line, word for word with only the order turned.

evidence.source: The right hand of our Lord hath wrought strength
evidence.target: Thy right hand, o Lord, is magnified in strength

117:16.note: The same psalm's triple 'the right hand of our Lord' answers the song's 'Thy right hand, o Lord, is magnified in strength'.

evidence.source: he brought them into the mount of his sanctification
evidence.target: bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thy inheritance, in thy most firm habitation, which thou hast wrought, o Lord: thy sanctuary Lord, which thy hands have confirmed

77:54.note: The psalm's history ends where the song pointed: God bringing his people in and planting them in the mountain of his sanctuary.

evidence.source: And he rained them Manna to eat, and bread of heaven he gave to them
evidence.target: Behold I will rain you bread from heaven

77:24.note: The psalm takes God's verb for its own: as God said 'I will rain you bread from heaven', so 'he rained them manna to eat'.

evidence.source: As in the provocation according to the day of the tentation in the desert: where your fathers tempted me
evidence.target: he called the name of that place, Temptation, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and for that they tempted our Lord, saying: Is the Lord among us or not?

94:9.note: The psalm's 'day of temptation in the desert' is the place Exodus itself names Temptation — Massa — where Israel said, 'Is the Lord among us or not?'

evidence.source: they made a calf in Horeb: and they adored the sculptile
evidence.target: he formed them by founder's work, and made of them a molten calf

105:19.note: The psalm of Israel's rebellions: 'they made a calf in Horeb, and they adored the sculptile' — Aaron's molten calf of Exodus 32.

evidence.source: Our Lord is pitiful, and merciful: long suffering, and very merciful
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

102:8.note: The psalm of thanksgiving opens its praise with the Sinai formula: 'Our Lord is pitiful and merciful, long suffering and very merciful'.

evidence.source: That hath not given his money to usury, and hath not taken gifts upon the innocent
evidence.target: Thou shalt not give him thy money to usury, and an overplus of the fruits thou shalt not exact of him

14:5.note: The entrance psalm's righteous man is drawn with Leviticus' usury clause — he 'hath not given his money to usury' to his brother. (Psalm 14 in the Vulgate numbering this corpus uses; 15 in modern Bibles.)

evidence.source: Sound ye with trumpet in the new moon, in the notable day of your solemnity.
evidence.target: The seventh month, on the first day of the month, shall be a Sabbath, a memorial, by sounding of trumpets

80:4.note: The psalm summons the trumpet for the appointed solemnity at the new moon — the memorial of blowing trumpets on the first day of the seventh month, which opens the autumn feasts of Leviticus 23.

evidence.source: And these have not known my ways: as I sware in my wrath: if they shall enter into my rest
evidence.target: they shall not see the Land for the which I sware to their fathers, neither shall any of them that hath detracted me, behold it

94:11.note: The oath the psalm sings — the text Hebrews 3-4 preaches — was sworn here, at Cades, against the generation of the spies: they shall not see the land.

evidence.source: And they coveted concupiscence in the desert: and tempted God in the place without water
evidence.target: For the common vulgar people that came up with them, burned with desire, sitting and weeping, the children of Israel being joined together with them

105:14.note: The psalm's 'concupiscence in the desert' is this burning desire for flesh — the craving that named the place itself, the Sepulchres of concupiscence (11:34). Paul's 'as they also coveted' is seed-carried at this verse.

evidence.source: And he rained upon them flesh as dust: and as the sand of the sea feathered fowls
evidence.target: And a wind coming forth from our Lord, taking quails over the sea brought them, and let them fall into the camp the space of one day's journey

77:27.note: The psalm's rain of flesh is this wind from the Lord, driving the quails in over the sea to fall around the camp. Wisdom's retelling of the quails is already keyed to this verse in our layer.

evidence.source: They were not defrauded of their desire. As yet their meats were in their mouth
evidence.target: As yet the flesh was in their teeth, neither had that kind of meat failed: & behold the fury of our Lord being provoked against the people, struck them with an exceeding great plague

77:30.note: Meats in the mouth, flesh in the teeth, and the blow falling while they ate — the psalm keeps Numbers' very image of the plague at the Sepulchres of concupiscence.

evidence.source: The earth was opened, and swallowed Dathan, and overwhelmed the congregation of Abiron
evidence.target: and opening her mouth, devoured them with their tabernacles & all their substance

105:17.note: The psalm's history names what this verse records: Dathan swallowed, Abiron's congregation overwhelmed, in the one opening of the earth.

evidence.source: And a fire flamed up in their synagogue: the flame burnt the sinners
evidence.target: But a fire also coming forth from our Lord, slew the two hundred fifty men, that offered the incense

105:18.note: The fire that flamed in their synagogue is the fire that took the two hundred fifty censer-bearers. Sirach's praise of Aaron reaches the same verse from the other side in our layer.

evidence.source: And they provoked him at the waters of contradiction: and Moyses was vexed for them
evidence.target: This is the water of contradiction, where the children of Israel quarrelled against our Lord, and he was sanctified in them

105:32.note: The psalm calls the place by the very name this verse gives it — the water of contradiction at Cades.

evidence.source: because they exasperated his spirit. And he plainly affirmed in his lips
evidence.target: Hear ye rebellious & incredulous: Can we out of this rock bring you forth water?

105:33.note: The psalm's diagnosis — a spirit exasperated, a rash word on the lips — is this cry before the rock, the word for which Moses lost the land he was not to enter.

evidence.source: God have mercy upon us, and bless us: illuminate his countenance upon us, and have mercy on us
evidence.target: Our Lord shew his face to thee, and have mercy upon thee

66:2.note: The psalm prays Aaron's blessing back upon the whole congregation — bless us, shew thy face on us, have mercy — in the blessing's own words and order.

evidence.source: The light of thy countenance, o Lord is signed upon us: thou hast given gladness in my heart
evidence.target: Our Lord turn his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace

4:7.note: The countenance lifted and turned upon the blessed one, and its fruit in the heart — gladness answering to the blessing's peace.

evidence.source: Let God arise, and let his enemies be dispersed, and let them that hate him fly from his face
evidence.target: Arise Lord, and be thine enemies dispersed, and let them fly that hate thee, from thy face

67:2.note: The psalm opens with Moses' cry at the rising of the ark, transposed into the third person for the liturgy — enemies dispersed, haters fled from his face — but the words are the ark's own.

evidence.source: Sehon the king of the Amorrheites: because his mercy is for ever
evidence.target: Of whom he was strucken in the edge of the sword, and his land was possessed from Arnon unto Jeboc

135:19.note: The litany's first conquered king is Sehon, struck in the edge of the sword at Jasa and possessed from Arnon to Jeboc. The seed points the sister psalm (134:11) at this chapter only.

evidence.source: And Og the king of Basan: because his mercy is for ever
evidence.target: Fear him not, for into thy hand I have delivered him, and all his people, and land: and thou shalt do to him as thou didst to Sehon the king of the Amorrheites, the inhabiter of Hesebon

135:20.note: The litany's second king is Og of Basan, delivered into Israel's hand by this word — do to him as thou didst to Sehon.

evidence.source: And Phinees stood, and pacified: and the slaughter ceased
evidence.target: And the plague ceased from the children of Israel

105:30.note: Phinees standing, and the plague ceasing — the psalm compresses the deed at the brothel house into its one effect, and the next verse reckons it to him for justice.

evidence.source: And it was reputed to him unto justice, in generation and generation even for ever
evidence.target: and there shall be as well to him as to his seed the covenant of priesthood for ever, because he hath been zealous for his God, and hath expiated the wicked fact of the children of Israel

105:31.note: The psalm reckons Phinees' zeal with Abraham's own reckoning word — reputed unto justice — and its 'for ever' is this covenant's: an everlasting priesthood to him and to his seed. Sirach's praise of Phinees is keyed to the same verse in our layer.

evidence.source: And they immolated their sons, and their daughters to devils.
evidence.target: They immolated to devils and not to God

105:37.note: The psalm's horrified summary of the Canaan years keeps the song's phrase: immolated — to devils. What Moses sang of strange gods, the psalm finds done with Israel's own children.

evidence.source: Because our Lord shall judge his people: and will be entreated toward his servants.
evidence.target: Our Lord will judge his people, and will have mercy on his servants

134:14.note: The psalm of the Exodus liturgy closes its history with the song's promise almost verbatim: the Lord will judge his people, and have mercy on his servants.

evidence.source: keep me, as the apple of the eye.
evidence.target: he led him about, and taught him: and kept him as the apple of his eye.

16:8.note: David asks for himself the keeping Israel received in the wilderness: kept as the apple of God's eye. The figure is the song's before it is the psalm's.

evidence.source: The chariot of God is ten thousand fold, thousands of them that rejoice, our Lord in them, in Sina in the holy place.
evidence.target: and with him thousands of Saints.

67:18.note: The processional psalm's Sinai theophany keeps Moses' numbers: Sinai, and the thousands with him. Galatians' 'ordained by angels' (3:19) stands in the same tradition but shares no wording beyond the angels, and is set aside; this verse carries the theophany.

evidence.source: the father of orphans, and judge of widows. God in his holy place:
evidence.target: He doth judgment to the pupil and the widow, loveth the stranger

67:6.note: The processional psalm names God by Deuteronomy's works: judgment done to the pupil and the widow — orphans' father, widows' judge.

evidence.source: The sea saw, and fled: Jordan was turned backward.
evidence.target: the waters that came downward stood in one place, and like a mountain swelling up appeared far from the city, that is called Adom, to the place of Sarthan

113:3.note: The psalm pairs the sea's flight (Exodus) with Jordan turned backward; the turning is Josue's crossing, where the downward waters stood in one place like a mountain. The seed carries this psalm verse only at chapter level for Josue (Josue 3); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: Put their Princes as Oreb, and Zeb,
evidence.target: And two men that were apprehended of Madian, Oreb and Zeb, Oreb he slew in the Rock of Oreb, Zeb in the press of Zeb.

82:12.note: The psalm prays that the enemy princes be made as Oreb and Zeb, Madian's princes taken in Gedeon's pursuit and slain at the places that took their names. The prayer's second pair, Zebee and Salmana, is keyed beside this at Judges 8:21.

evidence.source: and Zebee, and Salmana. All their Princes:
evidence.target: Gedeon rose up, and slew Zebee and Salmana

82:12.note: The same psalm verse names Madian's kings as well as its princes: Zebee and Salmana, whom Gedeon himself slew after Succoth and Phanuel refused him. Keyed separately from the Oreb-and-Zeb half of the verse because the deaths stand in different chapters.

evidence.source: and Samuel among them that invocate his name: They invocated our Lord and he heard them:
evidence.target: and Samuel cried to our Lord for Israel, & our Lord heard him.

98:6.note: The psalm enrols Samuel with Moses and Aaron among those who called on the Lord and were heard. The hearing it presupposes is this one: Samuel cried to the Lord for Israel at Masphath, and the Lord heard him, before the thunder of 7:10.

evidence.source: his seed shall continue for ever.
evidence.target: And thy house shall be faithful, and thy Kingdom for ever before thy face, and thy throne shall be firm continually.

88:37.note: The covenant psalm swears David's oath back to God: his seed shall continue for ever, his throne as the sun (88:38). The oath it swears is Nathan's closing sentence, kingdom for ever and throne firm continually.

evidence.source: who spake to our Lord the words of this canticle, in the day, that our Lord delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul, and he said:
evidence.target: And David spake to our Lord the words of this song, in the day that our Lord delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul.

17:1.note: Psalm 17 is David's song of deliverance — the same song 2 Kings 22 preserves in the history, under a heading the two books share nearly word for word. The song is keyed once more inside, at its theophany (17:8 to 22:8).

evidence.source: The earth was shaken & trembled: the foundations of mountains were troubled, and were moved, because he was wrath with them.
evidence.target: The earth quaked and trembled, the foundations of the mountains were strucken, and shaken, because he was angry with them.

17:8.note: Inside the shared song, the theophany verse in both tellings: earth trembling, mountains' foundations shaken, because he was angry. The wording differs in small words between psalter and history, as copied songs do; the verse is the same verse.

evidence.source: The Psalm of David, when he fled from the face of Absalom his son.
evidence.target: Arise let us fly: for there will be no escape for us from the face of Absalom

3:1.note: The psalm's own heading sets it in Absalom's revolt: David fleeing from the face of Absalom his son. The flight the heading names is this verse, David rising to fly from Jerusalem before Absalom's face. In this corpus the heading stands as the psalm's first verse.

evidence.source: when Nathan the Prophet came to him, after that he had sinned with Bethsabee.
evidence.target: Our Lord therefore sent Nathan to David:

50:2.note: The Miserere's heading, the psalm's second verse in this corpus, dates it to Nathan's coming after David's sin with Bethsabee. The coming it names is this verse: the Lord sent Nathan to David, and the parable of the ewe lamb followed. The seed carries Psalms 50 toward 2 Kings 12 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: he struck the rock and waters ran, & torrents flowed:
evidence.target: thou shalt strike the rock, & water shall go out thereof, that the people may drink.

77:20.note: The historical psalm retells the struck rock of Horeb. Earlier stages keyed this psalm's manna and quails; the rock verses were left unkeyed.

evidence.source: he turned their rivers into blood, & their showers that they might not drink.
evidence.target: he struck the water of the river before Pharao and his servants: which was turned into blood.

77:44.note: Psalm 77's plague recital, first plague: the rivers into blood.

evidence.source: He sent upon them a swarm of flies, and it eat them: and the frog, and it destroyed them.
evidence.target: there came a very grievous fly into the houses of Pharao & of his servants, & into all the Land of Ægypt:

77:45.note: The psalm gathers the fly and the frog plagues into one verse; this entry anchors the fly, Exodus 8's frog stands at 8:6.

evidence.source: he killed their vineyards with hail:
evidence.target: the hail smote in all the Land of Ægypt all things that were in the fields,

77:47.note: The hail plague in the psalm's recital.

evidence.source: he struck all the first-born in the land of Ægypt: the first fruits of all their labours
evidence.target: our Lord struck every first-begotten in the Land of Ægypt,

77:51.note: The last plague in the psalm's recital: the firstborn struck at midnight.

evidence.source: Israel entered into Ægypt, and Jacob was a sojourner in the land of Cham.
evidence.target: he came into Ægypt with all his seed,

104:23.note: Psalm 104's covenant recital reaches Jacob's descent into Egypt; Genesis 46:27 to this psalm is keyed in the Genesis stage from the other side of the recital.

evidence.source: He sent darkness, and obscured:
evidence.target: there was made horrible darkness in the whole Land of Ægypt three days.

104:28.note: Psalm 104's plague recital opens, in its own order, with the darkness.

evidence.source: He turned their waters into blood: and killed their fishes.
evidence.target: he struck the water of the river before Pharao and his servants: which was turned into blood.

104:29.note: The waters into blood in Psalm 104's recital; Psalm 77's telling of the same plague is entered separately above.

evidence.source: Their land brought forth frogs in the inner chambers of their kings.
evidence.target: the frogs came up, and covered the Land of Ægypt.

104:30.note: The frogs in Psalm 104's recital, into the kings' own chambers.

evidence.source: the cænomyia came: and the sciniphs in all their coasts.
evidence.target: there were made sciniphs on men and on beasts:

104:31.note: The sciniphs are named with the same rare word in the psalm and in Exodus.

evidence.source: He made their rains hail: fire burning in their land.
evidence.target: our Lord gave thunders, and hail, and running lightnings on the land:

104:32.note: The hail and fire of Psalm 104's recital.

evidence.source: He said, & the locust came, & the bruchus whereof there was no number.
evidence.target: the burning wind raised the locusts:

104:34.note: The locusts in Psalm 104's recital, without number.

evidence.source: he struck every first begotten in their land: the first fruits of all their labour.
evidence.target: our Lord struck every first-begotten in the Land of Ægypt,

104:36.note: The firstborn in Psalm 104's recital, closing its plagues as Exodus closes its own.

evidence.source: he rebuked the Red sea, and it was made dry: and he led them in the depths as in a desert.
evidence.target: turned it into dry ground: and the water was divided.

105:9.note: Psalm 105's confession opens its history with the sea rebuked and made dry.

evidence.source: water overwhelmed those that afflicted them: there did not one of them remain.
evidence.target: the waters returned, and overwhelmed the chariots & the horsemen of all Pharao's army,

105:11.note: Not one of them remain, in the psalm and in Exodus alike.

evidence.source: Who struck Ægypt with their first-begotten: because his mercy is for ever.
evidence.target: our Lord struck every first-begotten in the Land of Ægypt,

135:10.note: The litany psalm's first Exodus item; the seed keys Exodus 11 to this psalm at chapter level only.

evidence.source: Who divided the Red sea into divisions: because his mercy is for ever.
evidence.target: turned it into dry ground: and the water was divided.

135:13.note: The divided sea in the litany psalm, under its mercy-for-ever refrain.

evidence.source: I will put his seed for ever and ever: and his throne as the days of heaven.
evidence.target: thy Kingdom for ever before thy face, and thy throne shall be firm continually.

88:30.note: Psalm 88 sings Nathan's oracle back to God: seed and throne for ever. The oracle's own verses are the target; Acts 13:22 to this psalm is the seed's.

evidence.source: Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy seat.
evidence.target: I will raise up thy seed after thee, which shall come forth of thy womb, and I will establish his Kingdom.

131:11.note: The sworn fruit-of-thy-womb of the psalm is Nathan's seed raised up after David. Later verses citing the psalm (Acts 2:30, John 7:42's context) are keyed elsewhere; this entry anchors the psalm to its own source.

evidence.source: Therefore will I confess to thee among nations, o Lord: and will say a Psalm to thy name.
evidence.target: Therefore will I confess unto thee, o Lord, among the Gentiles, and will sing to thy name.

17:50.note: The same song in both books. Paul's use of this verse (Romans 15:9) is the seed's; the Samuel copy was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Magnifying the salvations of his king, and doing mercy to his Christ David, and to his seed for ever.
evidence.target: Magnifying the salvations of his king, and doing mercy to his Christ David, and to his seed for ever.

17:51.note: The song's last verse, word for word in both books.

evidence.source: when he changed his countenance before Abimelech, and he dismist him, and he went away
evidence.target: he changed his countenance before them, and slipt down between their hands:

33:1.note: The psalm's title names David feigning madness. Stated openly: the title says Abimelech, while the king in 1 Kings 21 is Achis of Geth; the episode is one and the same, the name difference is the texts' own.

evidence.source: when he fled from the face of Saul into the cave.
evidence.target: there was a cave, which Saul entered into, to do his easement: moreover David and his men lay hid in the inner part of the cave.

56:1.note: The cave psalm's title and the cave at 1 Kings 24. The seed keys 1 Kings 24 to this psalm at chapter level; the title's own verse is entered here.

evidence.source: when he was in the desert of Juda.
evidence.target: David abode in the desert in most strong places, & he tarried in the mount of the desert Ziph,

62:1.note: The desert psalm's title and David in the desert of Ziph, in Juda, while Saul sought him.

evidence.source: Who shall ascend into the mount of our Lord? Or who shall stand in his holy place?
evidence.target: Lord who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? Or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

23:3.note: Two entrance liturgies asking the same question at the sanctuary door; Psalm 23's answer (clean hands, pure heart) follows in its next verse as Psalm 14's follows in its own.

evidence.source: God hath looked forth from heaven, upon the children of men: to see if there be that understandeth, or seeketh after God.
evidence.target: Our Lord hath looked forth from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there be that understandeth, and seeketh after God.

52:3.note: Psalm 52 is Psalm 13 sung again with God's name in place of the Lord's; the seed keys the two psalms only at 13:1 to the whole of 52.

evidence.source: O God intend unto my help: Lord make haste to help me.
evidence.target: It may please thee, o Lord, to deliver me: Lord have respect to help me.

69:2.note: Psalm 69 is the closing cry of Psalm 39 lifted out and sung on its own; the seed keys the two psalms only at chapter level (39 to 69:3).

evidence.source: Let all that seek thee rejoice, and be glad in thee, and let them say always: Our Lord be magnified:
evidence.target: Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad upon thee: and let them that love thy salvation, say always: Our Lord be magnified:

69:5.note: The lifted-out ending keeps Psalm 39's rejoicing verse almost word for word.

evidence.source: Confess ye to our Lord because he is good: because his mercy is for ever.
evidence.target: Confess ye to our Lord because he is good: because his mercy is for ever.
