135:1.note: The litany psalm opens with the festal psalm's opening line, which becomes its own refrain; the seed keys 117:1 to Psalm 135 only at chapter level (in reverse).

evidence.source: he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.
evidence.target: He conceived sorrow, and hath brought forth iniquity

7:15.note: The psalm sings Eliphaz's sentence almost in his words. The seed keys the psalm's preceding verse (7:14 in this corpus) to Job 15 at chapter level; the conceiving line itself stands at 7:15 here.

evidence.source: Lo the sinners themselves, and they that abound in the world, have obtained riches.
evidence.target: Why then do the impious live, are they advanced, & strengthened with riches?

72:12.note: Asaph's psalm is built on Job's question: sinners abounding in the world and obtaining riches is the spectacle that nearly made his feet slip (72:2-3).

evidence.source: Who giveth to beasts their food: and to the young ravens that call upon him.
evidence.target: Who prepareth for the raven her meat, when her young ones cry to God

146:9.note: The psalm answers the whirlwind's question with praise: the God who asked who prepares the raven's meat is confessed as the one who feeds the young ravens that call upon him.

evidence.source: Thou hast set a bound, which they shall not pass over
evidence.target: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt not proceed farther, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves.

103:9.note: The creation psalm confesses as praise what the whirlwind declares as command: a bound set for the sea — hitherto shalt thou come, and no farther.

evidence.source: Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, o Lord, and shalt teach out of thy law.
evidence.target: Blessed is the man that is corrected of God: refuse not therefore the chastising of our Lord

93:12.note: Eliphaz's beatitude — blessed the man corrected of God — becomes the psalm's blessed man instructed and taught out of the law. James 1:10 is keyed to this verse of Job by the seed's margin on other grounds; the psalm's taking of the beatitude was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Words of our Lord be chaste words: silver examined by fire, tried from the earth, purged seven fold.
evidence.target: Every word of God tried by fire, is a buckler to them that hope in him

11:7.note: Agur's confession — every word of God tried by fire — is the psalm's silver examined by fire and purged sevenfold, carried from the psalmist's trouble into the proverb. The seed carries the psalm only at chapter level (Proverbs 30).

evidence.source: The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak judgment.
evidence.target: She hath opened her mouth to wisdom, and the law of clemency is in her tongue.

36:30.note: The valiant woman's portrait closes the Proverbs with the psalm's just man in feminine form: a mouth opened to wisdom, a tongue carrying the law of clemency where the psalm's tongue speaks judgment. The seed carries the psalm only at chapter level (Proverbs 31).

evidence.source: he was compared to beasts without understanding, and became like to them.
evidence.target: there is one death of man, and beasts, and the condition of both equal: as man dieth, so they also die

48:13.note: The wisdom psalm's refrain — man in honour compared to beasts and become like them — is the Preacher's sentence in brief: one death of man and beasts, and the condition of both equal.

evidence.source: brought out of the iron furnace of Ægypt
evidence.target: the hard works of clay and brick

4:20.note: Deuteronomy's 'iron furnace of Egypt' is the brick-kiln bondage of Exodus 1 named in a single image.

evidence.source: The blessing of him, that appeared in the bush
evidence.target: appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush

33:16.note: In Moses' blessing of Joseph, God is named simply as him 'that appeared in the bush' — the theophany of Exodus 3 become one of his titles.

evidence.source: thou shalt bind them as a sign on thy hand, and they shall be and shall move between thine eyes
evidence.target: it shall be as a sign in thy hand, and as a monument before thine eyes

6:8.note: The sign upon the hand and the monument before the eyes were first appointed for the memorial of the Exodus; Deuteronomy binds the words of the Law itself with the same sign.

evidence.source: and fed thee with Manna in the wilderness, which thy fathers knew not
evidence.target: Man-hu! Which signifieth: What is this! For they knew not what it was

8:16.note: Deuteronomy's recital: God fed Israel 'with manna, which thy fathers knew not' — Exodus records the not-knowing itself: 'Man-hu — what is this? for they knew not what it was'.

evidence.source: who brought forth rivers out of the hardest rock
evidence.target: thou shalt strike the rock, & water shall go out thereof

8:15.note: Deuteronomy's recital of the wilderness: God 'brought forth rivers out of the hardest rock' — the rock of Horeb, struck at God's command.

evidence.source: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God, as thou didst tempt him in the place of tentation
evidence.target: he called the name of that place, Temptation

6:16.note: 'Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God, as thou didst tempt him in the place of temptation' — Deuteronomy turns the named place of Exodus 17 into a standing commandment.

evidence.source: thou shalt destroy his name under heaven
evidence.target: I will destroy the memory of Amalec from under heaven

25:19.note: The blot-out command is repeated at the end of the Law in nearly Exodus' words: what God swore at Rephidim, Israel is charged to perform in the land.

evidence.source: Give from among you wise and skillful men, and such whose conversation is approved in your tribes, that I may appoint them your princes
evidence.target: provide out of all the people men that are wise, & do fear God, in whom there is truth, and that do hate avarice, and appoint of them tribunes, and centurions

1:13.note: Moses' own retelling of the appointment of rulers: the wise men of Jethro's counsel become, in Deuteronomy, the heads chosen from the tribes.

evidence.source: hath he spread his wings, and he hath taken him, and carried him on his shoulders
evidence.target: I have carried you upon the wings of eagles

32:11.note: The Song of Moses takes up God's Sinai word and makes it a picture: as the eagle carries her young, 'I have carried you upon the wings of eagles'.

evidence.source: I the Lord thy God, that brought thee out of the Land of Ægypt out of the house of servitude
evidence.target: which brought thee forth out of the Land of Ægypt, out of the house of servitude

5:6.note: Deuteronomy 5 repeats the Decalogue of Exodus 20 entire, on the plains of Moab a generation later; the preface stands word for word at the head of both givings.

evidence.source: as thou didst request of our Lord thy God in Horeb, when the assembly was gathered, and saidst: I will no more hear the voice of our Lord my God, and this exceeding great fire I will see no more, lest I die
evidence.target: let not our Lord Speak to us, lest perhaps we die

18:16.note: The promise of the prophet is grounded in Israel's plea at Horeb: 'let not our Lord speak to us, lest perhaps we die' — Deuteronomy quotes the plea back as the reason God will speak through a mediator.

evidence.source: And do you therefore love strangers because you also were strangers in the Land of Ægypt
evidence.target: for you know the hearts of strangers: because yourselves also were strangers in the Land of Ægypt

10:19.note: The motive is Exodus' own, repeated verbatim: love the stranger, 'because yourselves also were strangers in the land of Egypt'.

evidence.source: two tables of stone written with the finger of God
evidence.target: two stone tables of testimony, written with the finger of God

9:10.note: Moses' retelling keeps the phrase entire: the tables were 'written with the finger of God' (the gift itself is Exodus 31:18; Exodus 32:16 says the same of the first tables).

evidence.source: I cast the tables out of my hands, and brake them in your sight
evidence.target: he threw the tables out of his hand, and brake them at the foot of the mount

9:17.note: Moses' own retelling of the breaking of the tables at the foot of the mount.

evidence.source: your sin that you had committed, that is, the calf, I took, and burnt it with fire, and breaking it into pieces, and bringing it wholly into dust, I threw it into the torrent
evidence.target: he burnt it, & beat it into powder, which he strawed into water, and gave thereof drink to the children of Israel

9:21.note: The calf's destruction retold by Moses: burnt, ground to powder, and strawed on water — in Exodus, water the children of Israel were made to drink.

evidence.source: He that said to his father and to his mother: I know you not; and to his brethren: I know you not
evidence.target: every man kill his brother, and friend, and neighbour

33:9.note: Levi's blessing is the wage of the calf: the Levites who, at Moses' word, knew neither brother nor friend nor neighbour are blessed as the tribe that 'said to his father and mother, I know you not'.

evidence.source: there rose no more a Prophet in Israel as Moyses, whom our Lord had known face to face
evidence.target: spake unto Moyses face to face

34:10.note: The epitaph of Moses measures all prophecy after him by Exodus' word: the Lord knew him 'face to face'.

evidence.source: Hew thee two tables of stones, as the former were
evidence.target: Cut thee two tables of stone like unto the former

10:1.note: The second tables in Moses' retelling: 'hew thee two tables of stones, as the former were', as God commanded after the breaking.

evidence.source: thou shalt not return to take it away: but thou shalt suffer the stranger, and the pupil, and the widow to take it away
evidence.target: neither shalt thou gather the ears that remain

24:19.note: Deuteronomy re-legislates Leviticus' gleaning law as the forgotten sheaf: what the reaper leaves behind is suffered to the stranger, the pupil and the widow. Leviticus extends the same mercy to the vineyard at 19:10 — left 'to the poor, and the strangers to take'.

evidence.source: and because they hired against thee Balaam, the son of Beor of Mesopotamia in Syria, to curse thee
evidence.target: Come therefore, and curse this people, because it is mightier than I

23:4.note: The hiring Deuteronomy will not let Israel forget is Balac's summons itself, in its own words: come, and curse this people.

evidence.source: & our Lord thy God would not hear Balaam, and he turned his cursing into thy blessing, for that he loved thee
evidence.target: That thou shouldst curse mine enemies I called thee: and thou contrary wise blessest them

23:5.note: The turning of cursing into blessing that Deuteronomy preaches is Balac's complaint verbatim: called to curse, he blessed contrariwise.

evidence.source: There shall not any of the men of this wicked generation see the good Land, which by oath I promised to your fathers
evidence.target: they shall not see the Land for the which I sware to their fathers, neither shall any of them that hath detracted me, behold it

1:35.note: Moses' retelling forty years on keeps the oath's own frame — not see the land, sworn to the fathers — with Caleb's exception following in both tellings.

evidence.source: until all the generation of the men that were warriors was consumed out of the camp, as our Lord had sworn
evidence.target: In this wilderness shall your carcasses lie. All you that are numbered from twenty years & upward, and have murmured against me

2:14.note: Thirty-eight years from Cadesbarne to Zared, Deuteronomy looks back and finds this sentence spent to the last man, 'as our Lord had sworn'.

evidence.source: whom the earth opening her mouth swallowed up with their houses and tabernacles, and all their substance, which they had in the midst of Israel
evidence.target: and opening her mouth, devoured them with their tabernacles & all their substance

11:6.note: Deuteronomy's rehearsal for the children keeps the event's own words — the earth's mouth, the tabernacles, all their substance.

evidence.source: because you did prevaricate against me in the midst of the children of Israel at the Waters of contradiction in Cades of the desert of Sin: and you did not sanctify me among the children of Israel
evidence.target: Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring in these peoples into the land, which I will give them

32:51.note: At the sentence of Moses' own death the charge is read back in its first words: you did not sanctify me at the waters of contradiction.

evidence.source: Remember what our Lord your God did to Mary, in the way when you came out of Ægypt
evidence.target: and behold Mary appeared white with leprosy as it were snow

24:9.note: The law of the leper in Deuteronomy is taught by a memory: what befell Mary in the way — white with leprosy as snow — for speaking against Moyses.

evidence.source: And you came to this place: and there came forth Sehon the king of Hesebon, and Og the king of Basan, meeting us to fight. And we struck them
evidence.target: Of whom he was strucken in the edge of the sword, and his land was possessed from Arnon unto Jeboc

29:7.note: The covenant renewal in the plains of Moab looks back one generation: both kings came forth to fight at the border, and both were struck — the first land Israel ever possessed.

evidence.source: And Josue the son of Nun was replenished with the spirit of wisdom, because Moyses did put his hands upon him
evidence.target: And imposing his hands on his head, he repeated all things that our Lord had commanded

34:9.note: The wisdom Josue is full of when Moses dies is traced by Deuteronomy's last page to this laying on of hands before Eleazar and all the assembly.

evidence.source: But that which is once gone out of thy lips, thou shalt observe, & shalt do as thou hast promised to our Lord thy God, & hast spoken with thy proper will and thine own mouth
evidence.target: If any man make a vow to our Lord, or bind himself by an oath: he shall not make his word frustrate, but all that he promised he shall fulfill

23:23.note: Deuteronomy restates the vow law first spoken to the princes of the tribes (30:2 in this corpus's numbering): what has gone out of the lips must be fulfilled, not made frustrate.

evidence.source: Thou shalt not pity him, & thou shalt take away the guilty blood out of Israel, that it may be well with thee
evidence.target: Pollute not the land of your habitation, which is polluted with the blood of innocents: neither can it otherwise be expiated, but by his blood, that sheddeth another man's blood

19:13.note: Deuteronomy's command to purge the guilty blood from Israel rests on this verse's doctrine, the Torah's fullest statement of it: a land polluted with blood is expiated no other way than by the blood of him who shed it.

evidence.source: the Lord thy God himself will pass over before thee, a devouring and consuming fire
evidence.target: because the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, jealous God.

9:3.note: Within the book itself: the confession of chapter 4 — the Lord thy God is a consuming fire — becomes the battle-promise of chapter 9, the same fire passing over before Israel. Hebrews 12:29's 'our God is a consuming fire' is the seed's, keyed to 4:24.

evidence.source: out of Ægypt I called my son
evidence.target: My first-begotten son is Israel

11:1.note: God called Israel 'my first-begotten son' in Exodus; Osee looks back: 'out of Egypt I called my son'.

evidence.source: But I the Lord thy God out of the Land of Ægypt: and God beside me thou shalt not know, and there is no Saviour beside me
evidence.target: I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the Land of Ægypt

13:4.note: Osee re-utters the Decalogue's preface as accusation: 'I the Lord thy God out of the land of Egypt — and God beside me thou shalt not know'.

evidence.source: but they have entered into Beelphegor, and are alienated into confusion, and are become abominable, as those things, which they loved
evidence.target: And Israel was professed to Beelphegor, and our Lord being angry

9:10.note: The prophet's one word for Israel's fall in the wilderness is this verse's: entered into, professed to, Beelphegor. The seed carries the psalm's witness (105:28) at this verse; Osee's is its own.

evidence.source: And I as it were the nurse of Ephraim, carried them in mine arms: and they knew not that I cured them.
evidence.target: the Lord thy God hath carried thee, as a man is wont to bear his little son, all the way that you have walked, until you came to this place.

11:3.note: The father who carried Israel in the wilderness 'as a man is wont to bear his little son' becomes in Osee the nurse who carried Ephraim in his arms — Deuteronomy's picture carried into the prophet's grief.

evidence.source: They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gabaa: he will remember their iniquity, and will visit their sin.
evidence.target: he brought forth his concubine to them, and he delivered her to them to be illuded: whom when they had abused all the night, they let her go in the morning.

9:9.note: Osee measures Ephraim's deep sin by the days of Gabaa — the Benjaminite city (Judges 19:14) where the Levite's concubine was abused all night and died. Osee 10:9 opens with the same Gabaa memory; it is set aside so the link is carried once, here.

evidence.source: They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gabaa
evidence.target: there came men of that city, the children of Belial (that is to say, without yoke) and besetting the old man's house

9:9.note: Osee names the days of Gabaa as the measure of Israel's deep sin; Judges 19 is the event itself — the men of Gabaa besetting the house. The seed carries Osee 9:9 -> Judges 19 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: I will give thee a king in my fury, and will take him away in mine indignation.
evidence.target: Now therefore your king is ready, whom you have chosen and desired: behold our Lord hath given you a king.

13:11.note: Osee hears God claim the kingship's giving as his own angry act: I will give thee a king in my fury. Samuel's presentation of Saul is that giving, after the request of chapter 8 and the thunder-sign of this chapter: behold, the Lord hath given you a king, the king you chose and desired. The seed carries Osee 13:10 toward 1 Kings 8 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: In the womb he supplanted his brother: and in his strength he was directed with the Angel
evidence.target: he tarried alone: and behold a man wrestled with him till morning

12:3.note: Osee reads Jacob's life back: the supplanting and the night wrestling. The seed carries Osee 12:3 -> Genesis 32 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: he prevailed against the Angel, and was strengthened
evidence.target: if thou hast been strong against God, how much more shalt thou prevail against men?

12:4.note: The prevailing of Peniel in Osee's retelling, answering to the Angel's own verdict in Genesis.

evidence.source: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept her
evidence.target: Jacob therefore served for Rachel seven years

12:12.note: The same event in both books: Jacob's service for his wife, which Osee compresses to a line. The seed carries Osee 12:12 -> Genesis 28 at chapter level, pointing at the flight rather than the service.

evidence.source: Convert o Israel to our Lord thy God: because thou art fallen in thine iniquity
evidence.target: Convert to me in all your heart, in fasting, & in weeping, and in mourning

14:2.note: The conversion call that closes Osee answers Joel's conversion call — 'convert' is the prophets' shared summons-word in this corpus, and Osee's whole book ends where Joel's remedy begins.

evidence.source: the precious blood as it were of an immaculate and unspotted Lamb, Christ
evidence.target: a lamb without spot, a male, of a year old

1:19.note: Christ is the 'immaculate and unspotted Lamb'; the paschal lamb of Exodus must be 'a lamb without spot'.

evidence.source: an elect generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation
evidence.target: you shall be unto me a Priestly Kingdom, and a holy nation

2:9.note: Peter transposes Sinai's 'priestly kingdom' into 'kingly priesthood' and keeps 'a holy nation' word for word; his 'people of purchase' carries on 19:5's peculiar people.

evidence.source: because it is written: You shall be holy, because I am holy
evidence.target: Be ye holy, because I the Lord your God am holy

1:16.note: Peter cites the holiness command with 'it is written'. Leviticus speaks it three times (11:44; 19:2; 20:7); this is the form addressed to the whole assembly. The seed already carries Peter's quotation at 20:7.

evidence.source: him which without acception of persons judgeth according to every one's work
evidence.target: that accepteth not person nor gifts.

1:17.note: The Father invoked in fear is Deuteronomy's impartial judge: without acception of persons, judging every one's work.

evidence.source: you have tasted that our Lord is sweet.
evidence.target: Taste ye, and see that our Lord is sweet:

2:3.note: Peter's tasted-that-the-Lord-is-sweet is the psalm's invitation taken up; the same psalm is quoted at length two chapters later in the epistle.

evidence.source: the stone which the builders rejected, the same is made into the head of the corner:
evidence.target: The stone, which the builders rejected: the same is made into the head of the corner.

2:7.note: Peter's stone citation at verse level; the seed keys 1 Peter 2 to this psalm only at chapter level (and to 117:25).

evidence.source: Let him decline from evil, and do good: let him inquire peace, & follow it:
evidence.target: Turn away from evil, and do good: seek after peace and pursue it.

3:11.note: Inside Peter's long Psalm 33 citation; the seed carries only 1 Peter 3:10 to 33:13, leaving the citation's remaining verses unkeyed.

evidence.source: the eyes of our Lord are upon the just, and his ears unto their prayers:
evidence.target: The eyes of our Lord upon the just: and his ears unto their prayers.

3:12.note: The next verse of Peter's Psalm 33 citation.

evidence.source: the countenance of our Lord upon them that do evil things.
evidence.target: the countenance of our Lord is upon them that do evil things:

3:12.note: The last member of Peter's Psalm 33 citation, at the psalm's next verse.

evidence.source: casting all your carefulness upon him, because he hath care of you.
evidence.target: Cast thy care upon our Lord: and he will nourish thee:

5:7.note: Peter's casting is the psalm's imperative turned into an exhortation; the seed keys 1 Peter 5 to this psalm only at chapter level.

evidence.source: that the probation of your faith much more precious than gold (which is proved by the fire)
evidence.target: he knoweth my way, and hath proved me as gold that passeth through the fire:

1:7.note: Job's confidence — proved as gold through the fire — becomes Peter's praise of a faith much more precious than gold, proved by the same fire.

evidence.source: God resisteth the proud, and to the humble he giveth grace.
evidence.target: He shall delude the deluders, and to the mild he will give grace.

5:5.note: Peter and James both cite the proverb in its Greek form — God resisteth the proud. Stated openly: this corpus's Proverbs, from the Vulgate, prints only the second half ('to the mild he will give grace'); the entry rests on that printed half, as James 4:6 is keyed by the seed to the neighbouring verse (3:35).

evidence.source: charity covereth the multitude of sins.
evidence.target: charity covereth all sins.

4:8.note: Peter takes the proverb's clause entire, widening 'all sins' to 'the multitude of sins'. The seed carries this verse of Peter only at chapter level (Proverbs 10); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: By whose stripes you are healed
evidence.target: with the wail of his stripe we are healed

2:24.note: Peter's healing clause is 53:5's stripe, pluralized. The seed keys 1 Peter 2:24 to 53:4 (the sins borne); the stripe that heals is the next verse's.

evidence.source: For you were as sheep straying
evidence.target: All we have strayed as sheep

2:25.note: Peter turns Isaias's confession into his readers' past: we all strayed as sheep. The Pastor to whom they are converted gathers the verse's second half, the iniquity laid on him, into 2:24.

evidence.source: Who when he was reviled, did not revile: when he suffered, he threatened not
evidence.target: and opened not his mouth

2:23.note: Peter's silent sufferer: reviled without reviling, suffering without threatening — the Servant who, offered, opened not his mouth.

evidence.source: the word of our Lord remaineth for ever
evidence.target: the word of our Lord abideth for ever

1:25.note: Peter's citation, second half. The seed keys 1 Peter 1:24 to 40:6 (the grass); the abiding word that closes the saying is 40:8's.

evidence.source: sanctify our Lord Christ in your hearts
evidence.target: The Lord of hosts him sanctify ye

3:15.note: Peter takes Isaias's charge — the Lord of hosts, him sanctify ye, be he your dread — and names its object openly: sanctify the Lord Christ in your hearts. The transfer is the point of the entry and is stated, not hidden.

evidence.source: Which sometime not a people: but now the people of God
evidence.target: I will say to Not my people: My people art thou

2:10.note: Peter applies Osee's reversal to his readers. The seed carries this only at chapter level (1 Peter 2:10 -> Osee 2); the mercy half of Peter's verse answers to 2:23, the people half quoted here to 2:24.

evidence.source: but only stand confidently, & you shall see the help of our Lord over you
evidence.target: stand, and see the great wonders of our Lord

20:17.note: Jahaziel's word to Josaphat replays Moses' word at the sea: stand, fear not, and see what the Lord will do.

evidence.source: It shall not be you that shall fight
evidence.target: Our Lord will fight for you and you shall hold your peace

20:17.note: 'It shall not be you that shall fight' is Exodus' promise in other words: 'Our Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace'.

evidence.source: for all the days of the desolation she kept a Sabbath, till the seventy years were expired
evidence.target: Then shall the land take pleasure in her sabbaths all the days of her desolation

36:21.note: The Chronicler reads the seventy years of exile as Leviticus 26:34 fulfilled, and says so in Jeremiah's name: the land, emptied of its people, at last keeps the sabbaths they had withheld from her.

evidence.source: the word of our Lord by the mouth of Jeremy might be accomplished, and the land might celebrate their Sabbaths: for all the days of the desolation she kept a Sabbath, till the seventy years were expired
evidence.target: And all this land shall be in desolation, and into astonishment: and all these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years

36:21.note: The Chronicler closes his history by naming Jeremy's word accomplished — the land desolate, the seventy years expired. The seed points Jeremias 25 at this verse at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here. The Sabbath-rest reasoning is the Chronicler's own, drawn from Leviticus 26, and is not claimed for Jeremias.

evidence.source: fire descended from heaven, and devoured the holocausts & victims: and the majesty of our Lord filled the house
evidence.target: a fire coming forth from our Lord, devoured the holocaust, and the fat that was upon the altar

7:1.note: Solomon's dedication is Leviticus 9 written large: fire descends and devours the offerings, and the majesty of the Lord fills the house, as at the tabernacle's first altar.

evidence.source: Ozias therefore the king was a leper until the day of his death, and he dwelt in a house apart full of the leprosy
evidence.target: he shall dwell alone without the camp

26:21.note: The leper king lives out the leper's sentence — cut off from the house of the Lord he had invaded, dwelling apart until his death — exactly as Leviticus 13:46 appoints for everyone the disease marks.

evidence.source: Counsel therefore being taken of the king and the Princes, and of all the assembly of Jerusalem, they decreed to make the Phase the second month
evidence.target: in the second month, the fourteenth day of the month at even: with azymes and wild lettuce shall they eat it

30:2.note: Ezechias' Passover is kept under this provision: the Phase of the second month, first given for the man unclean upon a soul or far off in his journey (9:10).

evidence.source: for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor acception of persons, nor desire of gifts.
evidence.target: a great God and mighty, and terrible, that accepteth not person nor gifts.

19:7.note: Josaphat charges his judges with Moses' words almost entire: no acception of persons, no gifts, with the God of gods. His 'the judgment is God's' (19:6) also answers Deuteronomy 1:17; the charge is keyed once, here.

evidence.source: The fathers shall not be slain for the children, nor the children for their fathers, but every one shall die in his own sin.
evidence.target: The fathers shall not be slain for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every one shall die for his own sin,

25:4.note: Chronicles retells Amasias' restraint with the law quoted word for word, 'as it is written in the Book of the law of Moyses'. The seed carries this verse only at chapter level (Deuteronomy 24); Kings' telling is keyed beside it.

evidence.source: fear not, neither dread ye the king of the Assyrians, and all the multitude, that is with him: for there are many more with us, than with him.
evidence.target: Fear not: for there are more with us than with them.

32:7.note: Ezechias heartens Jerusalem in Eliseus's words at Dothan — more with us than with them — now spoken of the unseen host against Assyria.

evidence.source: Give me wisdom and intelligence, that I may come in and go out before thy people
evidence.target: give to thy servant a docible heart, that he may judge the people, and discern between good & evil.

1:10.note: Salomon's request at Gabaon in both histories: wisdom to judge this great people. Our layer already keys Wisdom's prayers to each telling separately; the tellings themselves were unkeyed to each other.

evidence.source: Salomon began to build the house of our Lord in Jerusalem, in mount Moria
evidence.target: he began to build a house to our Lord.

3:1.note: The temple begun, in both histories. Chronicles anchors it at Moria and Ornan's floor; Kings anchors it by the years from the Exodus. Our layer keys Genesis 22:2 to the Chronicles verse for the Moria name.

evidence.source: the Priests could not stand and minister for the darkness. For the glory of our Lord had filled the house of God.
evidence.target: the Priests could not stand and minister for the cloud: for the glory of our Lord had filled the house of our Lord.

5:14.note: The glory fills the finished house in both tellings; Chronicles prints darkness where Kings prints cloud, as the texts stand.

evidence.source: which keepest covenant and mercy with thy servants, that walk before thee in all their heart:
evidence.target: which keepest covenant and mercy with thy servants, that walk before thee in all their heart.

6:14.note: The dedication prayer opens in both histories with Deuteronomy's confession of the covenant-keeping God; our layer keys the Kings verse back to Deuteronomy 7:9.

evidence.source: if they shall sin to thee (for there is no man that sinneth not)
evidence.target: if they shall sin to thee (for there is no man which sinneth not)

6:36.note: The prayer's confession that there is no man that sinneth not, in both tellings. The seed keys 1 John 1:8 to each verse separately; the tellings were unkeyed to each other.

evidence.source: I have heard thy prayer, and have chosen this place to me for a house of sacrifice.
evidence.target: I have heard thy prayer & thy petition which thou hast prayed before me: I have sanctified this house, which thou hast built

7:12.note: The night answer to the dedication prayer in both histories: heard, and the house sanctified for the Name.

evidence.source: The queen of Saba also, when she had heard the fame of Salomon, came to prove him in hard propositions in Jerusalem
evidence.target: the queen of Saba also having heard the fame of Salomon, in the name of our Lord came to prove him in hard propositions.

9:1.note: The queen of Saba's visit in both histories. The seed carries the pair only at chapter level (3 Kings 10).

evidence.source: he forsook the counsel of the Ancients, and began to treat with young men, that had been brought up with him
evidence.target: Who left the counsel of the ancients, which they had given him, and admitted youngmen, that had been brought up with him

10:8.note: Roboam forsakes the ancients for the young men, in both histories — the schism's hinge in one verse.

evidence.source: Sesac the king of Ægypt retired from Jerusalem, taking away the treasures of the house of our Lord, and of the king's house
evidence.target: in the fifth year of the reign of Roboam, Sesac the king of Ægypt came up into Jerusalem

12:9.note: Sesac's invasion in both histories: Kings dates the coming up, Chronicles inventories what he carried away, the temple treasures and Salomon's golden shields.

evidence.source: I saw our Lord sitting in his throne, and all the host of heaven assisting him on the right hand and on the left.
evidence.target: I saw our Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven assisting him on the right hand and on the left:

18:18.note: Micheas's vision of the throne before Ahab's last battle, in Kings and in Chronicles, nearly word for word.

evidence.source: they brought forth the king's son, and put the crown upon him, and the testimony, and gave the law to be in his hand, and they made him king
evidence.target: he brought forth the king's son, and put upon him the diadem, and the covenant: and they made him king, and anointed him

23:11.note: Joas brought forth and crowned in the temple, in both histories — the child king hidden from Athalia made king by Joiada.

evidence.source: forthwith there rose a leprosy in his forehead before the Priests, in the house of our Lord upon the altar of incense.
evidence.target: our Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death

26:19.note: Ozias the leper king in both histories: Kings states the stroke and the separate house; Chronicles alone tells why — the censer seized at the altar of incense.

evidence.source: he made his sons to pass through fire, to the Valebenennom: he observed dreams, followed soothsayings
evidence.target: he made his son pass through fire: and he used soothsaying, and observed divinations

33:6.note: Manasses' banned rites enacted, in both histories. Our Deuteronomy stage keys the Kings verse to the law's banned list (18:10) and set the Chronicles telling aside there as its duplicate; the two tellings are keyed to each other here.

evidence.source: Helcias the Priest found the Book of the law of our Lord by the hand of Moyses.
evidence.target: I have found the Book of the law in the house of our Lord

34:14.note: The finding of the Book in the temple repairs, in both histories — the event that drives Josias's reform.

evidence.source: Josias made in Jerusalem a Phase to our Lord, which was immolated the fourteenth day of the first month.
evidence.target: Make a Phase to our Lord your God, according as it is written in the Book of this covenant.

35:1.note: Josias's Passover in both histories: Chronicles dates and describes it, Kings gives the king's command from the found Book. The Kings verse is keyed back to Deuteronomy's Phase command separately.

evidence.source: came up Nechao the king of Ægypt to fight in Charcamis beside Euphrates: and Josias went forth to meet him.
evidence.target: came up Pharao Nechao the king of Ægypt, against the king of Assyrians to the river Euphrates: and Josias the king went to meet him: and was slain in Mageddo

35:20.note: Josias goes out against Nechao in both histories; Kings names the place of his death, Mageddo, which Zacharias's mourning remembers.

evidence.source: he made Sedecias his uncle king over Juda and Jerusalem.
evidence.target: And he appointed Matthanias his uncle for him: and called his name Sedecias.

36:10.note: The last king set up by Babylon in both histories: Chronicles calls him by his royal name only; Kings preserves his former name, Matthanias.

evidence.source: Two & forty years old was Ochozias when he began to reign
evidence.target: Two and twenty years old was Ochozias when he began to reign

22:2.note: The same accession in both histories — and the ages differ as printed: forty-two in Chronicles, twenty-two in Kings. Entered as parallel with the discrepancy stated, not harmonised.

evidence.source: gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?
evidence.target: the seed of Abraham my friend:

20:7.note: Josaphat pleads the land-promise to 'the seed of Abraham thy friend'; Isaias preserves the same divine title for Abraham, the friend of God, in the same phrase.

evidence.source: Fear not, neither dread ye this multitude: for it is not your battle, but God's.
evidence.target: for it is his battle, & he will deliver you into our hands.

20:15.note: Jahaziel's oracle to Josaphat is David's word to Golias turned into a promise: the battle is God's, not yours.

evidence.source: According to the days of thy coming forth out of the Land of Ægypt I will shew him marvels
evidence.target: terrible and laudable, doing marvels

7:15.note: God promises Micheas a repetition of the Exodus: 'according to the days of thy coming forth out of Egypt I will shew him marvels' — the song's God is 'doing marvels'.

evidence.source: What God is like to thee, which takest away iniquity
evidence.target: Who is like to thee among the strong, o Lord?

7:18.note: Micheas opens with the song's own question — 'Who is like to thee?' — and turns it from God's power against Egypt to his taking away of iniquity.

evidence.source: what Balaam the son of Beor answered him: from Setim even to Galgal, that thou mightest know the justices of our Lord
evidence.target: and taking up his parable, he said: From Aram hath Balac king of the Moabites brought me, from the mountains of the East

6:5.note: The answer God bids his people remember is the parables of chapters 23-24; this is their head, where Balaam owns that Balac brought him to curse.

evidence.source: because I am fallen: I shall arise, when I have sit in darkness, our Lord is my light.
evidence.target: For seven times shall the just fall, and shall rise again

7:8.note: Micheas answers his enemy with the proverb's law of the just man: fallen, he shall rise again.

evidence.source: the mount of the house of our Lord prepared in the top of mountains, and high above the hills: & peoples shall flow to it
evidence.target: the mountain of the house of our Lord shall be prepared, in the top of mountains, and it shall be elevated above the little hills: and all nations shall flow unto it

4:1.note: The mountain oracle stands in both prophets nearly word for word (Micheas 4:1–3 and Isaias 2:2–4). Which prophet spoke first the texts do not say, and this entry does not pretend to settle it; the seed points Isaias 2 at Micheas 4:1 at chapter level.

evidence.source: Come, let us go up to the mountain of our Lord, & to the house of the God of Jacob: & he will teach us of his ways
evidence.target: come and let us go up to the mount of our Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us his ways

4:2.note: Second verse of the shared oracle; see Micheas 4:1 in this draft.

evidence.source: they shall cut their swords into coulters, and their spears into spades: nation shall not take sword against nation
evidence.target: they shall turn their swords into coulters, and their spears into sithes: nation shall not lift up sword against nation

4:3.note: The swords-into-ploughshares verse of the shared oracle — the verse Joel 3:10 deliberately reverses, entered in this draft.

evidence.source: Manna failed after they did eat of the corn of the Land
evidence.target: the children of Israel did eat Manna forty years, till they came into the habitable land

5:12.note: The manna that began in the desert fails at Gilgal, exactly where Exodus set its term: Israel ate it 'until they touched the borders of the land of Chanaan'.

evidence.source: as Moyses the servant of our Lord had commanded the children of Israel, and it is written in the volume of the law of Moyses: an Altar of unhewed stones which iron hath not touched
evidence.target: thou shalt not build it of hewed stones: for if thou lift up thy knife over it, it shall be polluted

8:31.note: Josue builds the altar on Ebal expressly 'as Moses had commanded... in the volume of the law' — the unhewed stones of Exodus' altar law, on which no iron has been lifted.

evidence.source: & I would not hear him, but contrarywise by him I blessed you, and delivered you out of his hand
evidence.target: That thou shouldst curse mine enemies I called thee: and thou contrary wise blessest them

24:10.note: Josue's farewell rehearses the same reversal, and keeps its key word: 'contrarywise' in both the complaint and the retelling.

evidence.source: Forty years old was I when Moyses the servant of our Lord sent me from Cadesbarne, to view the Land, & I reported to him that which to me seemed true
evidence.target: Send men that may view the Land of Chanaan, which I will give to the children of Israel, one of every tribe, of the Princes

14:7.note: Caleb, pleading for Hebron in his old age, names the errand that began with this command — sent from Cadesbarne to view the land.

evidence.source: Is it a small thing to you that you sinned in Beelphegor, and until this present day the spot of this abomination abideth in us? And many of the people fell dead
evidence.target: And Israel was professed to Beelphegor, and our Lord being angry

22:17.note: The tribes beyond Jordan are warned by the standing spot of Phogor: the sin that abides is this professing to Beelphegor, for which the many fell.

evidence.source: saying: Our Lord commanded by the hand of Moyses, that a possession should be given us in the midst of our brethren. And he gave them according to the commandment of our Lord a possession in the midst of their father's brethren
evidence.target: The daughters of Salphaad require a just thing: give them possession among their father's kin, and let them succeed him in the inheritance

17:4.note: In the dividing of the land the daughters plead the ruling itself, and Josue gives the possession 'according to the commandment of our Lord' — this commandment, spoken to Moyses at their first asking.

evidence.source: Separate the cities of the fugitives, of the which I spake to you by the hand of Moyses
evidence.target: determine what cities shall be for the succour of fugitives, that have not voluntarily shed blood

20:2.note: Josue separates the very cities God 'spake of by the hand of Moyses': the refuge law of this chapter put into possession, six cities among the Levites' forty-eight (35:6).

evidence.source: Separate the cities of the fugitives, of the which I spake to you by the hand of Moyses;
evidence.target: three cities shalt thou separate to thee in the midst of the Land, which our Lord thy God will give thee in possession,

20:2.note: Josue separates the refuge cities 'of the which I spake to you by the hand of Moyses' — the appointment Deuteronomy made (and Numbers 35 gives in full, keyed in our Numbers stage at Hebrews 6:18). The verb is the law's own: separate.

evidence.source: but they shall be a pit and a snare for you, and a stumbling block at your side, and stakes in your eyes, till he take you away and destroy you from his excellent Land
evidence.target: they that remain, shall be unto you as it were nails in your eyes, and spears in your sides, and they shall be your adversaries in the Land of your habitation

23:13.note: Josue's farewell takes up the warning spoken on the march: the nations left in the land as nails — stakes — in the eyes, and spears in the sides.

evidence.source: And when the sun was down, he commanded the soldiers to take them down from the gibbets.
evidence.target: his body shall not remain upon the tree, but the same day shall be buried

10:27.note: The five kings hang until sundown and no longer: Josue takes them down at the sun's going down, the same day, as the law of the hanged man commands.

evidence.source: that you love our Lord your God, and walk in all his ways, and observe all his commandments, and cleave to him, and serve him in all your heart, and in all your soul.
evidence.target: what doth the Lord thy God require of thee, but that thou fear the Lord thy God, and walk in his ways, and love him, and serve the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul:

22:5.note: Josue's farewell charge to the Transjordan tribes is a cento of this chapter: walk in his ways, love him, serve him with all the heart and soul — Deuteronomy 10:12's requirement, with the cleaving of 11:22 woven in.

evidence.source: as I have been with Moyses, so will I be with thee: I will not leave nor forsake thee.
evidence.target: himself will be with thee: he will not leave, nor forsake thee

1:5.note: God repeats to Josue, in the first person, the promise Moses had reported to him at the commissioning: I will not leave nor forsake thee. The transposition is only of person, as with Psalms 67:2 in our Numbers stage.

evidence.source: Take courage, and be strong: for thou shalt by lot divide to this people the Land, for the which I sware to their fathers
evidence.target: Take courage, & be strong: for thou shalt bring in this people into the Land, which our Lord sware that he would give to their fathers, and thou shalt divide it by lot.

1:6.note: God takes up Moses' charge to Josue in Moses' own words — take courage, be strong, divide the land by lot — now spoken over Moses' grave.

evidence.source: Every place the step of your foot shall tread, will I deliver to you, as I have spoken to Moyses.
evidence.target: Every place that your foot shall tread, shall be yours. From the desert, and from Libanus, from the great river Euphrates unto the west sea shall be your borders.

1:3.note: God's first word to Josue quotes the border-promise of Deuteronomy and names its source: 'as I have spoken to Moyses'. The borders that follow in Josue are this verse's.

evidence.source: I have recounted whatsoever Amalec hath done to Israel: how he resisted them in the way when they came up out of Ægypt
evidence.target: I will destroy the memory of Amalec from under heaven

15:2.note: God's 'recounting' of Amalec to Saul is the oath written at Rephidim falling due: the memory of Amalec, sworn to be destroyed from under heaven, is now to be destroyed by Israel's king.

evidence.source: Seek me a woman that hath a pythonical spirit, and I will go to her, and will ask by her
evidence.target: Man, or woman, in whom is a pythonical or divining spirit

28:7.note: Saul, who had put away the diviners under this very law, goes by night to a woman 'that hath a pythonical spirit' — the law's own phrase for what he seeks.

evidence.source: but that which you owe render unto it for sin
evidence.target: he shall offer for his offence a ram without spot out of the flocks

6:3.note: Even the Philistines' diviners know an offended god is answered with the offence offering: they send golden emerods and mice 'for sin' beside the ark — Leviticus' asham imitated by Gentiles, restitution carried to the sanctuary.

evidence.source: for neither is he a man that he may repent
evidence.target: God is not as man, that he may lie, nor as the son of man, that he may be changed

15:29.note: Samuel's sentence over Saul is Balaam's confession turned to judgment: God is not as man, to lie or to repent of his word — so the kingdom is rent and not restored.

evidence.source: I will give him to our Lord all the days of his life, & the razor shall not come upon his head
evidence.target: a razor shall not pass over his head

1:11.note: Anna's vow for Samuel borrows the Nazarite's visible mark — the unshorn head of a child given to the Lord all the days of his life.

evidence.source: appoint us a king, that he may judge us, as also all nations have.
evidence.target: and sayest: I will set a king over me, as all nations have round about:

8:5.note: The elders ask in the very words Moses foresaw: a king, 'as all nations have'. Deuteronomy had written the request into the law four centuries before it was spoken.

evidence.source: Our Lord mortifieth and quickeneth, bringeth down to hell and fetcheth back again.
evidence.target: I will kill, and I will make to live: I will strike, and I will heal, and there is none that can deliver out of my hand.

2:6.note: Anna's canticle sings the song of Moses back: the Lord who kills and makes alive, who brings down and fetches back. Wisdom 16:13 speaks the same confession, but its words track Anna's form; her canticle carries the verse here.

evidence.source: the word that I did covenant with you when you came out of the Land of Ægypt
evidence.target: If therefore you will hear my voice, and keep my covenant

2:6.note: Aggeus steadies the builders by 'the word that I did covenant with you when you came out of the land of Egypt' — the covenant whose terms are 'if you will hear my voice, and keep my covenant'.

evidence.source: If a man take sanctified flesh in the skirt of his garment, and touch with the skirt thereof bread, or broth, or wine, or oil, or any meat: shall it be sanctified?
evidence.target: Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof, shall be sanctified

2:13.note: Aggeus is sent to 'ask the priests the law': his test case probes Leviticus 6:27, where what touches the sin offering's flesh is sanctified. The priests rule that holiness does not travel at second hand — and the prophet turns the ruling on the people's works.

evidence.source: If one polluted on a soul touch any of all these, shall he be contaminated?
evidence.target: He that toucheth a thing unclean by occasion of that is dead

2:14.note: The second test case is Leviticus' corpse-uncleanness: defilement, unlike holiness, does spread by touch. The priests' 'He shall be contaminated' applies the law of Aaron's seed to the whole nation.

evidence.source: You have sowed much, and brought in little: you have eaten, and have not been filled
evidence.target: Thou shalt eat, and shalt not be filled

1:6.note: Aggeus preaches Micheas' curse as present fact: eaten and not filled. The seed carries Aggeus 1:6 -> Micheas 6 at chapter level only (and to Deuteronomy 28 likewise).

evidence.source: I struck you with the burning wind, and with the blast, and with hail, all the works of your hands: and there was none among you, that returned to me
evidence.target: I struck you with a burning wind, and with blasting, the multitude of your gardens, and all your vineyards

2:18.note: Aggeus recalls Amos' striking — burning wind and blast, and none returning — in Amos' own refrain-words. Corpus numbering note: the striking verse stands at Aggeus 2:18 in this text, where modern editions number it 2:17.

evidence.source: I will take thee o Zorobabel son of Salathiel my servant, saith our Lord, and will put thee as a signet, because thee have I chosen
evidence.target: if Jechonias the son of Joakim the king of Juda shall be a ring on my right hand, thence will I pluck him off

2:24.note: The signet reversed: Jechonias, Zorobabel's grandfather, was the ring plucked off in Jeremias; Aggeus sets the grandson as the signet chosen. Same image, opposite sentence — graded parallel.

evidence.source: He that shall curse father or mother, dying let him die
evidence.target: He that curseth his father, or mother, dying let him die

7:10.note: Mark's form of the same quotation: 'He that shall curse father or mother, dying let him die'.

evidence.source: And a woman which was in an issue of blood twelve years
evidence.target: The woman that hath a flux of blood many days not in her menstrual time

5:25.note: The woman's twelve-year issue is the case Leviticus 15:25 governs — a flux beyond the menstrual time, unclean all the days she is subject to it. She reaches Jesus through the crowd the law would have kept her apart from.

evidence.source: Hear Israel: the Lord thy God, is one God.
evidence.target: Hear Israel, The Lord our God, is one Lord.

12:29.note: Jesus' answer to the scribe begins with the Shema itself. The seed keys this verse of Mark to 6:5 (the love-command that follows at Mark 12:30); the words the Lord speaks first are 6:4's.

evidence.source: and to love his neighbour as himself, is a greater thing than all holocausts and sacrifices.
evidence.target: For Better is Obedience Than Victims: and to harken rather than to offer the fat of rams.

12:33.note: The scribe's confession — love is a greater thing than all holocausts and sacrifices — is Samuel's sentence to Saul turned into a comparison of loves: better is obedience than victims. Jesus answers, Thou art not far from the kingdom. Osee 6:6's mercy-and-not-sacrifice stands in the same field and is set aside; Mark's comparative is Samuel's shape.

evidence.source: the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light
evidence.target: the sun is darkened in his rising, and the moon shall not shine in her light

13:24.note: Mark's form of the same discourse clause. The seed keys Mark 13:24 to Ezechiel 31:7; the sun-and-moon wording is Isaias 13:10's.

evidence.source: they were as sheep not having a shepherd
evidence.target: my sheep were dispersed, because there was no Pastor

6:34.note: Mark's form of the same compassion sentence, at the feeding of the five thousand.

evidence.source: such tribulations as were not from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, neither shall be
evidence.target: a time shall come such as hath not been from the time since nations began even until that time

13:19.note: Mark's form of the same unexampled-tribulation saying, its beginning measured from creation where Daniel measures from the beginning of nations.

evidence.source: as it were the form of the sapphire stone the similitude of a throne
evidence.target: under his feet as it were a work of sapphire stone

1:26.note: On Sinai the elders saw under God's feet 'as it were a work of sapphire stone'; by the Chebar, Ezechiel sees the throne itself in the likeness of sapphire above the firmament.

evidence.source: my tabernacle shall be in them: & I will be their God, and they shall be my people
evidence.target: I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel & will be their God

37:27.note: Ezechiel's restoration promise re-utters the tabernacle's dedication word: 'I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel, and will be their God'.

evidence.source: And my tabernacle shall be in them: & I will be their God, and they shall be my people
evidence.target: I will set my tabernacle in the midst of you

37:27.note: Ezekiel's restoration promise gathers Leviticus 26:11-12 into one verse — the tabernacle set among them, God theirs, they his people. The Apocalypse takes the same promise up at 26:12 (entered separately).

evidence.source: my sabbaths I gave to them, to be a sign between me and them: & that they might know that I am the Lord sanctifying them
evidence.target: it is a sign between me and you in your generations: that you may know that I am the Lord, which sanctify you

20:12.note: Ezechiel re-utters God's Sinai word almost verbatim: the sabbaths given 'to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord sanctifying them'.

evidence.source: which a man doing, shall live in them
evidence.target: which a man doing, shall live in them

20:11.note: Ezekiel, rehearsing the gift of the statutes in the wilderness, quotes Leviticus' own promise attached to them word for word. Paul quotes the same clause at Romans 10:5 (seed-carried).

evidence.source: Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers
evidence.target: so that you shall eat the flesh of your sons & of your daughters

5:10.note: Ezekiel re-pronounces the covenant curse of Leviticus 26 as present judgment on Jerusalem. The siege of Samaria enacts it literally (4 Kings 6:29, entered as parallel).

evidence.source: approached not to a menstruous woman
evidence.target: To a woman, having her flowers, thou shalt not approach

18:6.note: Ezekiel's portrait of the just man is a digest of the holiness code; this clause is Leviticus 18:19 in the prophet's own dress.

evidence.source: hath not lent to usury, and not taken more
evidence.target: Thou shalt not give him thy money to usury, and an overplus of the fruits thou shalt not exact of him

18:8.note: The paired marks of the just man — usury not charged and 'more' not taken — are Leviticus 25:37's own pair: money to usury, overplus exacted. Psalm 14:5 sings the same clause (entered separately).

evidence.source: And I will sanctify my great name, that is polluted among the Gentiles, which you have polluted in the midst of them
evidence.target: Pollute not my holy name that I may be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel

36:23.note: Leviticus ends the priestly charges with the command not to pollute the Name, that it be sanctified in Israel's midst. Ezekiel takes the charge up for the exile, where the Name was polluted among the Gentiles instead. Matthew 6:9's 'hallowed be thy name' reaches Leviticus through this verse and is set aside as mediated.

evidence.source: they shall teach my people what is between a holy thing and polluted, & between clean and unclean they shall shew to them
evidence.target: that you may have knowledge to discern between the holy and profane, between the polluted and clean

44:23.note: The charge given to Aaron after the death of Nadab and Abihu — to discern between holy and profane, polluted and clean — is handed on to Ezekiel's temple priests as their teaching office.

evidence.source: All carrion, and thing taken by a beast of birds, and of cattle the Priests shall not eat
evidence.target: Carrion and that which was taken of a beast, they shall not eat, nor be polluted in them

44:31.note: Leviticus' carrion ban for the priests is re-enacted nearly word for word in Ezekiel's temple law.

evidence.source: widow, and her that is divorced they shall not take for wives, but virgins of the seed of the house of Israel
evidence.target: but a widow and her that is put away, and a filth, and a whore he shall not take, but a maid of his own people

44:22.note: Ezekiel's temple law extends the high priest's marriage rule — no widow, no divorced woman, a virgin of his own people — to all the priests of the restored house, with one stated exception for a priest's widow.

evidence.source: And my sheep were dispersed, because there was no Pastor: & they came to be devoured of all the beasts of the field, and were dispersed
evidence.target: lest the people of our Lord be as sheep without a pastor

34:5.note: Ezechiel's charge against the shepherds of Israel opens where Moses' prayer began: a flock with no pastor is a flock dispersed and devoured.

evidence.source: And this is the border of the land: toward the North quarter, from the great sea by the way of Hethalon, as they come to Sedada
evidence.target: from the which they shall come unto Emath as far as the borders of Sedada

47:15.note: Ezechiel's survey of the restored land retraces this chapter's borders: the north line still runs from the great sea by Emath toward Sedada and Enan (34:7-9) — the old lot lines kept for the new possession.

evidence.source: and I spread my garment over thee, and covered thy ignominy. And I sware to thee, and I entered a covenant with thee, saith our Lord God: and thou wast made mine.
evidence.target: spread thy mantle upon thy servant, because thou art nigh of kin.

16:8.note: God's espousal of Jerusalem is spoken in Ruth's own gesture: I spread my garment over thee, and entered a covenant. At the threshing floor Ruth asks Booz, her near kinsman, to spread his mantle over his handmaid — the covering that claims a wife. Ezechiel takes the gesture up into God's mouth.

evidence.source: these three men shall be in the midst thereof, Noe, Daniel, & Job: they by their justice shall deliver their own souls
evidence.target: that man was simple, and right, and fearing God, and departing from evil.

14:14.note: Ezechiel ranks Job with Noe and Daniel as a man whose justice could deliver his own soul; the justice he presumes is the book's opening verdict on Job. The prophet's second naming (14:20) is set aside as this entry's duplicate.

evidence.source: if these three men shall be in the midst thereof, Noe, Daniel, & Job: they by their justice shall deliver their own souls
evidence.target: My God hath sent his Angel, and hath shut up the mouths of the lions, and they have not hurt me: because before him justice hath been found in me

14:14.note: Ezechiel names Daniel with Noe and Job as the righteous whose justice delivers their own souls; the lions' den is that justice on record — shut mouths, because justice was found in him.

evidence.source: I will make the stars thereof to wax black: the sun I will cover with a cloud, & the moon shall not give her light
evidence.target: the moon shall not shine in her light

32:7.note: Ezechiel reworks Isaias's day-of-the-Lord astronomy for Pharao: stars blackened, sun cloud-covered, moon lightless. The seed points Ezechiel 32 at Isaias 13:10 at chapter level, and keys Matthew 24:29 to this verse of Ezechiel; the Isaias anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: hath given his bread to the hungry, and covered the naked with a garment
evidence.target: Break thy bread to the hungry & the needy, & harborless bring in into thy house: when thou shalt see the naked cover him

18:7.note: Ezechiel's portrait of the just man recites Isaias's fast: bread given to the hungry, the naked covered. The seed points Ezechiel 18 at Isaias 58:7 at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: The fathers did eat a sour grape, & the teeth of the children are set on edge?
evidence.target: The fathers did eat the bitter grape, and the teeth of the children are set on edge

18:2.note: The sour-grapes proverb stands in both prophets, with its wording varied (sour grape in Ezechiel, bitter grape in Jeremias — the difference is printed, not harmonized). Jeremias prophesies the days when they shall say it no more; Ezechiel quotes it in use in the land and refutes it at length.

evidence.source: Lo thou art wiser than Daniel: every secret is not hid from thee
evidence.target: every word of wisdom and understanding, that the king demanded of them, he found in them more by ten fold

28:3.note: Ezechiel taunts Tyre's prince with Daniel as the living byword for wisdom — Daniel still a young exile at Babylon's court, already found tenfold wiser in every word of wisdom the king demanded.

evidence.source: In that day shall that which is upon the bridle of the horse be holy to our Lord
evidence.target: wherein thou shalt grave after the work of a graver, Holy to the Lord

14:20.note: The words graven on the high priest's golden plate — 'Holy to the Lord' — are in Zacharias' last day found upon a horse's bridle: the inscription itself is quoted and spread over all Jerusalem.

evidence.source: shall go up from year to year, to adore the King, the Lord of hosts, and to celebrate the festivity of tabernacles
evidence.target: From the fifteenth day of this seventh month, shall be the festivity of tabernacles seven days to the Lord

14:16.note: The feast given to Israel in Leviticus 23 is opened by Zechariah to 'all that shall be left of all Nations': every surviving people goes up to Jerusalem from year to year to keep it.

evidence.source: for he that shall touch you, toucheth the apple of mine eye:
evidence.target: and kept him as the apple of his eye.

2:8.note: The song's tenderness turned to a threat: Israel kept as the apple of God's eye means the nations that touch her touch the eye itself.

evidence.source: great lamentation in Jerusalem, as the lamentation of Adadremmon in the field of Mageddon.
evidence.target: they carried him away into Jerusalem, & he died, & was buried in the monument of his fathers, and all Juda & Jerusalem mourned for him.

12:11.note: Zacharias measures the coming mourning by Mageddon's: Josias, slain at Mageddo, mourned by all Juda and Jerusalem. The seed carries Zacharias 12:11 only at chapter level (2 Paralipomenon 35).

evidence.source: great lamentation in Jerusalem, as the lamentation of Adadremmon in the field of Mageddon
evidence.target: but went forward to fight in the field of Mageddo

12:11.note: Zacharias measures the coming mourning by the lamentation for Josias, slain in the field of Mageddo (his lamentations are rehearsed at 2 Paralipomenon 35:25). The seed carries Zacharias 12:11 -> 2 Paralipomenon 35 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: living waters shall issue forth out of Jerusalem: half of them to the East sea, and half of them to the last sea
evidence.target: waters issued forth under the threshold of the house toward the East

14:8.note: Two temple-river visions: Ezechiel's waters from under the threshold, Zacharias' living waters out of Jerusalem to both seas. Same institution and shape, little shared wording — graded parallel.

evidence.source: the widow, and the pupil, and the stranger, and the poor do not calumniate
evidence.target: A widow and an orphan you shall not hurt

7:10.note: Zacharias gathers the old law's protected ones — widow and pupil (orphan) first — into his justice charge. The seed carries Zacharias 7:10 -> Exodus 22 at chapter level only.

evidence.source: Behold thy gods Israel, which brought thee out of the Land of Ægypt
evidence.target: These are thy gods Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Ægypt

12:28.note: Jeroboam sets up his calves with Aaron's very formula — 'Behold thy gods, Israel, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt' — the apostasy quoting the apostasy.

evidence.source: the glory of our Lord had filled the house of our Lord
evidence.target: the cloud covered the tabernacle of testimony, and the glory of our Lord filled it

8:11.note: Solomon's dedication replays the tabernacle's: the cloud, and the glory of the Lord filling the house, so the priests cannot stand. (In this corpus Exodus 40 runs to thirty-six verses; the filling of the tabernacle stands at 40:32.)

evidence.source: the fire of our Lord fell, and devoured the holocaust, and the wood, and the stones
evidence.target: a fire coming forth from our Lord, devoured the holocaust, and the fat that was upon the altar

18:38.note: Carmel replays the tabernacle's dedication: fire from the Lord falls and devours the holocaust, and all the people fall on their faces as Israel did at Aaron's first altar. Solomon's dedication repeats it again (2 Paralipomenon 7:1, entered separately).

evidence.source: they brought him forth without the city, and killed him with stones
evidence.target: Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let all that heard him put their hands upon his head, and let all the people stone him

21:13.note: Naboth is condemned on a manufactured blasphemy charge and executed in the blasphemy law's own form — brought forth outside and stoned by the multitude. Stephen's death follows the same shape without the law's warrant (Acts 7:58, set aside: no verbal anchor).

evidence.source: And he said: I saw all Israel dispersed in the mountains, as sheep not having a shepherd, and our Lord said: These have no master
evidence.target: and may go out and enter in before them, and bring them out, or bring them in: lest the people of our Lord be as sheep without a pastor

22:17.note: Micheas' vision over Ahab is Moses' fear for the congregation after him, in the same figure: Israel scattered as sheep not having a shepherd — and the Lord's answer there is that they have no master.

evidence.source: And there were horses brought for Salomon out of Ægypt, and Coa
evidence.target: he shall not multiply to himself horses, nor lead back the people into Ægypt

10:28.note: The king law's first fence — no multiplying horses, no turning back to Egypt for them — and Salomon's merchants do exactly this. The narrative keeps the law's own geography: the horses come out of Egypt.

evidence.source: And he had wives as it were queens seven hundred, and concubines three hundred: and the women turned away his heart.
evidence.target: He shall not have many wives, that may allure his mind, nor huge weights of silver & gold.

11:3.note: The king law's second fence, broken with its foretold consequence: many wives, and the heart turned away. The same verse's silver and gold are multiplied at 3 Kings 10.

evidence.source: which keepest covenant and mercy with thy servants, that walk before thee in all their heart.
evidence.target: keeping his covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to them that keep his precepts, unto a thousand generations:

8:23.note: Salomon opens the temple prayer with Deuteronomy's confession: the faithful God keeping covenant and mercy. The dedication stands on the law's own description of God.

evidence.source: Sadoc the priest took a horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Salomon
evidence.target: Samuel therefore took the horn of oil, & anointed him in the midst of his brethren

1:39.note: Salomon anointed with the horn of oil as David had been: the son's hurried anointing at Gihon repeats the father's at Bethlehem, horn and all.

evidence.source: Lord God of Abraham, and Isaac, and Israel, shew this day that thou art the God of Israel
evidence.target: I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.

18:36.note: Elias opens the Carmel prayer with the burning-bush name of God — Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, who is Jacob.

evidence.source: walked in the strength of that meat forty days, & forty nights, unto the mount of God, Horeb.
evidence.target: he was there with our Lord forty days & forty nights: he did not eat bread, and he drunk no water

19:8.note: Elias's forty days and nights to Horeb retrace Moyses' forty on the same mountain, fed once for the whole journey as Moyses was kept without bread and water.

evidence.source: mouth to mouth I speak to him: and plainly, and not by riddles and figures doth he see the Lord
evidence.target: spake unto Moyses face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend

12:8.note: God's defence of Moses against Miriam and Aaron rests on Exodus' word: with him he speaks 'mouth to mouth', as at Sinai he spoke 'face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend'.

evidence.source: The Lord is patient and full of mercy, taking away iniquity and wicked deeds
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

14:18.note: Moses, pleading after the spies, quotes God's own proclamation on Sinai back to him — patient, full of mercy, taking away iniquity; the quotation runs on into 34:7, to the visiting of the fathers' sins upon the children.

evidence.source: For Nadab and Abiu died, when they offered the strange fire in the sight of our Lord
evidence.target: offering before our Lord strange fire, which was not commanded them

3:4.note: The genealogy retells the book's own tragedy in a single clause: strange fire, which was not commanded. The same retelling at Numbers 26:61 is set aside as a duplicate.

evidence.source: let all the multitude stone him without the camp
evidence.target: Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let all that heard him put their hands upon his head, and let all the people stone him

15:35.note: The sentence on the sabbath wood-gatherer is pronounced in the blasphemy law's own form — brought forth without the camp and stoned by all the people — though his offence was the sabbath, not the Name.

evidence.source: a fire also coming forth from our Lord, slew the two hundred fifty men, that offered the incense
evidence.target: And fire coming forth from our Lord, devoured them, & they died before our Lord

16:35.note: Core's company repeats Nadab and Abihu's offence — incense offered without command — and meets their fire. Unauthorized incense is answered from the same presence in both books.

evidence.source: and I will take of thy spirit, and will deliver to them, that they may sustain with thee the burden of the people, and thou only be not burdened
evidence.target: & so it may be lighter for thee, the burden being imparted unto others

11:17.note: The seventy elders are Jethro's counsel come of age: the burden of the people imparted to others — now with Moses' own spirit delivered to them, which Exodus' judges did not have.

evidence.source: because you did offend me in the desert Sin in the contradiction of the multitude, neither would you sanctify me before them upon the waters
evidence.target: Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring in these peoples into the land, which I will give them

27:14.note: When Moses must provide his successor, the old sentence is recited once more — the book keeps its own record straight, word for word in the charge.

evidence.source: our Lord raised up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians: & he made proclamation in all his Kingdom
evidence.target: Who say to Cyrus: Thou art my pastor, and thou shalt accomplish all my will. Who say to Jerusalem: Thou shalt be built; and to the temple: Thou shalt be formed.

1:1.note: Esdras opens with Jeremiah's word accomplished, and behind Jeremiah stands Isaias naming Cyrus a century earlier: my pastor, who shall say Jerusalem be built and the temple be formed. The seed carries 1 Esdras 1:1 only at chapter level (Isaias 44).

evidence.source: Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians: All the Kingdoms of the earth hath the Lord the God of heaven given me, and he hath commanded me that I should build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Jewry.
evidence.target: Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians: All Kingdoms of the earth hath the Lord the God of heaven given me, and he hath commanded me that I should build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Jewry:

1:2.note: Esdras re-issues the decree with which Chronicles ends — the same royal document, quoted, so that the return begins where the exile's book closed. 'All the Kingdoms' / 'All Kingdoms' differs as printed.

evidence.source: he hath commanded me that I should build him a house in Jerusalem
evidence.target: Thus saith the Lord to my christ Cyrus, whose right hand I have taken

1:2.note: Cyrus's decree is the oracle performed: Isaias names him the Lord's christ, his right hand taken, two centuries ahead; Esdras records his own words charging him to build the house. The seed points 1 Esdras 1 at chapters 44 and 45; the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: They that came with Zorobabel, Josue, Nehemia, Saraia, Rahelaia, Mardochai, Belsan, Mesphar, Beguai, Rehum, Baana:
evidence.target: They that came with Zorobabel, Josue, Nehemias, Azarias, Rahamias, Nahamani, Mardochæus, Belsam, Mespharath, Begoai, Nahum, Baana.

2:2.note: The register of the return stands in both Esdras and Nehemias lists. The leaders' names after the first two differ in form as printed (Saraia/Azarias, Rahelaia/Rahamias and so on); the lists are parallel registers, not one copied cleanly from the other.

evidence.source: they made the solemnity of tabernacles, as it is written, and holocaust every day by order according to the precept
evidence.target: From the fifteenth day of this seventh month, shall be the festivity of tabernacles seven days to the Lord.

3:4.note: The returned exiles keep Tabernacles 'as it is written' — the writing is Leviticus's appointment of the feast from the fifteenth day of the seventh month.

evidence.source: there prophesied Aggæus the Prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo, prophesying to the Jews, that were in Jewry and Jerusalem
evidence.target: the word of our Lord was made in the hand of Aggeus the Prophet, to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, duke of Juda, and to Jesus the son of Josedec the grand Priest

5:1.note: Esdras names the two prophets whose preaching restarted the temple; Aggeus's own book opens with that word, addressed to the same Zorobabel and Jesus (Josue). Zacharias's opening belongs with his own verse, keyed next at 5:2.

evidence.source: Then rose up Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Josue the son of Josedec, and began to build the temple of God in Jerusalem
evidence.target: The hands of Zorobabel have founded this house, and his hands shall perfit it

5:2.note: Zorobabel rises and begins to build; Zacharias, the second prophet Esdras names, promises that the hands that founded the house shall finish it.

evidence.source: the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the Priest from the beginning:
evidence.target: But Eleazar the son of Aaron took a wife of the daughters of Phutiel: who bare him Phinees.

7:5.note: Esdras's pedigree is run back link by link to Aaron; its last links stand in Exodus itself — Eleazar son of Aaron, father of Phinees.

evidence.source: they have taken of their daughters to them and to their sons, and have mingled the holy seed with the people of the lands.
evidence.target: nor make marriages with them. Thy daughter thou shalt not give to his son, nor take his daughter for thy son:

9:2.note: Esdras's crisis is Deuteronomy's marriage ban broken: daughters taken for themselves and their sons, the holy seed mingled. Nehemias enforces the same law a generation later, keyed at 2 Esdras 13:25.

evidence.source: thou a propitious God, & gracious, and merciful, long suffering and of much compassion, didst not forsake them
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

9:17.note: The Levites' great prayer confesses Israel's rebellion in the words of the proclamation: a God 'propitious, gracious and merciful, long suffering and of much compassion', who did not forsake them.

evidence.source: thou a propitious God, & gracious, and merciful, long suffering and of much compassion, didst not forsake them.
evidence.target: Our Lord is pitiful, and merciful: long suffering, and very merciful.

9:17.note: Nehemias' great confession prays the mercy proclamation in the form Psalm 102 sings it. The fountainhead is Exodus 34:6, keyed in the Exodus stage; this entry records the psalm form Nehemias' wording follows.

evidence.source: and sinned in thy judgments, which a man should do, and shall live in them
evidence.target: which a man doing, shall live in them

9:29.note: Nehemiah's great confession takes up the life-promise of the statutes, in adapted words, as the very words Israel sinned against. Ezekiel 20:11 quotes the clause word for word (entered as quotation).

evidence.source: that the children of Israel should dwell in tabernacles, on the solemn day, the seventh month
evidence.target: shall dwell in bowers seven days

8:14.note: Nehemiah's generation finds the booths command 'written in the law' and keeps it as it had not been kept since the days of Josue — the feast of Leviticus 23:34-42 revived out of the book itself.

evidence.source: and they hired against them Balaam to curse them: and our God turned the cursing into blessing
