evidence.target: That thou shouldst curse mine enemies I called thee: and thou contrary wise blessest them

13:2.note: Read aloud from the law in the restored congregation (the text is Deuteronomy 23), the cursing turned to blessing is anchored here at the moment Balac heard it. The seed points this verse only at Numbers 22 by chapter.

evidence.source: and they hired against them Balaam to curse them: and our God turned the cursing into blessing.
evidence.target: & our Lord thy God would not hear Balaam, and he turned his cursing into thy blessing, for that he loved thee.

13:2.note: The returned exiles read the exclusion of Ammon and Moab aloud (13:1) and remember its ground in Deuteronomy's own words: God turned the cursing into blessing. The seed carries this verse only at chapter level (Deuteronomy 23); the precedent of our Numbers stage (the same verse, there refused verse-anchoring by the seed) is followed here. Our layer already keys Deuteronomy 23:5 back to Numbers 23:11.

evidence.source: and they possessed the land of Sehon, and the land of the king Hesebon, and the land of Og the king of Basan
evidence.target: Of whom he was strucken in the edge of the sword, and his land was possessed from Arnon unto Jeboc

9:22.note: Nehemias' great confession counts the firstfruits of the promise kept as these two kingdoms east of Jordan — Sehon's land and Og's, possessed in this chapter.

evidence.source: although you shall be led away to the uttermost parts of heaven, thence will I gather you, and bring you back into the place
evidence.target: If thou be dispersed as far as the poles of heaven, thence will our Lord thy God draw thee back.

1:9.note: Nehemias pleads Moses' promise back to God in Moses' own measure: scattered to heaven's uttermost, gathered thence. The prayer is Nehemiah 1 in modern editions; the corpus keeps it in 2 Esdras.

evidence.source: in the presence of the men, and women, & of those that understood: & the ears of all the people were attent to the book.
evidence.target: and the people being assembled together, as well men as women, children, & strangers, that are within thy gates: that hearing they may learn, and fear our Lord your God

8:3.note: Esdras' reading at the water gate is the assembly Deuteronomy ordained: the law read aloud (31:11) before men and women assembled, that hearing they may learn. Nehemiah 8 in modern editions.

evidence.source: Forty years didst thou feed them in the desert, and nothing was wanting to them, their garments waxed not old, & their feet were not worn.
evidence.target: Thy raiment, wherewith thou wast covered hath not decayed for age, and thy foot is not worn, lo this is the fortieth year.

9:21.note: The Levites' great prayer keeps Deuteronomy's two wonders in one verse: garments unworn and feet unworn through forty years. Deuteronomy speaks it twice — here in the humbling chapter, and at 29:5 — and 'nothing was wanting' is 2:7's word besides.

evidence.source: I beseech thee Lord God of heaven, strong, great, and terrible, which keepest covenant and mercy with them that love thee, and keep thy commandments:
evidence.target: I beseech thee o Lord God great and terrible, which keepest covenant, & mercy to them that love thee, and keep thy commandments.

1:5.note: Nehemias opens his prayer in Daniel's words — the great and terrible God keeping covenant and mercy — a generation after Daniel prayed them in Babylon. Both prayers themselves rest on Deuteronomy 7:9, keyed in our layer at Daniel 9:4.

evidence.source: Do you every one exact usuries of your brethren?
evidence.target: take not usuries of him, nor more than thou gavest:

5:7.note: Nehemias rebukes the nobles with the jubilee law's own word: usuries exacted of brethren, where Leviticus forbids taking usury of a brother.

evidence.source: thou didst divide the sea before them, and they passed through the midst of the sea in dry land: but their persecutors thou threwest into the depth, as a stone into the rough waters.
evidence.target: our Lord took it away, a vehement and burning wind blowing all the night, and turned it into dry ground: and the water was divided.

9:11.note: The Levites' prayer retells the sea crossing in Exodus's own elements: divided water, dry ground, the persecutors sunk like a stone — the stone is Exodus 15's song, the crossing Exodus 14's.

evidence.source: To mount Sinai also thou didst descend, and spakest with them from heaven, and thou gavest them right judgments, and the law of truth
evidence.target: our Lord descended upon the mount Sinai in the very top of the mount

9:13.note: The prayer's Sinai line against Exodus's own: the Lord descended on the mount, and there spoke and gave the law.

evidence.source: Bread also from heaven thou gavest them in their hunger
evidence.target: Behold I will rain you bread from heaven

9:15.note: The prayer keeps Exodus's very phrase for the manna: bread from heaven, given in hunger.

evidence.source: they killed thy Prophets, which admonished them earnestly to return to thee
evidence.target: thy Prophets they have slain with the sword, and I alone am left

9:26.note: The Levites confess in Elias's complaint: the prophets killed by the people they were sent to recall. Our layer keys Romans 11:3 and 1 Machabees 2 to the same complaint; Nehemias's use of it was unkeyed.

evidence.source: thou art just in all things, that have come upon us: because thou hast done truth, but we have done wickedly.
evidence.target: Lord God of Israel thou art just: because we are left, which should be saved as at this day. Behold we are before thee in our sin

9:33.note: Nehemias's Levites pray Esdras's confession over again: thou art just, we are before thee in our sin. The two great penitential prayers of the return answer each other.

evidence.source: there was found written in it, that the Ammonites and the Moabites should not enter into the Church of God for ever:
evidence.target: The Ammonite and the Moabite yea after the tenth generation shall not enter into the church of our Lord, for ever:

13:1.note: The public reading finds Deuteronomy's exclusion written and acts on it the same day. Our layer keys 13:2 to the blessing-into-cursing ground at 23:5; the exclusion itself stands at 23:3.

evidence.source: adjured them by God, that they should not give their daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for their sons, and for themselves, saying:
evidence.target: Thy daughter thou shalt not give to his son, nor take his daughter for thy son:

13:25.note: Nehemias binds the people by oath in the law's exact terms — give not your daughters, take not theirs — the same ban Esdras had wept over at 1 Esdras 9:2.

evidence.source: because he is benign & merciful, patient and of much mercy
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

2:13.note: Joel summons Israel to return on the strength of the proclamation: 'he is benign and merciful, patient and of much mercy'.

evidence.source: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons, and your daughters shall prophesy
evidence.target: O that all the people might prophesy, and that our Lord would give them his spirit!

2:28.note: What Moses wished over Eldad and Medad — all the people prophesying, the Lord giving them his spirit — Joel promises outright: the spirit poured on all flesh. Peter preaches Joel's form at Pentecost; the wish underneath it is this verse.

evidence.source: Cut your ploughs into swords, and your spades into spears
evidence.target: they shall turn their swords into coulters, and their spears into sithes

3:10.note: Joel summons the nations to war in the exact inverse of Isaias' (and Micheas') peace oracle — the reversal only works because the original wording is in the hearer's ear.

evidence.source: I will render you the years, which the locust, the bruke, and the blast, and the eruke hath eaten: my great strength which I have sent upon you
evidence.target: the grass of the earth was devoured, and what fruits soever on the trees, which the hail had left: there was also nothing at all left that was green

2:25.note: Joel's locust host, sent by God and devouring the land bare, is the Exodus plague returned upon Israel herself; Joel promises the eaten years rendered back. Same plague-shape, graded parallel.

evidence.source: I know that thou art a clement, and merciful God, patient, and of much compassion, and forgiving upon the evil
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

4:2.note: Jonas quotes the proclamation back at God as a complaint — 'I know that thou art a clement and merciful God, patient and of much compassion' — the formula almost word for word, turned into a grievance that Nineveh was spared.

evidence.source: out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou hast heard my voice.
evidence.target: he hath heard my voice from his holy temple: and my cry in his sight, hath entered into his ears.

2:3.note: Jonas' prayer from the fish is woven from the psalms; here the heard-cry and the temple meet. The seed keys Jonas 2:3 to Psalms 119 and 129 at chapter level.

evidence.source: all thy surges, and thy waves have passed over me.
evidence.target: All thy high things, and thy ways have passed over me.

2:4.note: Jonas' waves are the psalm's waters passing over the soul. This corpus prints the psalm's word as ways where the sense is waves; the shared clause have passed over me is what is printed in both.

evidence.source: I am cast away from the sight of thine eyes: but yet I shall see thy holy temple again.
evidence.target: I am cast away from the sight of thine eyes.

2:5.note: Jonas quotes the psalm's cast-away word and answers it with his own yet I shall see thy temple.

evidence.source: The waters have compassed me even to the soul:
evidence.target: Save me, o God: because waters are entered into my soul.

2:6.note: The waters-to-the-soul of the great passion psalm, prayed again inside the fish.

evidence.source: I in the voice of praise will immolate to thee: what things soever I have vowed I will render
evidence.target: Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise, and pay thy vows to the Highest.

2:10.note: Jonas' vow from the fish is Psalm 49's sacrifice of praise and paying of vows, performed.

evidence.source: he desired for his soul to die, and said: It is better for me to die than to live
evidence.target: he desired for his soul to die, and said: It sufficeth me Lord, take my soul

4:8.note: Jonas under the ivy repeats Elias under the juniper in the same words — 'he desired for his soul to die' stands in both verses; the prophet angry at mercy sits where the prophet weary of flight sat.

evidence.source: Our Lord is patient, and great of strength, and cleansing, he will not make innocent
evidence.target: no man of himself is innocent before thee

1:3.note: Nahum takes the proclamation's severe edge: the Lord is patient, but 'cleansing, he will not make innocent' — Exodus: 'no man of himself is innocent before thee'.

evidence.source: God is jealous, & our Lord revenging
evidence.target: The Lord his name is Jealous, God is an emulator

1:2.note: Nahum's God 'is jealous' — Exodus gives the jealousy a name: 'The Lord, his name is Jealous'.

evidence.source: Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that Evangelizeth, and preacheth peace
evidence.target: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that evangelizeth & preacheth peace

1:15.note: Nahum takes up Isaias' beautiful-feet herald against Nineveh's fall. The seed carries Nahum 1:15 -> Isaias 52 at chapter level only; Romans 10:15 quotes Isaias' form.

evidence.source: the children of Israel could not behold the face of Moyses for the glory of his countenance
evidence.target: seeing the face of Moyses horned, they were afraid to come near

3:7.note: Paul: the children of Israel 'could not behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance'; Exodus: seeing Moses' face — the DR prints 'horned', for the Vulgate's word — 'they were afraid to come near'.

evidence.source: when he shall be converted to our Lord, the veil shall be taken away
evidence.target: Which going in to our Lord, and speaking with him, he took away until he went forth

3:16.note: Paul reads Moses' own act spiritually: as Moses, going in before the Lord, took away the veil (named at 34:33 and 34:35) until he came forth, so 'when he shall be converted to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away'.

evidence.source: That I will dwell, and walk in them, and will be their God; and they shall be my people
evidence.target: I will walk among you, & will be your God, & you shall be my people

6:16.note: Paul's temple catena quotes the covenant promise of Leviticus 26:11-12. The seed carries this verse of Paul at 26:11 (the tabernacle clause); the walking-and-people clause stands at 26:12.

evidence.source: I will dwell, and walk in them, and will be their God; and they shall be my people
evidence.target: my tabernacle shall be in them: & I will be their God, and they shall be my people

6:16.note: Paul's temple-of-the-living-God promise is composite: its dwelling formula stands in Leviticus 26:11–12 (entered in our layer to this same verse of Ezechiel) and its tabernacle form is Ezechiel's — my tabernacle in them, I their God, they my people. Both anchors are recorded; this entry claims the tabernacle wording.

evidence.source: Bear not the yoke with infidels.
evidence.target: Thou shalt not plough with an oxe and ass together.

6:14.note: Paul's unequal yoke is the law's plough-team: an ox and an ass under one yoke, kinds that cannot pull together. The image is Deuteronomy's; the application — fellowship with unbelief — is the apostle's.

evidence.source: he that soweth sparingly, sparingly also shall reap: and he that soweth in blessings, of blessings also shall reap.
evidence.target: Some divide their own goods, and are made richer: others take violently not their own, and are always in poverty.

9:6.note: Graded parallel: Paul's sowing economy is the proverb's scattering economy — dividing one's goods and growing richer — with no shared wording beyond the shape of the law itself.

evidence.source: we must all be manifested before the judgement seat of Christ, that every one may receive the proper things of the body, according as he hath done, either good or evil.
evidence.target: all things that are done, God will bring into judgement for every error, whether it be good or evil.

5:10.note: Paul's judgment seat is the Preacher's closing sentence with its seat named: God will bring all things done into judgement, whether good or evil — every one receiving according as he hath done, either good or evil.

evidence.source: written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God: not in tables of stone, but in the tables carnal of the heart
evidence.target: in their heart I will write it

3:3.note: Paul's living epistle, written on heart-tables, is the new covenant's inscription: my law in their bowels, in their heart I will write it. The stone-tables contrast is Exodus's half of Paul's sentence; the heart-writing is Jeremias's, and only that is claimed here. The Ezechiel 36:26 anchor of the same verse is entered separately.

evidence.source: not in tables of stone, but in the tables carnal of the heart
evidence.target: will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a fleshy heart

3:3.note: Stone against flesh: Paul's not-in-stone-but-heart tables take up Ezechiel's surgery, the stony heart taken away and a fleshy heart given. The Jeremias 31:33 anchor of the same verse (the heart-writing) is entered separately.

evidence.source: that no man should consecrate his son or daughter by fire to Moloch
evidence.target: Of thy seed thou shalt not give to be consecrated to the idol Moloch

23:10.note: Josiah defiles Topheth to end the rite Leviticus 18:21 forbids — seed consecrated to Moloch, passed through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom.

evidence.source: We therefore boiled my son, and did eat him
evidence.target: so that you shall eat the flesh of your sons & of your daughters

6:29.note: In the Samaria siege the covenant curse stops being a threat: two mothers boil and eat a son, and the king of Israel hears the case in the famine Leviticus 26:29 foretold. Ezekiel re-pronounces the same curse (entered as allusion).

evidence.source: But the money for offence, & the money for sins, they brought not into the temple of our Lord, because it was the Priests'
evidence.target: the law of both hosts shall be one: to the Priest that offereth it, it shall pertain

12:16.note: Joas's temple repairs respect the old rule: the money for offence and for sins is not treasury income, because Leviticus assigns both hosts — and their price — to the priest who offers them.

evidence.source: And he made his son pass through fire: and he used soothsaying, and observed divinations, and made pythons, and multiplied enchanters
evidence.target: Neither let there be found in thee any that shall expiate his son, or daughter, making them to pass through the fire: or that demandeth of soothsayers, and observeth dreams and divinations

21:6.note: Manasses' reign is Deuteronomy's banned list enacted item by item — the son through the fire, soothsaying, divinations, pythons. Chronicles' retelling of the same reign (2 Paralipomenon 33:6) is set aside as this entry's duplicate.

evidence.source: The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers: but every one shall die in his own sin.
evidence.target: The fathers shall not be slain for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every one shall die for his own sin,

14:6.note: Amasias spares his father's murderers' children 'according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moyses' — and the history quotes the law nearly entire. The seed points this verse at Deuteronomy 21 by chapter; the words quoted stand at 24:16.

evidence.source: Elias took his mantle, and folded it together, and smote the waters, which were divided into two parts, and they both passed over by the dry land.
evidence.target: stood girded upon the dry ground in the midst of Jordan, and all the people passed over through the dry channel.

2:8.note: Jordan opens a second time: Elias and Eliseus cross on dry ground where Israel crossed behind the ark. The river, the dry passage, and the two parts are the link; the instruments differ, mantle for ark.

evidence.source: Elias ascended by a hurl wind into heaven.
evidence.target: he walked with God, and was seen no more: because God took him.

2:11.note: Only two men leave the earth without the text recording a death: Henoch, whom God took, and Elias, taken up by the whirlwind. Graded parallel — the shape is shared, the wording is not.

evidence.source: brake the brazen serpent, which Moyses had made: for until that time the children of Israel burnt incense to it
evidence.target: Moyses therefore made A brazen Serpent, and set it for a sign

18:4.note: Ezechias destroys the very sign Moyses made, because the sign had become an idol — the verse names its maker, and Numbers is the making.

evidence.source: Make a Phase to our Lord your God, according as it is written in the Book of this covenant.
evidence.target: that thou mayest make the Phase to our Lord thy God: because in this month our Lord thy God brought thee out of Ægypt by night.

23:21.note: Josias commands the Passover 'as written' — and what is written is Deuteronomy's command to make the Phase to the Lord thy God. Centralised at Jerusalem, as Deuteronomy requires and Samuel-era practice had not been.

evidence.source: It is the sepulchre of the man of God, which came from Juda, and foretold these things which thou hast done upon the altar of Bethel.
evidence.target: a child shall be born to the house of David, named Josias, and he shall immolate upon thee priests of the excelses

23:17.note: At Bethel Josias asks after the tomb of the man who, three centuries earlier, had named Josias himself against that altar. The history itself closes the prophecy's loop.

evidence.source: I have anointed thee king over the people of the Lord of Israel
evidence.target: Jehu the son of Namsi thou shalt anoint king over Israel

9:6.note: The young prophet at Ramoth Galaad does what Elias was charged to do on Horeb: Jehu is anointed king over Israel, a generation after the charge was given.

evidence.source: My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the guarder thereof.
evidence.target: My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the guider thereof.

13:14.note: Joas weeps over the dying Eliseus in Eliseus's own words over the ascending Elias — the cry is quoted, with only the last noun's spelling differing as printed (guarder/guider).

evidence.source: with the mantle of Elias, that fell down to him, he smote the waters, and they were not divided.
evidence.target: when Elias came to him, he cast his mantle upon him.

2:14.note: The mantle that fell at the ascension is the mantle cast on Eliseus at the plough: the call and the succession are one garment, and Eliseus proves it at the same river.

evidence.source: For we are pilgrims before thee, and strangers, as all our fathers
evidence.target: you are my strangers & sojourners

29:15.note: David's prayer over the temple treasury takes its self-understanding from the land law: because the land is God's, even Israel's king is his stranger and sojourner, and nothing dedicated is truly his own.

evidence.source: Deal manfully, and take courage, and do it: fear not, and be not dismayed: for our Lord my God will be with thee, and will not leave thee, nor forsake thee
evidence.target: himself will be with thee: he will not leave, nor forsake thee: fear not, neither dread thou.

28:20.note: David hands the charge down a second time: as Moses charged Josue, so David charges Salomon, with the same promise in the same words — the charge of 31:6–7 and the promise of 31:8 in one breath.

evidence.source: Achar, who troubled Israel, and sinned in the theft of the anathema.
evidence.target: Because thou hast disturbed us, our Lord disturb thee in this day. And all Israel stoned him

2:7.note: Chronicles' genealogy remembers Achar (Josue's Achan) by his deed: he troubled Israel in the anathema's theft. Josue's sentence answers word for word — thou hast disturbed us — and ends in the stoning the genealogy presupposes.

evidence.source: Saul therefore caught his sword, and fell upon it.
evidence.target: Saul therefore caught his sword, and fell upon it.

10:4.note: Chronicles retells Saul's death in Samuel's words, the closing clause verbatim: refused by his armourbearer, Saul caught his sword and fell upon it. The same event told twice; Chronicles adds its own verdict at 10:13-14, which is its commentary, not a second entry.

evidence.source: But Satan rose against Israel: and moved David to number Israel.
evidence.target: stirred up David among them saying: Go, number Israel and Juda.

21:1.note: Chronicles retells the census in Samuel's shape — David moved to number Israel — but the two books name the mover differently, and the difference is stated, not harmonized: Samuel opens with the fury of the Lord stirring David up; Chronicles says Satan rose against Israel and moved him. The same event, told twice, with its tension on the page.

evidence.source: they anointed him king over Israel, according to the word of our Lord, which he spake in the hand of Samuel.
evidence.target: they anointed David to be king over Israel.

11:3.note: David made king over all Israel at Hebron, in both histories; Chronicles adds that it was according to the word spoken by Samuel.

evidence.source: Our Lord therefore was angry against Oza, & struck him, for that he had touched the Ark: and he died there before our Lord.
evidence.target: our Lord was wrath with indignation against Oza, and struck him for the rashness: who died there before the ark of God.

13:10.note: Oza struck at the ark's first bringing up, in Samuel and in Chronicles.

evidence.source: I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to me for a son
evidence.target: I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to me for a son

17:13.note: Nathan's oracle in both histories, word for word at its centre: the son of David held in a father-son covenant.

evidence.source: David struck the Philisthiims, and humbled them
evidence.target: David struck the Philisthiims, and humbled them

18:1.note: The wars of David open in both histories with the same sentence; what David took differs in the verses' second halves (Geth in Chronicles, the bridle of tribute in Samuel), and is left as printed.

evidence.source: at such time when kings are wont to go forth to battle, Joab gathered together the army
evidence.target: at such time when kings are wont to proceed to battles, David sent Joab

20:1.note: The Rabba campaign opens with the same season formula; Chronicles passes over the Bathsabee matter that fills Samuel's chapter. The seed carries the pair only at chapter level (2 Kings 11).

evidence.source: Thou hast shed much blood, and fought very many battles, thou canst not build a house to my name
evidence.target: Shalt thou build me a house to dwell in?

22:8.note: Chronicles gives the reason Samuel's oracle leaves unstated: the man of blood may not build. Samuel records the refusal; Chronicles records its ground.

evidence.source: Joab the son of Sarvia began to number, and finished not: because upon this there fell wrath upon Israel
evidence.target: Our Lord therefore sent the pestilence in Israel: and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men.

27:24.note: Within Chronicles itself: the registrar's note that the census number was never registered points back to the plague chapter it came from.

evidence.source: know the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart
evidence.target: keep his ceremonies, and his precepts & judgments, and testimonies as is written in the law of Moyses

28:9.note: David's charge to Salomon stands in two forms: Chronicles' assembly charge (know God, serve him, seek and find) and Kings' deathbed charge (walk in his ways, keep the law of Moyses). Graded parallel — same charge, different words preserved.

evidence.source: the sons of Phares, Hesron and Hamul.
evidence.target: Phares begat Esron

2:5.note: Juda's line in the genealogies meets Ruth's closing genealogy at Phares and Hesron (Esron), the line that runs to David.

evidence.source: The children of Amram: Aaron, Moyses, and Maria.
evidence.target: who bare him Aaron & Moyses.

6:3.note: The priestly genealogy's head in Chronicles against its source in Exodus: Amram's children are Aaron, Moyses and Maria.

evidence.source: Chant to him, and sing to him: & tell ye all his marvelous things.
evidence.target: Chant to him, and sing to him: tell ye all his marvelous works.

16:9.note: David's thanksgiving psalm at the ark is a cento of psalms; this line is Psalm 104's, with only its last word differing as printed (things/works). The seed carries the psalm only at chapter level for 16:8.

evidence.source: Remember for ever his covenant: the word, which he commanded unto a thousand generations.
evidence.target: He hath been mindful for ever of his testament; of the word which he commanded unto a thousand generations.

16:15.note: The cento again: the covenant remembered to a thousand generations, in David's singing of it and in the psalm it is taken from.

evidence.source: For all the gods of the peoples, be idols: but our Lord made the heavens.
evidence.target: Because all the gods of the Gentiles are devils, but our Lord made the heavens.

16:26.note: The cento's line from Psalm 95, graded allusion, not quotation: the second half is word for word, but the gods are 'idols' in Chronicles and 'devils' in the psalm, as printed. The seed keys Psalm 95:1 to 16:23; this verse was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Save us o God our Saviour: and gather us together, and deliver us out of the nations, that we may confess to thy holy name
evidence.target: Save us, o Lord our God: and gather us out of the Nations. That we may confess to thy holy name

16:35.note: The cento closes with Psalm 105's closing prayer: save us, gather us out of the nations, that we may confess thy holy name.

evidence.source: Touch not my anointed: and unto my Prophets be not malicious.
evidence.target: Touch not my anointed, and toward my Prophets be not malignant.

16:22.note: The Touch not my anointed of the Chronicles psalm is this verse of Psalm 104.

evidence.source: Tell his glory among the gentiles: among all peoples his marvelous works.
evidence.target: Shew forth his glory among the Gentiles, his marvelous works in all peoples.

16:24.note: The second half of David's psalm follows Psalm 95; the seed carries only 16:23 to 95:1 from this stretch.

evidence.source: our Lord is great, and laudable exceedingly: and terrible over all gods.
evidence.target: our Lord is great, and exceeding laudable: he is terrible above all gods.

16:25.note: Great and terrible above all gods, in both copies.

evidence.source: adore our Lord in holy honour.
evidence.target: adore ye our Lord in his holy court.

16:29.note: The adore-in-holiness of the Chronicles psalm is Psalm 95's adore in his holy court.

evidence.source: Let all the earth be moved before his face: for he founded the world unmovable.
evidence.target: he hath corrected the round world, which shall not be moved:

16:30.note: Earth moved before his face, and the world unmovable, in both copies.

evidence.source: he is come to judge the earth.
evidence.target: he cometh to judge the earth. He will judge the round world in equity,

16:33.note: The trees of the forest in the Chronicles verse answer to Psalm 95:12; the judge-of-the-earth clause is this verse's.

evidence.source: Confess ye to our Lord, because he is good: because his mercy is for ever.
evidence.target: Confess ye to our Lord because he is good: because his mercy is for ever.

16:34.note: The great refrain that opens Psalm 105 (and 106, and 117); the seed keys 16:34 to Psalm 105 at chapter level and to 106:1 at verse level.

evidence.source: Blessed be our Lord the God of Israel from eternity unto eternity: and let all the people say: Amen,
evidence.target: Blessed be our Lord the God of Israel from everlasting unto everlasting: and all the people shall say: Be it, be it.

16:36.note: The doxology that ends the psalter's fourth book ends David's psalm in the Chronicles too.

evidence.source: shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumbs of his right hand and foot
evidence.target: he had touched the tip of the right ear of every one, and the thumbs of the right hand and foot

14:14.note: Within the book itself: the cleansed leper is restored with the consecration rite of Aaron's sons — the host's blood on the right ear, the right thumb, the right foot — as one re-ordained into the camp.

evidence.source: and with the error of Balaam, have for reward poured out themselves
evidence.target: having the price of divination in their hands

1:11.note: Jude's 'for reward' is this price: the hire of cursing, carried in the messengers' hands, is the error's whole motive.

evidence.source: and have perished in the contradiction of Core
evidence.target: and opening her mouth, devoured them with their tabernacles & all their substance

1:11.note: The perishing Jude names is this: the earth opening her mouth on Core's company in their contradiction of Moses and Aaron.

evidence.source: When Michael the Archangel, disputing with the devil, made altercation for the body of Moyses
evidence.target: Michael one of the chief princes came to aid me

1:9.note: Michael the archangel in contention with the devil answers Daniel's Michael, the chief prince whose warfare is contention with the unseen princes. Stated openly: the dispute over Moyses' body itself stands nowhere in Daniel — this entry claims only Michael's office and contention, which are Daniel's gift to the later books.

evidence.source: because thou shalt conceive & bear a son, whose head the razor shall not touch: for he shall be a Nazarite of God, from his infancy, and from his mother's womb
evidence.target: All the time of his separation a razor shall not pass over his head, until the day be expired, that he is consecrated to the Lord

13:5.note: Samson is the law's lifelong Nazarite: the angel lays this chapter's razor rule on him from the womb, and his mother's abstinence (13:4) extends the consecration backward before his birth.

evidence.source: There never came iron upon my head, because I am a Nazarite, that is to say, consecrated to God from my mother's womb: if my head shall be shaven, my strength shall depart from me
evidence.target: a razor shall not pass over his head

16:17.note: Samson's confession to Delila is the vow's own term spoken at its breaking point — no razor on the consecrated head; shorn, he is as other men.

evidence.source: And Haber the Cineite was in time past departed from the rest of the Cineites his brethren of Hobab, the cousin of Moyses
evidence.target: And Moyses said to Hobab the son of Raguel the Madianite, his allied: We march toward the place, which our Lord will give us: come with us, that we may do thee good

4:11.note: The Cineans dwelling in Israel — Haber among them, in the days of the Judges — are there because Hobab took this invitation and did not return to his own country.

evidence.source: Israel therefore sent messengers to Sehon the king of the Amorrheites, who dwelt in Hesebon, & they said to him: Suffer me to pass through thy land unto the river
evidence.target: And Israel sent messengers to Sehon King of the Amorrheites, saying

11:19.note: Jephte's embassy to Ammon argues Israel's title from this embassy — the same messengers, the same request for passage, the same refusal that ended at Jasa.

evidence.source: Lord when thou wentest out of Seir, and didst pass by the countries of Edom, the earth was moved
evidence.target: Our Lord came from Sinai, and from Seir is he risen to us: he hath appeared from mount Pharan, and with him thousands of Saints.

5:4.note: Debora's song sings the same march Moses blessed: the Lord rising from Seir, the earth moved at his going forth. The theophany tradition begins in both songs.

evidence.source: And when Othoniel the son of Cenez, the younger brother of Caleb had taken it, he gave him Axa his daughter to wife.
evidence.target: And Othoniel the son of Cenez, the younger brother of Caleb took it: & he gave him Axa his daughter to wife.

1:13.note: Within this group: Judges retells Caleb's offer and Othoniel's taking of Cariath Sepher in Josue's own words, nearly verbatim. The same event told twice, once in each book — the seam where Judges takes up Josue's narrative.

evidence.source: And you drank wine to the Nazareites: and the Prophets you commanded, saying: prophesy not
evidence.target: they shall abstain from wine, & every thing that can make one drunk

2:12.note: The sin Amos charges on Israel is forcing the consecrated to break the first rule of their consecration — wine, which the Nazarite shall not touch.

evidence.source: Him that maketh Arcturus, and Orion
evidence.target: He that maketh Arcturus, and Orion, and Hyades

5:8.note: Amos names the Maker in Job's own catalogue words: maketh Arcturus and Orion. The seed carries nothing between Amos and Job.

evidence.source: Our Lord will roar out of Sion, and out of Jerusalem he will give his voice
evidence.target: our Lord will roar out of Sion, and out of Jerusalem he will give his voice: and the heavens, and the earth shall be moved

1:2.note: Amos opens with Joel's roar sentence nearly word for word — the twelve quoting each other, as the group note expected.

evidence.source: the mountains shall drop sweetness, and all hills shall be tilled
evidence.target: the mountains shall distill sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk

9:13.note: Amos' plenty and Joel's plenty share the dropping-sweetness mountains. The seed carries this only at chapter level (Joel 3:18 -> Amos 9).

evidence.source: God will come from the South, and the holy one from mount Pharan: His glory shall cover the heavens
evidence.target: he hath appeared from mount Pharan, and with him thousands of Saints. In his right hand a fiery law.

3:3.note: Habacuc's prayer sees the coming from the same mountain Moses named: Pharan, and the glory covering the heavens.

evidence.source: The sun and the moon stood in their habitation,
evidence.target: And the Sun & Moon stood still, till the people revenged themselves of their enemies.

3:11.note: Habacuc's prayer re-sees the Gabaon theophany: sun and moon standing in their habitation answers Josue's sun against Gabaon and moon against Aialon, both standing still. Graded allusion: the prophet is singing a new theophany in the old one's words, not citing the history.

evidence.source: he will make my feet as of the harts': and upon my high places he
evidence.target: That perfited my feet as it were of harts: and setting me upon high things.

3:19.note: Habacuc's canticle closes with David's song: feet as the harts', and the high places.

evidence.source: the earth shall be replenished, that they may know the glory of our Lord, as waters covering the sea
evidence.target: the earth is replenished with the knowledge of our Lord, as the covering waters of the sea

2:14.note: Habacuc's earth-filled promise reworks Isaias' holy-mountain word, glory known where Isaias has knowledge.

evidence.source: Against a priest receive not accusation, but under two or three witnesses.
evidence.target: but in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word stand.

5:19.note: Paul applies the law of witnesses to the church's own elders: no accusation received but under two or three witnesses. The seed carries the same law for Matthew 18:16, 2 Corinthians 13:1, John 8:17 and Hebrews 10:28; Timothy's church-order use was unkeyed.

evidence.source: For the root of all evils is covetousness
evidence.target: A covetous man shall not be filled with money: and he that loveth riches, shall take no fruit of them

6:10.note: Paul's root answers the Preacher's fruitlessness: the covetous man shall not be filled with money, and he that loveth riches shall take no fruit of them — of that loveless root, all evils.

evidence.source: The hands of pitiful women have sodden their own children: they were made their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
evidence.target: and thou shalt eat the fruit of thy womb, and the flesh of thy sons & of thy daughters, which our Lord thy God shall give thee, in the distress and vastation wherewith thine enemy shall oppress thee.

4:10.note: The siege-curse of Deuteronomy, fulfilled in Jerusalem's own streets and wept over: pitiful women's hands soddening their own children. Baruch's confession of the same curse is keyed to this verse in our layer.

evidence.source: He shall give the cheek to him that striketh him
evidence.target: I have given my body to the strikers, & my cheeks to the pluckers

3:30.note: Lamentations' counsel to the suffering man is Isaias's Servant turned into a rule of patience: give the cheek to him that strikes, as the Servant gave his cheeks to the pluckers.

evidence.source: For the children of Israel had sworn to them, and Saul would strike them of zeal, as it were for the children of Israel & Juda.
evidence.target: We have sworn to them in the name of our Lord the God of Israel, and therefore we may not touch them.

21:2.note: David learns the famine is for Saul's striking the Gabaonites, to whom Israel had sworn. The oath Saul broke is the one Josue's princes state here: sworn in the Lord's name, therefore untouchable. The seed carries this verse of 2 Kings only at chapter level (Josue 9); the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: What is man that thou magnifiest him? Or why settest thou thy heart toward him?
evidence.target: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? Or the son of man, that thou visitest him?

7:17.note: Job asks the psalm's wonder-question in affliction's key: what is man, that God should regard him. Entered as a verbal echo between the two books, without asserting which text was written first.

evidence.source: By a dream in a vision by night, when heavy sleep falleth upon men
evidence.target: in vision will I appear to him, or in sleep I will speak to him.

33:15.note: Elihu's doctrine of God's night-speaking — by a dream in a vision, when heavy sleep falls — rests on the Lord's own word to Aaron and Mary: in vision he appears, in sleep he speaks.

evidence.source: Behold the fear of our Lord, that is wisdom: and to depart from evil, understanding.
evidence.target: The fear of our Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

28:28.note: The wisdom hymn ends where Proverbs begins: the fear of the Lord is wisdom itself. Job's form — that is wisdom — and Solomon's — the beginning of wisdom — state the one sentence from its two ends.

evidence.source: Did not he make me in the womb that made him also
evidence.target: The rich and poor have met one another: our Lord is the maker of both.

31:15.note: Job pleads his servants' cause from the proverb's ground before Solomon states it: one Maker made master and servant in the womb, as rich and poor have one Maker of both.

evidence.source: If we confess our sins, he is faithful & just, for to forgive us our sins
evidence.target: he that shall confess, and shall forsake them, shall obtain mercy.

1:9.note: The proverb's promise — he that confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy — is the ground of John's: if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive.

evidence.source: He that shall have the substance of the world, and shall see his brother have need, and shall shut his bowels from him
evidence.target: He that stoppeth his ear at the cry of the poor, himself also shall cry and shall not be heard.

3:17.note: The proverb's stopped ear against the poor man's cry becomes John's shut bowels against the brother in need; both ask how a man so closed can stand before God.

evidence.source: Whatsoever you do, work it from the heart as to our Lord, and not to men
evidence.target: Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, work it instantly

3:23.note: Paul's household rule is the Preacher's urgency with its reason changed: whatsoever thy hand is able to do, work it — instantly, says Ecclesiastes, for there is no work in hell; from the heart as to the Lord, says the apostle.

evidence.source: The Mandragoræs have given a smell.
evidence.target: found mandragoras: which he brought to his mother Lia

7:13.note: The bride's mandrakes at the gates are Rachel's mandrakes of the wheat harvest, the love-fruit Ruben found in the field and Lia's son brought home. The corpus spells the word Mandragoræs in the Canticle and mandragoras in Genesis; the plant and its errand are the same.

evidence.source: in the name of Jesus every knee bow of the celestials, terrestrials, and infernals:
evidence.target: every knee shall be bowed to me, and every tongue shall swear

2:10.note: Every knee bowing, transferred to the name of Jesus. The seed keys Romans 14:11 to this verse and this verse of Philippians to 45:14; the hymn's own anchor is 45:23.

evidence.source: he sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself as though he were God
evidence.target: shall be elevated, & magnified against every god: and against the God of gods he shall speak magnifical things

2:4.note: The man of sin extolled above all called God, shewing himself as God, is Daniel's king magnified against every god, speaking magnifical things against the God of gods. The temple-sitting detail is Paul's; the self-magnifying against God is Daniel's, and only that is claimed.

evidence.source: If the grape gatherers had entered in to thee, would they not have left thee at the least a cluster?
evidence.target: If the grape gatherers had come upon thee, they had not left a cluster

1:5.note: Abdias' Edom oracle and Jeremias' Edom oracle (ch. 49) share whole sentences; the seed carries Abdias 1:1 -> Jeremias 49 at chapter level only. Verse anchors are filled in this and the next two entries.

evidence.source: How have they searched Esau, have they sought out his hidden things?
evidence.target: I have discovered Esau, I have revealed his secrets, and he cannot be concealed

1:6.note: The searching of Esau, common to both Edom oracles.

evidence.source: destroy the wise out of Idumea, and prudence from the mount of Esau
evidence.target: Why is wisdom no more in Theman? Counsel is perished from the children

1:8.note: The wisdom of Edom destroyed — Jeremias asks why wisdom is no more in Theman, Abdias answers with its destruction.
